The board closed the public hearing but could not adopt the resolution because two sheds and a barn built under earlier building permits never received Planning Board/ARB sign-off (a town-side glitch); it opted to send the applicant to the ARB and adopt at a later meeting without requiring the applicant to reappear.

The board had previously closed the public hearing and instructed the applicant to obtain ARB approval before returning for adoption. With ARB approval now in hand, the board adopted the draft resolution without the applicant needing to appear.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court (two-family residences)
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shari, Hudson Engineering & Consulting
cases.lastStatus: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)

trajectory.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)

timeline.summary: Two proposed two-family dwellings on the first two lots of a recently approved three-lot subdivision. Much of the driveway, utilities and stormwater remain unchanged from the subdivision plans; updates add the buildings and elevated decks (at-grade rear terraces to be removed). Outstanding items include structural plans and protective barriers for tall retaining walls, a driveway revision to add a required parking space per unit, and a possible gross land coverage variance the applicant expects to avoid by converting a turnaround area to parking. Chairman Carthy strongly pressed for tiered, more attractive retaining walls (some near 10-11 ft) rather than a single tall wall. No hearing yet; revised plans to follow.

The applicant presented revised site/steep-slope plans for two two-family residences, addressing prior comments by adding a terraced retaining wall to soften the driveway wall's appearance, providing two dedicated parking spaces per unit, reworking side/rear grading, and clarifying overland footing-drain discharge. Outstanding engineering memo items (landscape plan revisions, planting detail, drain pipe sizes/inverts, peak flows) were deemed handleable administratively. The board approved the resolution for 4 Massaro Court that night; since the buildings are identical, 2 Massaro Court would be approved administratively at a future meeting once the applicant obtains ARB approval, without needing to return. The board flagged that any rock encountered on the up-hill site would require checking back.

timeline.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)
timeline.summary: This is the last of a previously approved three-lot, two-family subdivision, with the first two lots already built. The town engineer raised concerns about the proposed house footprint's proximity and view-shed impact on the adjacent home, plus an exposed-foundation/grade drop-off at the rear northwest corner. The applicant's engineer agreed to regrade that corner (up to about 372) and consider shifting the house, while noting retaining walls are less substantial than the prior lots and structural wall designs are under town review. The board was generally comfortable and directed the project to the ARB and a revised grading plan before a public hearing.

cases.name: 4 Kensico Court (Awesome Landscaping)
cases.applicant: John G. Scarlett Jr. for Awesome Landscaping

timeline.summary: Proposed reuse of an existing building for a small (~150 sq ft) office plus truck parking and outdoor storage for a landscaping business. Review letter issues include lighting, some existing parking spaces sitting on town property, and 20-ft aisles that fall short of the 24-ft standard. The board discussed reworking the ~51-space lot to become code-compliant (or seeking targeted ZBA variances) while preserving impervious coverage and truck turnaround. The chair was supportive of the concept and directed the applicant to produce the best compliant site plan possible before any variance request.

The board reviewed a revised plan for a parking lot where some spaces had encroached on town/road right-of-way. The applicant eliminated the off-property spaces (they cannot be counted and may need physical removal if the highway department requires it) and restriped the existing lot, converting some aisles to one-way angled parking, yielding 41 spaces against a 30-space requirement. One outstanding item is a lighting plan for the area, which the applicant has engaged someone to prepare. The board praised the 'clever design' and will schedule a public hearing once the paperwork and notice are ready.

The applicant sought an amended site plan to add a second tenant (a landscaping equipment/vehicle storage use) to a warehouse building that had never received formal site plan approval. Changes included reworking parking to a one-way in/out layout with spaces designated for the principal building versus the tenant, and a new lighting design brought up to current dark-sky code. No members of the public appeared. The board closed the hearing and approved the amended site plan, with the lighting review satisfying condition number two.

cases.name: 909 North Broadway Cigar / Membership Club (Sir John's Plaza)
cases.applicant: James Montelione (representing the membership club)

timeline.summary: A town-board special-use-permit application for a membership club at Sir John's Plaza was referred to the Planning Board for comment. The chair questioned how the code's required 25-foot-deep planting buffer would be satisfied given the site's history and rock conditions, and the planner explained the buffer requirement is aimed at screening golf-course-type clubs, not two converted storefronts. The board had no substantive objections. It voted to send a positive referral back to the town board.

A cigar membership club (special permit already granted by the Town Board, now in the site-plan phase) faced a parking question in the Surjon's Plaza strip mall. Adam Kaufman explained the membership-club parking code offers three standards and recommended the one-space-per-200-square-feet floor-area standard (about nine spaces), which likely avoids a variance, noting the shared lot and evening-only use. Members debated whether to use the more conservative fire-code/occupancy figure (about 17-18 spaces) as a more defensible, realistic number. The board agreed to cite a standard, made a referral to the ZBA for a parking variance if necessary, and Adam agreed to run the numbers; the submitted plan already showed 18 spaces.

The board took up the change-of-use site plan for the Social Life members club and cigar lounge. The planner explained the applicant already obtained its special use permit and, because the prior use was a bakery, the off-street parking calculation for the shopping center showed no parking variance was needed (17 spaces under the one-space-per-three-seats standard). With no physical changes to the site, this was a simple change of use. Members joked about the concept, asked about liquor licensing and membership tiers, then closed the hearing and approved the change-of-use site development plan.

cases.name: 7 New King Street
cases.address: 7 New King Street, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: P. Daniel Hollis (attorney) and Joe Rina (engineer) for the Santamaria/Lord company

timeline.summary: Applicant proposed squaring off and adding ~6,000 sf to an existing warehouse (former hunt/rod-and-gun club) used to store maintenance materials for the owner's real-estate portfolio, on a PFOA-affected, bottled-water property. Discussion centered on whether warehouse is a permitted use in the IND-AA district; the board and staff agreed the cleanest path is a petition to the town board to make warehouse a permitted use rather than chase a nonconforming-use argument. Staff also flagged parking counts, wetland-buffer disturbance and a drainage easement to be eliminated.
This was listed as a discussion item, but no one appeared for the applicant. The board laid the matter over to a future meeting.

cases.name: 428-436 Main Street
cases.applicant: P. Daniel Hollis (attorney) for the property owner

timeline.summary: Discussion of whether a 1996 ZBA parking variance for this pre-existing nonconforming mixed-use building was a blanket approval covering any future use. Counsel Baroni and staff disagreed with the blanket reading, advising the applicant either to return to the ZBA for any additional variance or to show that the currently proposed all-retail mix is no more intense than the 1996 uses (supported by a 1996 appraisal). The board agreed the appraisal plus resolution gives a benchmark to move forward.

Largely procedural update to a site plan approved in January 2025. The prior approval was conditioned on providing parking for an accessory apartment; the ZBA later granted a variance for 22 parking spaces, so the site plan must be updated to match. The board declined to skip the required (now-expired) public hearing and scheduled a new hearing, with a resolution expected at the next meeting.

cases.name: Summer Club golf-course-community residential development (Route 22)
cases.applicant: Mark Winegarten (attorney), Jeff Mandel (principal), Ken Anderson (architect), Paul Sisak (JMC engineer) for Summit Club Partners LLC

timeline.summary: Applicant updated the board on the 73-unit residential component (7 AFFH units), reporting they eliminated the seventh building and its roadway and folded the AFFH units into the six existing buildings, consolidated amenities into a single relocated clubhouse (with a subdivision-line shift), and detailed guest golf cottages, on-site water district and sewage plans. Debate focused on overflow accessory parking within the buffer (which the applicant argued is code-permitted and offered to land-bank), screening adequacy, traffic on Route 22, and finalizing the water plan; the residential component is progressing toward a public hearing once the water plan is firmed up.

Work session on the residential component (6 buildings, ~73 units plus amenities) of a golf-course-community floating zone. The board and town staff catalogued outstanding items - water system design, wastewater/SCADA, conservation easement, AFFH units and phasing, over-55 restriction, recreation fees, and a newly added golf maintenance building - and pressed the applicant to reconcile the town water/sewer director's comments before approval. The board made clear the public hearing (continuing Nov 14) would not close soon.

cases.name: 23 Bedford Banksville Road zoning text amendment
cases.applicant: Tony Vinciano (Vinciano), attorney; Peter Gregory, engineer

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a site plan for occupancy of an existing ~15,500 sq ft multi-tenant office/storage building plus removal of the existing contractors' yard, with the previously proposed self-storage building now withdrawn from this application; the board declined to vote, citing possibly non-permitted storage/woodworking-metalworks uses and requiring a building-inspector opinion, and kept the hearing open.

The town board sent back draft language to rezone the property to CBB instead of GB (to bar the more intensive warehouse/self-storage use), and the Planning Board discussed whether narrowing permitted uses could have unintended consequences before making a positive referral back to the town board, 3-0.

cases.name: 11 Whipperwill Lane (single-family home / lane improvements)
cases.applicant: Ralph Alfonzetti (applicant/engineer), rep. by attorney Corey Selm of Zarin & Steinmetz

timeline.summary: Applicant's team (attorney Corey Salomon and engineer Ralph) presented a switch to the smaller 5,800 sq ft home, private-road widening within the right-of-way, an emergency-vehicle turnaround, and commitments negotiated with neighbors; the board pressed for an engineered survey of the road improvements and a detailed landscape plan before approval, then adjourned the reopened public hearing.

Public hearing on the revised plan addressing four prior items (lane improvements, relocated turnaround, tree removal, private agreement with neighbors); board closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree-removal permit as amended to add a no-parking restriction on the turnaround and relocation of two trees.

cases.name: The Bristol at 90 Business Park Drive - Armonk Fire Department non-emergency call agreement
cases.applicant: HSR / Bristol at Armonk (attorney Nick Capadora; Amy Silver-Maguire, COO, Ultimate Care)

timeline.summary: The applicant sought to replace the 2012 site-plan condition requiring a 24-hour on-site EMT (which they say conflicts with New York State law) with a detailed emergency-care policy aimed at eliminating non-emergency calls to the Armonk Fire Department; the board directed staff and counsel to draft an amended site-plan resolution with an accountability mechanism, to return for a public hearing.

The board adopted an amended resolution plus an emergency-care policy and flowchart establishing a procedure to reduce non-emergency calls to the Armonk Fire Department, with the fire department to report back to the planning board biennially for accountability.

cases.name: 8 Cold Drive
cases.applicant: Nizar Masu (attorney Corey Salomon, Zarin & Steinmetz; wetland expert Steve Moreno; landscape architect Richard Quigley)

timeline.summary: The homeowners asked to amend a 2021 approval to swap the pool and sport-court locations, which would disturb a small (~900 sq ft) marginal wetland/drainage pocket, remove about 26 trees, and cut into steep slopes, offset by a proposed 2.5:1 mitigation wetland, a rain garden, and robust reforestation; the board voiced real concern about disturbing a wetland for a recreational amenity and referred the wetland question to the Conservation Board with 'no promises.'

The same attorney reported on 8 Cold Drive, noting the applicant pulled the clearing and grading permit for the sport court and anticipates constructing it in spring. The board granted the requested extension of time without objection.

cases.name: 126 Lafayette Avenue (NC Auto Repair)
cases.applicant: DNV/DNC Auto Repair

timeline.summary: A rooftop-solar site plan surfaced that the building's current auto-service use was never approved by the Planning Board (it had been approved as a tree-service base of operations); the board asked the applicant to demonstrate conformance with the town code's auto-repair/body-shop requirements so a legal site plan can be granted before permitting the rooftop solar.

Public hearing on a site plan to legitimize the existing auto-repair use, add a 48-panel rooftop solar system and a three-bay rear addition, and remove a deteriorated Butler building and cargo trailer. No public appeared. Discussion covered the low-profile roof-mounted panels (nine inches above the roofline), the absence of a parapet wall (the adjacent Bell & Tony building screens it), and stormwater: the engineer noted no existing runoff treatment and required capture/treatment of roof-drain and paved-area runoff to the town engineer's satisfaction. The board opened and closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution the same night, approving the application with the stormwater condition.

cases.name: Two Trip Lane (extension of time)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer)

timeline.summary: Board discussed a requested extension of time tied to a prior notice of violation; the building inspector felt a year was unnecessary, and after discussion the board granted a three-month extension, mainly to allow the required Town Board submission.
The board granted an additional three-month extension of time at the request of the building inspector, noting the applicant is due before the town board Wednesday.

cases.name: Gateway residential project extension of time, 45 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Tony Viviano with Mike Tucker

timeline.summary: Applicant reported completing the required off-site mitigation (Town Board license along Maple/municipal lot, modified deed and CBA); board resolved the affordable-unit count (30 market-rate plus 4 affordable of 34 total), reviewed stormwater/floodplain and wetland-mitigation conditions, then closed the hearing and approved the site plan and wetlands permit.

The board granted a site-plan extension of time to August 11, 2025, mirroring the town board's special-use-permit extension. Discussion centered on the town's dissatisfaction with the property's appearance ('an eyesore' at the town entrance) and a 'gentleman's agreement' for the applicant to clean up the site; the board also pressed on why the permitted on-site rock crushing hadn't occurred (the crushed material is intended for reuse in the project).

Public hearing on an amended site plan, wetland and tree removal permit to remediate a heavily disturbed wetland site where a prior owner built an unpermitted second story (increasing bedrooms beyond septic approval) triggering a stop-work order. The board could not close the hearing pending ARB approval and DEC/health permits, but voted to have the planner convey to the building inspector that it would not object to relief allowing at-risk interior four-bedroom work; item carried to July.
The scheduled public hearing was rolled over to the next meeting and not heard.

cases.name: 3 Cedar Hill Road
cases.address: 3 Cedar Hill Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Homeowner (house addition and new front porch)

timeline.summary: A corner lot fronting on the scenic East Middle Patent Road requires Planning Board site plan approval for a first- and second-floor addition; the board discussed screening/visibility and a wetland delineation update and directed the applicant to the ARB before returning for a public hearing and resolution.

Public hearing for a house addition and new front porch on a corner lot that, because it fronts scenic East Middle Patent Road, carries two front-yard setbacks and thus came to the Planning Board rather than the RPRC. The chair explained the procedural quirk; the planner confirmed no variances were needed and that the project is wetland-compliant with verified flags and ARB approval already obtained. No public spoke. The board opened the hearing, closed it and granted the resolution in a single sequence.

cases.name: 26 Carolyn Place
cases.applicant: San Car Residence (Ralph Oppenzetti / architect Lutto Delio)

timeline.summary: The board discussed the proposed rear-yard pool and cabana with removal of illegally placed fill and legalization of existing house issues, then debated whether the gross-land-coverage overage requires a variance and voted to refer the applicant to the Zoning Board of Appeals, deferring a public hearing until any variance is resolved.

This application had its public hearing previously closed, but action was pending the applicant's ARB review. With ARB complete and a fill issue resolved (the applicant is removing the fill) plus a revised plan addressing town-engineer comments, the board proceeded. There were no outstanding board concerns. The board approved the site plan and tree-removal permit.

cases.name: 88 Byron Ridge Road
cases.address: 88 Byron Ridge Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Builder represented by Dan Sherman

timeline.summary: Applicant seeks a wetlands permit for a fence along the clearing/grading limit line and a propane tank; the board accepted the explanation that soil washed under the silt fence rather than being imported fill, and referred the buffer mitigation to the conservation board while encouraging a building-department permit for the LP tank.

This was an after-the-fact wetlands matter: additional disturbance occurred in the regulated wetland buffer during construction, drawing a notice of violation, and the originally approved 2022 mitigation plan had not been implemented for years. A proposed fence and 7,600 sq ft of 'no-mow' lawn had drifted into the record but were removed; the mitigation plan and fill removal have now been completed and observed by the town wetlands consultant, and the Conservation Board recommended approval. The board adopted the resolution as amended, adding a clarifying 'whereas' that the fence was removed and the placed fill was removed, with five-year monitoring beginning.

cases.name: John McNada site plan (shopping center, North Broadway)
cases.applicant: John Magnotta (represented by Mr. Dagostino; engineer Dave Toriano, PE)

timeline.summary: A field-change/as-built request to bless deviations from the approved plan (reconfigured/compact parking, relocated landscaping, revised lighting, an uninstalled light pole); the board, led by James Jensen's objections, was unwilling to simply rubber-stamp after-the-fact work and directed the applicant to return with an improved landscaping plan to break up the 'sea of asphalt.'

The applicant's team presented additional landscaping to soften the rear parking/blacktop area and screen the lot from North Broadway, noting the retaining-wall area was largely unplantable; the board approved the field change, to be memorialized by a resolution in the file.

cases.name: 47 High Street - demolition and new house (John Nickett, builder)
cases.applicant: John Nickitch (rep. Jim Atticarico, Cronin Engineering)

timeline.summary: The board reviewed the new-home site plan with a driveway off Cobbler's Lane; the driveway falls short of the required 200-foot sight line (about 140 ft) due to the crest, so a ZBA variance is likely, and neighbors raised traffic-safety concerns.

Reopened public hearing on demolishing the existing house and building a new one with a driveway relocated onto Cobblers Lane; numerous neighbors opposed the Cobblers driveway over traffic/visibility safety, but the applicant demonstrated ~201 ft of sight distance (meeting the 200 ft minimum) and the board adopted the resolution as amended (added a 50 ft septic separation and pretreatment fabric conditions) over Michael Pollack's dissent.

cases.name: 111 Lafayette Avenue - US mail logistics truck parking/warehouse
cases.applicant: Property owner operating a postal mail-hauling business

timeline.summary: Preliminary discussion of converting the property into the main office/operations base for a bulk-mail hauling business; the board needed floor plans, truck-parking layout, storage and access details and directed the applicant to meet with the town planner and engineer before proceeding.

Public hearing on a site plan to allow overnight commercial truck parking accessory to a warehouse/office building; the board worked through the parking table (9 office spaces required, 15 truck spaces, 24 provided), closed the hearing, and approved the resolution as amended to add conditions for a replacement fence and code-compliant lighting, plus floor plans to support the parking count.

cases.name: Summer Club extension of time
cases.applicant: Summer Club subdivision applicant

timeline.summary: The board supported the applicant's request to remove 72 interior trees early (before building permits) for marketing/staging of the first phase of townhouses, with stump grinding and wood-chip stabilization, and separately granted a 90-day extension of time for the final subdivision plat while health-department (sewage, water withdrawal/system) approvals are pending.
The board granted an extension of time for the Summer Club approval, a procedural item with little discussion.

cases.name: 76 Byron Ridge Road
cases.address: 76 Byron Ridge Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Lizzero

timeline.summary: Referred from the RPRC, this expansion of an existing lakeside house sits partly in a state-regulated wetland buffer; the engineer described the septic (a county no-objection letter was sought), stormwater Cultec chambers and a rain garden, a wetland mitigation/planting plan, and a reworked driveway with screening, and the board referred the application to the Conservation Board while asking that all resolution conditions be addressed promptly.

The applicant proposed an addition to an existing three-bedroom single-family house with a new driveway/curb, a rain garden for stormwater, and an extensive wetland-buffer mitigation planting plan (proposing ~16,475 sq ft of mitigation against a required ~12,838). No new bedrooms and no direct wetland impacts other than a path to Byram/Barbers Lake. The Byram Ridge Lake Homeowners Association representative and the Conservation Board both supported the plan, which they said greatly improves existing invasive-choked conditions. A board member questioned whether to approve with a long list of open resolution items or wait, but the engineer confirmed most items were already completed in the July 14 submission and the board was satisfied; the hearing was closed and the resolution approved.

cases.name: Goldman pool and patio (15 Stony Brook Place)
cases.applicant: Goldman (landscape architect John DeFeo)

timeline.summary: The landscape architect described a 20x40 pool and patio entirely within the 100-foot wetland buffer, constrained by septic setbacks, with a mitigation/invasive-removal plan; the board scheduled a site visit with the conservation board and directed the applicant to apply to the conservation board.

Public hearing on an in-ground pool, retaining wall and patio located entirely within the wetland buffer; with a Conservation Board recommendation of approval and mitigation plantings plus a five-year monitoring plan, the board closed the hearing and approved the resolution.

cases.name: 50 East Middle Patent Road - reconstruction of condemned house
cases.applicant: Property owner (rep. with Chris Wilson, UDI East)

timeline.summary: Amended site plan in the scenic district after a condemned 250-year-old foundation forced full demolition and rebuild of the main residence on the same footprint; the board was sympathetic to the sympathetic replacement design and referred the front-yard setback variance (48.1 ft vs. 75 required) to the ZBA pending ARB review.

Public hearing on rebuilding a house that had been condemned and fully demolished due to powder-post beetle damage; the new structure keeps the identical footprint but is three feet taller (still within height limits) with three added windows. Hearing closed and resolution approved.

cases.name: 1 Virginia Road (U-Haul)
cases.applicant: U-Haul, represented by Peter Gatto Jr. (Peter Gatto Associates)

timeline.summary: Site plan (first filed around 2015) to extend an existing rear canopy across the loading dock and rebuild three properly-sized truck ramps, with no changes to the front, sides or traffic path. The board discussed counting existing sheds in FAR and revisited the long-standing question of a Virginia Road sidewalk, concluding a single sidewalk would be a 'sidewalk to nowhere' and better handled through comprehensive town planning. Next steps are ARB approval and a public hearing.

After-the-fact site plan approval for a canopy and shed used for vehicle release/dispatch, plus an extended rear canopy and new rear loading ramps, in the IND-A district. Michael Pollack read the public hearing notice. The applicant had already obtained ARB approval matching the existing canopy in kind. Remaining conditions were largely minor (engineering comments, a lighting plan, and an FAR calculation the planner still needs). The board closed the hearing and approved the resolution, with the planner to confirm zoning compliance before signing.

cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue (Marquis Associates)
cases.applicant: Trevor, on behalf of property ownership; BOCES tenant (computer intake/repair)

timeline.summary: The applicant proposes a change of use from warehouse to warehouse plus work room for a BOCES computer intake/repair operation with about five employees in roughly 3,300 sq ft. Because the change of use compounds an existing off-street parking deficiency variance, the board referred the applicant to the ZBA. There was a side discussion about the building being labeled 56 while the town address is 70, and concern that the fire department could be misdirected. The board moved to send the applicant to the ZBA and anticipated scheduling a planning board hearing after a ZBA decision.

The applicant proposed converting roughly 1,768 sq ft of warehouse space to office within an existing building on a ~1.1-acre IND-A site. The only real issue had been parking: 87 spaces required versus 66 provided, resolved by a 21-space variance the ZBA granted in August. The board and applicant treated the matter as straightforward with no public comment. The hearing was closed and the resolution adopted.

cases.name: 84 Business Park Drive
cases.address: 84 Business Park Drive, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Eric Lashins, 84 Business Park Associates LLC

timeline.summary: A 60,470 sq ft office building on ~3.8 acres in the PLI zone with 242 existing spaces (4 per thousand). A newly signed lease with a medical user changes the parking formula, leaving the site four spaces short and requiring a four-space variance, though the applicant maintains ample parking exists. Members questioned the change of use and the medical share of the building, and several agreed the town's 4-per-thousand formula is antiquated. The board voted to refer the application to the ZBA.

Public hearing on a partial change of use from general office to medical office, which triggered a need for four additional parking spaces. The applicant had received a positive referral from the ZBA. With no comments or concerns from the Board or staff, Ruisi moved to approve the site plan for the change of use and it passed.

cases.name: 1 Israel Townsend Hill (Lot 4, 32 Orchard Drive subdivision)
cases.address: 1 Israel Townsend Hill, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello (representing)

timeline.summary: Discussion/introduction of a proposed four-bedroom home on the 1.6-acre Lot 4, consistent with the original subdivision, with eight trees for removal, moderate-to-steep slopes, a walkout basement, two retaining walls, and a septic system under county review. The home was reoriented to face Israel Townsend Hill Road. The applicant asked to set a public hearing; the Board scheduled a site walk (next Wednesday) and agreed to notice a hearing for Oct 27.

Second/new single-family house on Lot 4 of the previously approved (2024) 32 Orchard Drive subdivision. The applicant proposed removing eight trees, two front retaining walls, a walkout, a septic system and well consistent with the approved IPP, directing stormwater to the shared BMP across Israel Townsend Hill. The home was slightly reoriented from the subdivision layout to align with the new street and reduce excavation/retaining walls. ARB approval was obtained Oct 15 with only minor landscaping comments; the board opened the hearing, took brief questions, closed it, and adopted the resolution.

cases.name: 263 Bedford-Banksville Road (equestrian property)
cases.applicant: attorney Jerry (J. Fane)
cases.lastStatus: approved (field change amendment; pergola and fence changes to return as amended planning board approval)

trajectory.status: approved (field change amendment; pergola and fence changes to return as amended planning board approval)

timeline.summary: An extension-of-time request for a large equestrian property with a new residence, pool/pool house, renovated exercise barn, second stable, and garage with room quarters above. Counsel explained construction is proceeding in good faith without compliance issues but cannot finish within the original 18-month window, and sought clarification that the completion deadline runs co-terminus with the building permit. The board granted a one-year extension.

timeline.status: approved (field change amendment; pergola and fence changes to return as amended planning board approval)
timeline.summary: A new landscape architect proposed relatively minor tweaks to the previously approved plan on this former horse-farm property: shifting the pool closer to the house, reducing patio and retaining-wall extents, adding planting to manage runoff, minor driveway curve/gate changes, and asking to use asphalt instead of gravel on a steep driveway segment. Drainage remains as previously engineered. The board treated most items as a field change but determined the pergola and fence changes require returning to the Planning Board (rather than being handled by the RPRC) since new structures can't be approved as a field change. Conservation liaison input was sought given the site's wetland-buffer history. The board adopted the field-change amendment resolution.

cases.name: IBM EV Charging Stations (1 New Orchard Road)
cases.address: 1 New Orchard Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: IBM; Seth Waltzman (representative) and colleague Stephanie

trajectory.status: discussion only (Level 2 to be approved at January hearing; board voted to recommend Town Board permit Level 3)

timeline.status: discussion only (Level 2 to be approved at January hearing; board voted to recommend Town Board permit Level 3)
timeline.summary: IBM proposed installing EV chargers in its gated, security-restricted visitor lot - three Level 2 plus one dual Level 3 fast charger - but town zoning currently limits infrastructure to Levels 1-2, so Level 3 requires a Town Board law change (a use variance being too high a bar). IBM stressed conduit run mostly above ground with minimal disturbance and no new municipal power load. The board noted a Town Board discussion on amending the EV-charger definition was already on that Wednesday's agenda, scheduled the site-plan public hearing for January, and voted to send a memo recommending the Town Board permit Level 3 charging at this gated site (which removes the highway-motorist concern).

IBM sought amended site plan approval to install four EV charging stations in its gated visitors' parking lot, to be built as Level 2 now and upgraded to Level 3 if the town adopts the pending code change permitting Level 3 chargers. Adam confirmed no planning concern and that approval would let IBM build Level 3 later without returning to the board. Carthy questioned the applicant's use of the word 'variance,' which staff clarified was actually a town-wide law change. The board opened and closed the hearing and adopted the resolution.

cases.name: 125 Business Park Drive (Lot 5, Westchester Business Park)
cases.address: 125 Business Park Drive, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Owner of Lot 5, Westchester Business Park
cases.lastStatus: public hearing reopened and closed; approved

trajectory.status: public hearing reopened and closed; approved

timeline.summary: The applicant sought reapproval of a previously approved but expired site plan for an approximately 9,390 sq ft warehouse and office building with associated parking and loading. The hearing was opened and immediately adjourned; no substantive discussion or public comment occurred.

timeline.status: public hearing reopened and closed; approved
timeline.summary: A prior approval had expired and the applicant re-ran the planning board process, obtaining the required Zoning Board of Appeals approval. The board reopened and closed the public hearing (no public present). A board member raised that the property sits in a wetland buffer and asked whether the wetlands regulations/buffers had changed since the original 2006/2008 approvals; confirmed they had not. The board adopted the NegDec and the draft resolution.

cases.name: 667 North Broadway (Virgin Mary & St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church)
cases.applicant: Virgin Mary and St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church (Father Tedros and a church representative)
cases.lastStatus: public hearing closed; approved with conditions

trajectory.status: public hearing closed; approved with conditions

timeline.summary: The church proposed a level sidewalk cutting across its own adjoining lot to give elderly and disabled parishioners accessible entry to the lower level of the church, avoiding numerous steps. No exterior changes to the building or the existing retaining wall are proposed, so the planner advised no ARB approval is needed and that existing non-conforming components would not require variances since nothing is changing. The chair explored whether an ADA ramp might serve better than the level walk, then directed the applicant to meet with the planner and schedule a public hearing.

timeline.status: public hearing closed; approved with conditions
timeline.summary: The church sought a new walkway to provide handicap access to the lower level of the church building, using the adjacent driveway as a drop-off. A neighbor who works at 661 North Broadway delivered a lengthy, highly critical presentation alleging application errors and omissions, structural risk to the church's stone wall and buttresses, missing earthwork/erosion controls, tree loss, and traffic/safety hazards at a busy intersection. The applicant and town engineer downplayed the cut/fill volume and structural risk, and the board added a condition requiring a soil-erosion-control plan to the town engineer's satisfaction plus existing DOT right-of-way documentation. The board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution as amended.

cases.name: 23 North Lake Road
cases.address: 23 North Lake Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: David Haber (owner); Conrad Rancotti, project architect; engineer (continuity from prior design)
cases.lastStatus: public hearing closed; site plan, wetlands permit, and tree-removal permit approved as amended (applicant to return for amendment)

trajectory.status: discussion only (to return after Conservation Board and ARB, then public hearing)
public hearing closed; site plan, wetlands permit, and tree-removal permit approved as amended (applicant to return for amendment)

timeline.status: discussion only (to return after Conservation Board and ARB, then public hearing)
timeline.summary: A new four-bedroom house reusing an existing, never-used pool and septic field on a steep site. The item before the board was an over-six-foot retaining wall (up to ~10.17 feet, ~7.17 feet retaining soil) at the front of a courtyard, faced in native stone. The architect also floated a modification relocating the third (one-car) garage next to the two-car garage, with a reduced two-car garage and a breezeway to limit added mass. The board found the design attractive and was supportive, directing the applicant to finish with the Conservation Board (meeting the 17th), return to the ARB for the change, and then come back for a public hearing. Stormwater and septic re-certification with the Health Department were noted.

timeline.status: public hearing closed; site plan, wetlands permit, and tree-removal permit approved as amended (applicant to return for amendment)
timeline.summary: A new single-family home requiring Planning Board review for an ~11-foot (8-foot structural plus 3-foot aesthetic extension) retaining wall, on a pond-front lot with wetlands, prior-owner disturbance, and an existing pool to be reduced. Chairman Carthy recused and left; Lawrence Ruisi acted as chair and Tom Crispi read the hearing notice. The core open issue was stormwater treatment: a buried CulTec system under the courtyard versus a town-engineer-suggested bioretention/rain garden in the wetland buffer, which would require returning to the conservation board. After debating whether approving now would set a precedent for laden conditions, the board approved the current plan (site plan, wetlands permit, tree-removal permit) as amended, with the applicant expected to return for a full amendment once the rain-garden and mitigation revisions are worked out. Conservation board representative George Trapow praised the project as a model example.

cases.name: NYC DEP Kensico-Eastview Wetland Mitigation (Old Post Road)
cases.address: Old Post Road / Route 120, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: NYC Department of Environmental Protection (Angel Riness and team)

timeline.summary: DEP presented the wetland mitigation component of the Kensico-Eastview Connection (KEC) water-tunnel program, tied to a shoreline stabilization project in Mount Pleasant. The mitigation would enlarge an existing wetland to establish ~2.5 acres of marsh/open water and ~1.7 acres of upland habitat, removing ~388 trees, using a Route 120 construction access and a one-acre staging area (five trees removed there). Construction expected late summer/early fall 2026 with limited truck traffic; rock removal by mechanical means with blasting as a contract option. The board asked about blasting radius, nearby houses and underground infrastructure near the reservoir/tunnel, and voted to refer the project to the Conservation Board.

The DEP presented the wetland mitigation component of the Kensico-Eastview Connection (KEC) program, including shoreline stabilization (1,600 linear feet of rip-rap hardening), creation of roughly 2.5 acres of wetland at the Big Peninsula, and a one-acre construction staging area at Old Post Road. Construction runs fall 2026 through roughly 2029-2031 within the town's noise ordinance hours, with minimal projected traffic (about three peak-hour trucks per direction). The Conservation Board reported it had done a site walk and given a positive recommendation, and the town planner noted a thorough submission with no significant concerns. The board opened the hearing, took public comment, closed it, adopted SEQRA findings identical to DEP's, and approved the site plan, wetlands, and tree removal permits.

cases.name: 1 East Middle Patent Road (accessory garage)
cases.address: 1 East Middle Patent Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Dan O'Connor, PC consulting engineer (three-car, ~810 sq ft garage)

timeline.summary: Discussion of a proposed 810-square-foot three-car accessory garage on a large scenic-road parcel, set well back from the road with no tree removal, minor grading/fill, an existing gravel access drive, and a rain-garden stormwater system. The chair questioned why the aerial/GIS didn't clearly show the gravel drive and probed whether any trees would come down, satisfied by the engineer's answers. The board sent the applicant to the ARB for reclamation approval before returning for a hearing.

The applicant proposed a detached 810-square-foot accessory garage; any accessory structure over 800 sq ft requires a special use permit, and the property sits along a scenic road. Thomas Crispi read the notice of public hearing. The ARB had approved the plan and the planner and engineer flagged only minor items (soil testing, cut/fill verification). With no public present and no objections, the board closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution with conditions.

cases.name: 6 Sterling Road South
cases.address: 6 Sterling Road South, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Hudson Engineering (James German / Nicholas Shri) for the property owner
cases.lastStatus: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)

trajectory.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)

timeline.summary: Discussion of a proposed detached garage with a guest bedroom plus a mudroom addition. The board wrestled with whether the structure is a permissible accessory structure, since code bars an accessory structure from combining a garage with living space, and questioned whether it should instead be characterized as an apartment with a garage (though it lacks a kitchen). The planner considered it a straightforward application with only technical comments outstanding, but proposed gross land coverage exceeds what is permitted, pointing toward a possible ZBA referral. With no applicant or representative present, the board took no action and held the matter for the next meeting.

timeline.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)
timeline.summary: The applicant proposed improvements to a single-family residence on a three-acre lot: removing the attached garage and building a larger three-car garage with a small living space/bedroom (going from five to six bedrooms), reshaping the driveway, and adding a mudroom, with a net decrease in impervious area and a new infiltration practice. The applicant addressed a septic concern by showing the 2004 system was designed for eight bedrooms. The main open item is a code provision barring living quarters in a garage, to be confirmed with the building inspector. The board directed the project to the ARB before returning for a public hearing.

cases.name: One Gion Lane - new single-family home
cases.applicant: Elliot / LEA (engineer for owner)

timeline.summary: Neighbor-notification meeting on a proposed ~3,800 sf home (5,900 sf including garage/decks) on a constrained R2A lot; neighbors raised driveway headlights, privacy, screening and stormwater concerns. After a long board debate about the large number of open items on the draft resolution and how much should be delegated administratively, the board closed the notification meeting and approved the resolution as amended, requiring a more deer-resistant screening plan in place of arborvitae.

cases.name: 100 Hunter Drive - tree removal and landscaping
cases.applicant: Dean Pushcar (landscape designer) for owner

timeline.summary: Neighbor-notification hearing on removal of 18 (net ~15 on-property) mostly poor-condition trees on a former estate lot in the R1A district, with a robust replacement plan of ~47 trees including green giant arborvitae, white spruce and shade trees. Chairman Carthy recused himself and Michael Pollack presided. A neighbor sought maximum privacy screening. The board found the plan much improved, closed the notification portion and adopted the resolution as amended (excluding right-of-way trees).

cases.name: One Kent Place - Maury (legalization of sheds/coolers/patios)
cases.applicant: Andrew Nester, JMC (for One Kent Place Inc.)

No public comment. The board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution, with a portion of patio/wall over the property line and part of a shed to be removed.

cases.name: 20 Manus River Road - house renovation, pool and cabana
cases.applicant: John Needham (owner) with Pete Gregory (engineer)

The board discussed the retaining wall, pool siting (rear vs side yard), and treated the utility work as a minor administrative wetlands permit; next steps are ARB review then a public hearing with a draft resolution.

cases.name: PODS storage facility - 94 Business Park

The board asked for a schematic showing interior staging and capacity and felt the meeting made progress.

cases.name: 14 Tall Woods Road in-ground pool and wetland permit

timeline.summary: Continued public hearing on an in-ground swimming pool with stormwater mitigation and a pool draw-down/irrigation storage system in an R-2A wetland-buffer area; after discussion of a rain garden, roof-runoff rerouting and relocating pool equipment indoors, the board closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution.

cases.name: 4 Armonk Heights Road new single-family home
cases.address: 4 Armonk Heights Road (corner of Fairway and Armonk Heights Road)
cases.applicant: Angela Gavino (owner/developer)

timeline.summary: Early site-plan review of a proposed ~7,000 sq ft home (with a barn removed from the plan after wetlands-consultant concerns); the board asked the applicant to reduce disturbance, consider tiered grading on steep slopes, stake out the house, and set up a Planning Board and Conservation Board site walk.

cases.name: Birken property, 99 Byram Ridge Road new single-family home
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch (LPN Engineering); Taylor Seguinza, architect

cases.name: Extensions of time (215 Business Park Drive, 124 Mount Kisco Road, Hidden Oaks subdivision)
cases.address: 215 Business Park Drive; 124 Mount Kisco Road; Hidden Oaks

cases.name: Hoberman lot-line realignment, 10 & 20 Round Hill Road (Rolling Hill subdivision)

cases.name: Tripling Lane residence site plan / wetlands

The Conservation Board liaison challenged leaving the wall and importing clean fill instead of restoring natural grade. The board referred the over-height driveway piers to the ZBA and asked for an interim/sequencing grading plan.

cases.name: Harris, 9 Sterling Road
cases.applicant: Harris

timeline.summary: The applicant was not ready and will return, likely at the next meeting; no substantive discussion occurred.

cases.name: 246 Massaro Court lot line change re-approval

timeline.summary: A public hearing was opened on re-approval of a previously approved lot line change whose approval and extension had expired; the applicant explained they still need time to finalize easements and file the plat with the county.

cases.name: Town of North Castle / Verizon municipal parking lot, 23 Whippoorwill Road East
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (engineer Joe; involves adjacent Verizon parcel)

cases.name: Summit Club maintenance building
cases.applicant: Summit Club (rep. Paul Sysak; architect Ken Anderson)

cases.name: Silver Lake Realty Company, 600/606 North Broadway
cases.applicant: Silver Lake Realty Company (Jim Fleming, architect)

timeline.summary: Public hearing opened and closed on a site plan to legalize existing uses in a building straddling the White Plains/North Castle line so building permits can issue; the board adopted the resolution with conditions after discussing a dog-grooming use question.

cases.name: Airport Campus townhomes (Toll Brothers)
cases.applicant: Toll Brothers (Max Nellin, attorney; Kevin Moses)

cases.name: 11 Whippoorwill Lane

cases.name: Harris pool and patio, 9 Sterling Road North
cases.applicant: Hugh Harris

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a new pool and patio in a town-regulated wetland buffer; with Conservation Board recommendation and only technical engineering items remaining, the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution approving it after roughly six years of review.

cases.name: Birken residence teardown and rebuild, 99 Byron Ridge Road
cases.applicant: Birken

cases.name: Rosenthal residence expansion, 10 Creamer Road
cases.applicant: Rosenthal

cases.name: 17 New King Street unpermitted canopy / ZBA referral

cases.name: Swansberg renovation, 103 Miller Road (scenic road)
cases.applicant: John Swansberg

timeline.summary: First presentation of a modest renovation of a pre-existing nonconforming 1700s house on a scenic road (68'8" front setback where 75' required), with a Mianus River Gorge easement; the board raised no substantive concerns and referred it to the ZBA for the front-yard setback and directed the applicant to the ARB and to set a public hearing.

cases.name: San Car residence pool relocation, 26 Carolon Place
cases.applicant: Sankar

timeline.summary: Discussion of relocating an existing pool, cabana, and pool equipment closer to the house, complicated by possible illegal/untested fill (red brick and concrete) and unpermitted interior work known to the building inspector; the board decided to conduct a site walk before proceeding.

cases.name: Red Brook Glen subdivision lots (site plan approval)

timeline.summary: Two adjacent lots created in the Red Brook Glen subdivision, each requiring planning board site plan approval per a plat note; the board and engineer found the lots straightforward (easy driveway grades, workable stormwater, outside the wetland buffer) and scheduled a site walk before acting.

cases.name: Conyers Farm-area remediation site plan (Kudrill property)
cases.applicant: Nicholas Kudrill, owner (Jay Fain, J. Fain Associates; engineer Tom Lautomat; Jerry Tortorella)

timeline.summary: The owner, who bought the property in Nov 2022 from a contractor whose work triggered a stop-work order and left the site unstable, is seeking a site plan, wetlands and tree permit to bring the site back into conformance with the prior approval (with 2:1 wetland mitigation and DEC coordination on a state wetland); citing time being of the essence, the board agreed to set a public hearing for June 24 while the applicant proceeds to the Conservation Board and ARB.

cases.name: 601 Bedford Road (Embassy Club / old country club)
cases.applicant: Nick (owner, resides on site)

timeline.summary: The applicant is restoring a fire-damaged former club building back into a house (with the existing house to become an accessory apartment) and reported the ARB required a strict restoration to the original appearance (cupola removed, six-over-six windows); unresolved septic and roof-stormwater questions remain because the existing leaching field cannot be located, and zoning variances are still to be defined, so the board asked the applicant to address staff comments before any ZBA referral.

cases.name: 34 Cream Road (amended site plan / wetlands permit update)
cases.applicant: Property owner (returning applicant)

timeline.summary: An update to a previously approved (2018) house design that now adds a pool with generally unchanged limits of disturbance; the Conservation Board recommended approval of the wetlands permit and the ARB reportedly approved the design, so the board indicated it can hold a public hearing and draft resolution at the next meeting.

cases.name: Canyon Club / golf course special use permit (Summer Club)
cases.applicant: Jeff Mendel (developer)

timeline.summary: On a town-board referral, the board discussed the special-use-permit parameters for the golf-course club (500 members, golf/tennis/pickleball/swimming, a 100-child summer day camp, golf outings, social events, up to 10 guest cottages, sewage-treatment-plant rebuild and new maintenance building) and debated whether 500 members is reasonable versus comparable clubs; it also voted to refer the applicant to the ZBA to address parking credit for on-site residents, and heard a project update from the developer.

Applicant (engineer Ralph Alfonzetti of AB Engineering) sought a rock-crushing permit to process ~1,000-1,200 yards of foundation rock on-site for reuse; the board approved it subject to a 10-day maximum, 9am-4:30pm hours, and voluntary neighbor notification by mailing.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge Preserve barn, 99 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Mianus River Gorge (Preserve)

timeline.summary: The Gorge proposes an accessory barn to the land steward's house; because it exceeds 25% of the main house floor area it needs a ZBA variance, so the board referred it to the ZBA to run in parallel while stormwater staff comments are addressed.

cases.name: Gobino residence, Kites Road (new house, pool, pool house)
cases.applicant: Angela Gobino

timeline.summary: Owner/developer presented a new house with pool and pool house on a steep hillside requiring extensive regrading and tiered retaining walls (cutting ~6,800 yards and importing ~7,800 yards of fill); the board urged him to rotate the pool, reduce wall tiers, and engage a landscape architect, and he agreed to revise and return.

Applicant reported the ZBA granted variances (curb-cut width, pier height) and soil testing witnessed by the town consultant found no hydric soil / no wetland at Four Trip; the board, satisfied with the resolved grading and swale recreation, agreed to set a public hearing for the next meeting.

cases.name: Maraki Tavarna restaurant, 450 Main Street (CVS shopping center)

timeline.summary: Change of use for a restaurant space at the CVS center; the applicant was not present so the item was adjourned, but the board held a long policy discussion about the cumulative parking-variance requests in the Armonk hamlet and whether the property should join or form a parking district rather than seek repeated variances.

Applicant seeks to convert an existing approved office/garage structure to an accessory apartment; because the structure was not built prior to 1984 it needs a ZBA variance, so the board referred it to the ZBA (applicant absent) to avoid losing a month.

cases.name: Shell gas station, 375 Main Street extension of time

timeline.summary: The board granted an extension of time for the Shell gas station; the applicant is still awaiting DOT permits for work in the state right-of-way and reconsidering scope amid an ownership change.

The applicant built a taller retaining wall pulled forward of the approved location, changed screening/landscaping, omitted parking-lot lighting and compactor bollards, and presented it as an as-built; the board declined to treat these as minor field changes and directed the applicant to return with a plan and presentation, possibly with a site visit.

cases.name: 35 Whipperwill Road East (filled-in pond / wetlands violation)
cases.applicant: homeowner, rep. by engineer Brian Hildenbrand

timeline.summary: Referral from the RPRC on a homeowner who filled in a rear pond (cited for safety) and received a notice of violation; the applicant installed a pump system and now seeks a wetlands permit for the disturbance. Board directed the matter to the Conservation Board and Town Engineer/Building Inspector for review of floodplain/storage impacts before returning.

cases.name: Maraki Taberna - 50 Main Street
cases.applicant: Maraki Taberna

timeline.summary: No applicant representative appeared; the item was carried to the next meeting, with staff to reach out beforehand.

cases.name: Windmill Road parcel (rear lot merger referral)
