Board recommended merging the rear parcel into the front lot with a covenant against resubdivision (rather than developing it), as far less controversial, and sent that recommendation back to the Town Board.

Public hearing opened on a site plan, wetland permit and tree removal application to legalize and remediate unpermitted work (fill, tree removal, house addition) ongoing since 2020. No public comment; the hearing was held open because the Architectural Review Board approval for the house addition is still outstanding, and the board adjourned the hearing to a future meeting.

cases.name: 103 Mianus River Road
cases.applicant: John Swansburg

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a scenic-roadway site plan to replace additions on the north end of the house within the same footprint, adding minimal building and land coverage. The applicant had ARB and ZBA approval and no public appeared; the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution.

Public hearing on an amended site plan, wetland permit and tree removal for a single-family residence with driveway and pool in a wetland buffer, previously approved in 2018. A neighbor asked about remaining tree removal and screening; the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution as amended, adding a long-term monitoring/access note on the site plan.

Discussion item treated as a field change: the required handicap access ramp was relocated from the front to the rear of the building. The board approved the field change so the building department could close out the permits.

Discussion of a restaurant expansion into an adjacent retail bay requiring roughly 15 additional parking spaces. The planner floated forming a Maple Avenue parking district, which the board and applicant viewed as a non-starter since the property owner would give up a parking asset for little benefit. The board referred the applicant to the ZBA for the parking variance without making a formal recommendation.

cases.name: Breezemont Day Camp, 60 Cocks Avenue
cases.applicant: Gordon Josie (owner/director) and Walter (co-director), Breezemont Day Camp

timeline.summary: The board took up the special use permit for the Breezemont day camp, an existing legal non-conforming use seeking to make it a permitted use so future improvements are possible; the applicant began explaining planned upgrades before the recording cut off.

cases.name: Battery/energy-storage legislation review
cases.applicant: Town Board (referral for legislation review)

timeline.summary: The board discussed proposed battery/energy-storage zoning legislation, state efforts to override local zoning, and the public-utility definition, then recommended the town board adopt the legislation.

Continued public hearing on an existing house being brought into conformance; the board reviewed updated architectural plans (bedroom count reduced to six to match a six-bedroom septic), retaining-wall and mitigation conditions, and pending DEC and health-department approvals, then closed the hearing and approved the amended site plan, tree removal and wetland permit.

A house under construction had its foundation built six inches too high and its front porch changed from piers to a poured wall, causing plan discrepancies that pushed it from the RPRC to the Planning Board. The board and neighbors raised concerns about front-yard grade, mass and retaining walls, and stormwater; the board scheduled a site visit, will bring the applicant back in August, and plans a September public hearing.
The board granted two extensions of time for the Summer Club at Armonk, one for the subdivision and one for the site plan, with no concerns raised.

A straightforward accessory barn on a scenic road that had already cleared the ZBA, ARB and engineering review returned for final action; the board found no neighbors present, closed the public hearing and approved the draft resolution quickly.

cases.name: 4 Trip Lane (Frederick Paul/Bolander)
cases.applicant: Frederick Paul

timeline.summary: A long-running application (started 2020) involving unpermitted work, tree removal and fill returned after obtaining ARB approval; the board reopened and closed the hearing, confirmed gross-floor-area was well under the maximum, amended the resolution to remove conditions 3 and 4, and approved it.

cases.name: 22 Whipple Well Road East retaining wall / grading

timeline.summary: Following a site walk, the board pressed the applicant on unclear grades, the height and consistency of a veneered retaining wall, stormwater infiltration units and screening; it asked for site sections, an as-built survey, and options showing one wall versus a second tier plus a robust landscape plan before proceeding.

cases.name: Jenny Clarkson property, 1700 Old Orchard Street - slope remediation

timeline.summary: Construction/demolition fill placed without permits had washed across Route 22 into the reservoir; the applicant proposed removing roughly 18 inches of C&D material with full-time inspection and re-grading a basin/swale. DEP and the Conservation Board signed off, but the board declined to place unresolved technical items in a resolution and directed the applicant's engineer to work out details offline with the town engineer before a hearing.

cases.name: 73 Whipple Well Road two-lot subdivision (Wellness Estates LLC)
cases.applicant: Wellness Estates LLC (Alice Geske)

timeline.summary: A sketch-plat discussion for a two-lot subdivision of an 8.8-acre R2A parcel containing a pond, watercourse, wetlands and steep slopes; frontage and the desire to preserve a 2005 septic system drove the irregular lot shape. The board found no major issues, discussed whether a better layout was possible, touched on the open-space/recreation-fee requirement, and encouraged the applicant to submit a preliminary application.
The board granted an extension of time for the airport campus approval on a routine motion with no discussion.

cases.name: Maraki Taverna restaurant expansion
cases.applicant: Maraki Taverna (represented by Chris Crocco)

timeline.summary: The board held the public hearing on the expansion of the restaurant into the adjacent space, confirmed the applicant had obtained its off-street parking variance from the ZBA, and adopted the site plan resolution.

cases.name: 10 Round Hill Way site plan
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Realty LLC (Cory Salmore, Zarin & Steinmetz)

timeline.summary: The board held the public hearing and adopted the site plan resolution as amended, requiring a substantial re-vegetated buffer on the regraded slope between the pool and the neighbor's property line and second-floor bedroom sprinklers.

cases.name: 20 Round Hill Way site plan
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Realty LLC (Cory Salmore, Zarin & Steinmetz)

timeline.summary: The board held a brief public hearing with no public comment, confirmed the clearing and grading limit line was not significantly changed and no wetland permit was needed, and adopted the resolution as amended for second-floor bedroom sprinklers.

cases.name: 9 Barnard (Nye and Barnard) retaining wall
cases.applicant: Joe Gentile

timeline.summary: Continued discussion of an existing over-height retaining wall built without a permit and the associated fill/soil testing; the board reaffirmed its preference for a tiered wall set back from the neighbor and directed HES and the applicant's environmental firm to coordinate on-site sampling, carrying the matter to the next meeting.

cases.name: Summer Club golf course maintenance facility
cases.applicant: Summer Club (JMC engineering)

timeline.summary: Review of the site plan for the golf-course maintenance building under the existing special-use permit; with few outstanding items the board directed the applicant to schedule a public hearing and move toward site-plan approval.

cases.name: Massaro Court 3-lot subdivision
cases.applicant: Bernardo and Philomena Luciano (Hudson Engineering)

timeline.summary: An approved but unfiled subdivision with a lot-line change; the board granted an extension of time and gave informal direction to let the town engineer get the plat signed, deferring several site-specific conditions to later site-plan review rather than reopening the resolution.

cases.name: Main Street building parking variance (CBA-2 district)
cases.applicant: George Calcutini (representing owner)

timeline.summary: Applicant sought flexibility to allow any permitted CBA-2 use, effectively raising the parking variance from about 20 to 32 spaces so tenants would not need to return for amended approvals; the board was reluctant to shift the parking burden onto the street, pushed the idea of joining a future parking district, and recommended the applicant go to the ZBA for two additional apartment spaces.

cases.name: 18 Carolyn Place additions and retaining wall
cases.applicant: homeowner (John Williams, Hierarch Design)

timeline.summary: Proposed side additions, porches, patio resurfacing and regrading with an over-six-foot retaining wall; once it emerged the tall wall was existing rather than new, the board concluded the matter belonged at the RPRC with an administrative wetlands permit and referred it back, carrying over the submission.

cases.name: 14 Middle Patent Road condition amendment
cases.applicant: applicant (Sarah O'Shea, attorney)

timeline.summary: Applicant requested moving three conditions to be satisfied prior to the certificate of occupancy so the building permit could issue and construction proceed; with the building inspector's concurrence the board granted the change.

cases.name: 88 Old Byram Lake Road (new single-family home)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer/representative)

timeline.summary: Public hearing for a new five-bedroom single-family home and removal of 18 regulated trees on a five-acre lot from the Red Brook Glen subdivision; the board found the plan conforming to what was contemplated during the subdivision and approved the site plan and tree removal permit with conditions for wetland-buffer demarcation and a foundation landscaping plan.

cases.name: 86 Old Byram Lake Road (new single-family home)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer/representative)

timeline.summary: Public hearing for a new five-bedroom home and removal of 23 regulated trees on an adjacent Red Brook Glen lot; the board approved the site plan and tree removal permit, discussing stormwater infiltration systems, existing screening to the neighbor, and boundary trees before adopting the resolution.

cases.name: Summit Club maintenance building
cases.applicant: David Lombardi, JMC (professional engineer for the Summit Club)

timeline.summary: Public hearing opened on a 7,220 sq ft maintenance building with chemical storage, fueling, and wash-water recycling as the next phase of the golf course redevelopment; the board discussed an off-street parking variance (shared-parking credit between the golf and residential parcels) and separation of chemical from petroleum storage. A recording gap obscures whether a vote was taken, though staff and members were favorable.

cases.name: New home concept - Cobbler-side driveway (High Street area)

timeline.summary: Concept-level discussion of a new home where the board weighed driveway access from the Cobbler side versus High Street; given existing screening on the neighbor's property, the board directed the applicant to proceed developing the home with the Cobbler-side driveway and return with a refined landscaping and tree-removal plan.

cases.name: 263 Bedford-Banksville Road (extension of time)
cases.applicant: represented by 'Jerry' (agent)

timeline.summary: The applicant, holding a prior special permit and site plan approval for a residence with pool, pool house, and personal equestrian accessory structures, requested and was granted a one-year extension of time to obtain permits and begin construction.

cases.name: Summit Club Partners LLC subdivision (extension of time)
cases.applicant: Summit Club Partners LLC

timeline.summary: The board granted a 90-day extension of time for the Summit Club subdivision, with the consultant reporting the applicant is working through the conditions and no concerns.

cases.name: 8 Coal Drive - pool, cabana and sport court
cases.applicant: Mr. Massu (rep. Corey Salmer, Zarin & Steinman)

timeline.summary: The board conducted and closed the public hearing (no public present) and adopted a resolution approving the site plan, tree removal, steep slope and wetlands permits for a pool, cabana and relocated sport court after the conservation board recommended approval of the wetlands permit.

Introduced for discussion but the substantive dialogue falls in a gap in the ASR transcript; later references indicate it involved a clearing-and-grading limit line similar to the Dellwood Farm Way pool item.

cases.name: Gavi - first-floor residential in commercial zone

timeline.summary: On a town board referral, the board reviewed the special use permit needed for two first-floor residential units (four dwelling units total, plus retail/restaurant work) and recommended the town board proceed with issuing the special use permit, which would then bring the applicant back for site plan approval.

Instead of a one-year extension, the board granted only a three-month extension of time at the building inspector's recommendation, because the mail-delivery property owner is storing trucks and excavated without a permit, not in conformance with the approved site plan; the short window is meant to pressure compliance.

cases.name: Sanders - pool at 12 Dellwood Farm Way (Hammond Ridge subdivision)
cases.applicant: Sanders

timeline.summary: The board discussed a request to modify the subdivision's clearing-and-grading limit line to allow a 75-foot lap pool that extends onto a steep slope and requires regrading and removal of roughly seven or eight trees; members found the impact minor on the four-acre wooded lot and reached consensus to schedule a neighbor-notification public hearing, pending stormwater calculations. Chair Carthy recused himself due to an interest in the application.

cases.name: Little Sparrows Nursery School (Hillside Church), 448 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Little Sparrows Nursery School / Hillside Church

timeline.summary: Public hearing on legalizing the school's expansion from two to six classrooms; the board closed the hearing, adopted a negative declaration, and approved the site plan subow to conditions 4 and 5 (lot-area-per-child) being proven out before the plan is signed.

cases.name: Shapiro residence, 8 Rosanne Drive
cases.applicant: Shapiro (represented by Corey Salomon, Zarin & Steinman)

timeline.summary: New application on a 17.9-acre R1A property for recreational amenities (tennis/hard-tru court, padel court, grass field, central activity building, pergola) plus legalizing a pre-1984 accessory apartment; the board referred it to the ZBA, conservation board, and ARB, with the intensity of sport-court lighting the principal unresolved concern.

Applicant who had filled in a ~21-foot pond in a floodplain now proposes to restore the pond and eliminate a force main; the conservation board already referred it favorably, and the board voted to schedule a public hearing even though the applicant was not present.

cases.name: Public hearing item, address unclear (Chair recused)

timeline.summary: A public hearing was opened and then immediately adjourned to the next meeting; the Chair indicated he would recuse himself and the board noted it was short-handed tonight.

cases.name: 4 Leisure Farm Drive (in-ground pool / clearing-limit amendment)
cases.applicant: Ben Miller and Jacqueline Baylor (rep. Dean Poshler)

timeline.summary: The board held and closed the public hearing on amending the approved clearing/grading limit line to allow a pool, patio, retaining wall, and stormwater retention system, agreed no additional screening was needed, and adopted the resolution.

cases.name: Gavi restaurant expansion (Armonk)
cases.applicant: Gavi restaurant (rep. John, engineer/architect team)

timeline.summary: The board continued the hearing on a restaurant addition (~600 sf), a new ~5,000 sf building with first-floor apartments (requiring a town-board special use permit), reconfigured parking (~52-53 spaces plus 4 basement resident spaces), and a streetscape/sidewalk extension; some questions remained so the hearing stayed open for a resolution next meeting.

cases.name: Breeze Mountain (children's camp) parking and screening
cases.applicant: Breeze Mountain camp (rep. Walter)

timeline.summary: The board reviewed parking and perimeter screening so it could tell the town board it is comfortable and let the special permit proceed; the applicant will formalize a front drop-off/pick-up area (pavers/gravel), continue off-site shuttle parking at two churches, and submit a blown-up parking plan. No vote was needed tonight.

cases.name: 12 Delwood Farm - in-ground pool (clearing & grading limit line amendment)

timeline.summary: Public hearing on amending the clearing-and-grading limit line in the Hammond Ridge subdivision to allow a new in-ground pool and associated regrading; the applicant was not present but the board opened and closed the hearing and approved the amendment, noting ten trees to be removed.

cases.name: 15 / 22 (Gabriel Court apartments site plan)
cases.applicant: Joseph Crockle (architect); David Gessel (engineer)

timeline.summary: Reopened and closed the public hearing and adopted the site plan resolution after the applicant revised driveway and parking slopes off Gabriel Court to meet code for entrance, ADA and conventional parking; an outstanding lighting-illumination plan condition remains prior to signing.

cases.name: Forge Legewood single-family house (expired approval restart)

timeline.summary: A previously approved new single-family house whose resolution had expired; the applicant was told not to attend, and the board agreed to schedule a new public hearing and re-approve, discussing new practice of addressing conditions before signing and revisiting the phased planting/tree-replacement plan in the wetland buffer.

cases.name: 4 Ledgewood Place - re-approval of expired residence site plan
cases.applicant: 4 Ledgewood Place LLC

timeline.summary: Public hearing for re-approval of an expired site plan, wetlands permit, and tree removal approvals for a new four-bedroom residence; with no public present the board declined to vote on the resolution because 17 conditions remain unsatisfied, opting instead to have the applicant address them with staff and return for administrative approval.

cases.name: 298 Bedford Banksville Road - accessory apartment special use permit

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a special use permit to legalize a detached accessory apartment in a structure previously approved as an office; the required ZBA variance had been obtained, the board found the resolution concise, and it approved the special use permit subject to a water test and showing required parking.

cases.name: 4 Alpine Drive - utility burial waiver request
cases.applicant: Dave Cicarni

timeline.summary: The applicant sought relief from Town Code 355-17 requiring new utility service to be placed underground, wanting instead to run overhead wires from a pole he had already erected across the street; despite sympathy for his practical and cost arguments, the board found no basis (no hardship, no precedent) to waive the statute and the town engineer remained firm that the service must go underground.

cases.name: 200 Business Park Drive - outdoor storage of construction trailers
cases.applicant: PTSD Northeast

timeline.summary: With the applicant absent, the board discussed a request by a healthcare-construction firm to store 40-yard containers/trailers behind a professional office building; citing extensive prior outdoor-storage concerns in that area, members were strongly disinclined to allow containers and suggested the applicant instead propose an enclosed structure meeting setbacks, parking, and FAR.

cases.name: 2 Massaro Court lot line change
cases.applicant: represented by Nick Lishari, Hudson Engineering

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a previously approved lot line change (no new lots) whose approvals had twice expired; the board held the hearing with no public present and re-approved it a third time, passing the negative declaration, preliminary and final subdivision plat resolutions so the plat can be signed and two-family houses built.

cases.name: Shapiro residence sport courts, 8 Rolling Drive
cases.applicant: represented by Cory Salomon (Zarin & Steinman), Paul Sci-Sack (JMC), architect Matt Barenz, lighting expert Steven Ballow

timeline.summary: Continued discussion of proposed tennis, padel and turf sport courts plus an activity building on a 17+ acre property, with ARB, conservation and zoning board sign-offs in hand. The central issue was court lighting; the applicant's lighting expert described dark-sky, house-side-shielded fixtures with no light trespass past 50 feet, and the board asked for a method to verify performance after installation before setting a public hearing next month.

cases.name: 215 Business Park Drive extension (former CarQuest warehouse)

timeline.summary: The board granted a routine one-year extension of time for a previously approved ~45,000 sq ft warehouse/office addition (original 2017 approval), noting the approval has now been extended for roughly six years and that new DEC stormwater work will be required.

cases.name: Airport campus project extensions
cases.applicant: represented by Max Millie (Cuddy & Feder)

timeline.summary: The board granted a standard 90-day subdivision extension and a one-year site plan approval extension for the airport campus project while staff finishes reviewing the filed subdivision and site plans for signature.

cases.name: Mail-truck parking application (industrial district)
cases.applicant: owner of multiple town properties (currently 176 Virginia)

timeline.summary: The applicant, who bought an industrial-district office/warehouse, wants to park mail trucks in the rear and reconfigure parking; the board referred the application to the ZBA (for the truck turning-radius variance and cars backing onto the street) and directed a concurrent town board track, with a planning board hearing to follow.

cases.name: Oamic Ingredients amended site plan, 6 Leviola Court
cases.applicant: Oamic Ingredients (Nella Morad)

timeline.summary: The board held and closed the public hearing on an amended site plan renewing/finalizing a previously approved 2022 resolution for a flavor-and-fragrance chemical warehouse and distribution use; after confirming no changes to approved chemicals or quantities, it adopted a negative declaration and the resolution.

cases.name: Bracemont estate, 8 Roseann Drive
cases.applicant: Property owner (represented by Zarin & Steinmetz / Paul, Ira Granberg, Stephen Ballow lighting expert)

timeline.summary: Continued public hearing on a site plan with special use, tree removal and wetlands permits for an activity building, tennis and padel courts with fencing and lighting, and an accessory apartment; the board was largely unsupportive of the court lighting, heard strong neighbor objections about noise and light, and kept the public hearing open pending more landscaping and cleanup of the resolution.

cases.name: Autobody shop solar and rear addition, 28 Lock
cases.applicant: Autobody shop owner

timeline.summary: The board referred the applicant to the Zoning Board of Appeals for use-setback variances, since existing repair bays sit nearer than the 25-foot minimum to a residential lot line; a rooftop solar amendment and a three-bay rear addition would return to the planning board afterward, with a possible spray-booth permit condition.

cases.name: Sankar residence, 26 Carillon Place
cases.applicant: Sankar

timeline.summary: Public hearing on legalizing unpermitted fill, tree removal and deck construction, plus relocating the pool and adding a cabana closer to the house; the board closed the public hearing but declined to adopt the resolution until outstanding conditions (C&D removal plan, stormwater, erosion control) are satisfied.

cases.name: 167 Miamis River Road (Miamis River Gorge headquarters)
cases.applicant: Miamis River Gorge (rep. Ralph Mastromonaco)

timeline.summary: Site plan to give the Gorge organization more operating space with modest parking improvements and a generator on a scenic road; the board referred front/rear yard setback variances to the ZBA, with a special-use permit for the residence/offices to be handled at the Town Board.

cases.name: One Stillwater Place restoration (wetland violation)
cases.applicant: Property owner (both sides represented)

timeline.summary: Review of a wetland-disturbance violation affecting both the applicant's property and an adjacent (Nannis/Manus) property; submitted plans only show impacts on the neighbor's parcel, so the board is awaiting revised plans and a mitigation plan for the applicant's own property before referring the matter to the Conservation Board.

cases.name: Shapiro residence, 8 Rocking Horse Road
cases.applicant: Shapiro

timeline.summary: The public hearing was reopened and closed; the board adopted the resolution as amended, approving the site with wetland mitigation plantings but explicitly declining to approve the tennis/sport court lighting as disruptive to neighbors, and refined conditions on SWPPP permit number, planting installation before CO, and five-year maintenance.

cases.name: Gasson special use permit (additional horses)
cases.applicant: Gasson

timeline.summary: With no applicant present, the board kept the special use permit for additional horses in front of it after the building inspector's site visit found numerous code items; the applicant must bring the property back into compliance before the board would recommend approval to the town board.

cases.name: Westchester County Airport residential development presentation (Nick Hartman)
cases.applicant: Nick Hartman, Chair, Westchester County Airport Advisory Board

timeline.summary: Guest Nick Hartman presented a draft report on the environmental and safety risks of dense residential development near the airport; the board discussed the tension between the county's opposition to such development and the local housing shortage, noting most of the affected land is in Rye Brook while Arrowwood-area development is nearby.

cases.name: Goldman pool within wetland buffer
cases.applicant: Goldman (property owner)

timeline.summary: Discussion of a pool located entirely within a wetland buffer around a piped water course; the applicant reported receiving a conservation-board permit and completing mitigation planting. The board wants the conservation-board memo (not yet received/distributed) before proceeding, and directed the applicant to notice and hold a public hearing, likely with a resolution ready at that meeting.

cases.name: Sauro residence remodel with accessory apartment, 8 Lions Road
cases.applicant: Steven Sauro (planning-board member, recused), engineer Ralph presenting

timeline.summary: Remodel of an existing four-bedroom home to add an accessory apartment above the garage (five bedrooms total on an existing five-bedroom septic, ~two acres), which requires a special use permit. No wetlands or steep slopes; main hurdle is Board of Health well/septic no-objection approval, with stormwater subsurface infiltration and some front-lot tree removal near the septic. Next step is ARB approval, then a public hearing.

cases.name: 75 Hickory Kingdom Road - request to retain original curb cut
cases.applicant: Applicant not named (represented via staff)

timeline.summary: The applicant, having built a new curb cut and driveway (approved through the RPRC and Conservation Board because it crossed a wetland buffer to fix unsafe sight lines), now asked to keep the original unsafe curb cut for emergency use. The board reached a consensus against allowing it, noting the new driveway was justified only by the old one's unsafety, but a public hearing/neighbor notification is required before a formal denial. A board member recused himself citing a relationship with the applicant.

cases.name: Overhead vs. underground electric service policy (4 Alpine / 21 Wood Wool Road)
cases.applicant: N/A (policy discussion; 4 Alpine applicant to be brought back)

timeline.summary: General discussion clarifying town code on electric service in areas of existing overhead lines: burying service to the house is required, but a single utility pole at the property line for overhead service is discretionary, not mandatory. A board member acknowledged his prior stricter interpretation was incorrect; the board decided to put 4 Alpine back on the agenda and have the applicant return rather than amend the application on its own.

cases.name: Sauro residence addition, pool and accessory apartment (8 Clients Road)
cases.applicant: Steven Sauro (owner; represented by engineer Ralph and Jennifer)

timeline.summary: Public hearing on a house addition, pool and accessory apartment over the garage; the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution as amended, conditioned on Board of Health approval and moving the water biological analysis to before CO.

cases.name: Alpine Drive residence - utility service relief
cases.applicant: Dave (homeowner building a new house on Alpine Drive)

timeline.summary: The applicant returned seeking relief from a prior condition requiring underground utility service, showing that essentially every comparable home in the neighborhood has overhead service; the board reconsidered its earlier determination and voted to allow the overhead wire across the street to a proposed pole with underground service from that pole to the house.

The board revisited a draft resolution for Four Ledgewood, originally approved in 2023 but lapsed amid health-department and other issues and recently re-approved. The applicant had returned with a tightened resolution that let the board remove a number of prior conditions. The chair expressed reservations about the underlying concept ('I'm not sure I love it') but the board approved the draft resolution.

cases.name: 76 Fireman's Road
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch, LP Engineering (addition to existing three-bedroom house)

timeline.summary: The engineer updated the board on a ~941 sq ft addition to an existing three-bedroom house that requires wetland review. The project cleared the Conservation Board on June 24 with a satisfactory mitigation plan, a joint DEC permit application was filed, and DEC was set to verify the wetland boundary that Friday. The county health department will issue its 'no objection' for the existing septic only after DEC acts. With stormwater testing and a sight-line analysis still outstanding, the board agreed the plan looks good and set a public hearing for the next meeting (two weeks out). Conservation liaison Vincent DeAnno stressed that mitigation conditions (contingency plan, five-year buffer plan, cost estimate, and full mapping of invasive species) must be locked in and not slip through the cracks.

cases.name: 11 New Kings Street (Park Place)
cases.address: 11 New Kings Street, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: 11 New Kings Street; attorney William Noll (Cuddy & Feder)

timeline.summary: Applicant requested a two-year extension of site plan approval for the Park Place automated parking structure near the airport, the eighth such extension. Counsel reported building permit review is underway with construction plans filed and no changes to design or circumstances. Carthy asked whether it would return again or be built; counsel expected it well underway within two years. The board granted the extension.

cases.name: 135 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)

timeline.summary: Request for a site plan waiver for a change of use in a ~23,000 sq ft office building, converting 3,000 sq ft from general office to dental office. Corey noted parking requirements are lower for the new use, so demand actually decreases. Carthy asked planner Adam Kaufman if he had concerns and he had none. The board granted the waiver.

cases.name: 124 Old Mianus Road
cases.address: 124 Old Mianus Road, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)

timeline.summary: Extension of time request. Corey reported additional comments received from the town engineer's office and the health department are being addressed, expecting to turn them around within about a week and a half. Carthy noted one item to review with planner Adam Kaufman offline. The board granted the extension.

cases.name: 18 Bedford-Banksville Road (propane exchange)
cases.applicant: Retail propane-sales operator (outdoor propane exchange cage)

timeline.summary: The board reviewed a special use permit for selling propane in an outdoor cage, which had gone to the town board and was awaiting the Planning Board's recommendation. Discussion focused on the fire department's questions about propane tank size and code compliance (to be handled by the building department under NYS building/fire code) and the fact that the submitted plan was a hand-drawn sketch lacking bollards. The board moved to recommend the town board proceed with the special use permit, subject to installation of bollards (or equivalent protective planters) and whatever else the building department and fire code require.

An administrative change-of-use on the second floor with adequate existing parking. Staff had determined the applicant did not need to formally appear, and the board treated it as a routine site-plan waiver. The board adopted the resolution with no substantive concerns.

cases.name: 1/11 Round Hill (driveway field change)
cases.applicant: (existing subdivision lot)

timeline.summary: The town engineer presented a minor field change shifting a driveway slightly back into the site to create a high point at elevation 90 and better tie in a bridge, with no additional disturbance and remaining within the easement. The Board opened and approved the field change by motion.

cases.name: 10 & 20 Round Hill Way
cases.address: 10 & 20 Round Hill Way, North Castle, NY

timeline.summary: The board opened and closed a public hearing on the 10 and 20 Round Hill Way site plans, steep slope permits and tree removal permits, then adopted draft resolutions for each lot. This was essentially a re-approval: the applications had been approved before as part of a subdivision and two site plans, but due to a miscommunication the site-plan resolutions expired and the plans were never signed, so they had to be re-submitted with prior field changes incorporated. A board member questioned how Lot 5 gets access, confirming a common driveway serves the lots off Round Hill via an easement reflected in the resolution. The board was satisfied and adopted both resolutions.

The board reviewed a straightforward change to the access configuration for the existing house within the Orchard Hill five-lot subdivision, where the current lot is bifurcated by a driveway serving a back lot. Two of the new houses have been added and two rear lots remain to come before the board. The item will proceed to a public hearing with neighbor notification by first-class mail and proof of mailing. A member cautioned that because the house is shifting slightly, the 250-foot neighbor notification list should be regenerated rather than reusing old labels.

cases.name: Single-family residence & pool (Angela) - cut/fill grading
cases.applicant: Angela (owner-applicant); engineer not present
cases.lastStatus: discussion only (direction given to respond to memos and schedule a public hearing)

trajectory.status: discussion only (direction given to respond to memos and schedule a public hearing)

timeline.status: discussion only (direction given to respond to memos and schedule a public hearing)
timeline.summary: A working discussion on a hillside single-family home with a pool, garage, and retaining walls where the applicant had already reduced imported fill and wall heights and relocated the pool per prior board feedback. New wetland flagging in the rear was coordinated between the applicant's wetlands engineer and the town's consultant (Dave). The planner questioned whether setting the first floor at 473 (vs. ~470.5 garage) could be lowered to reduce cut/fill and wall grading; the board directed the applicant's professionals to answer the planner's and town engineer's memos and then set a public hearing.

cases.name: 62 Nethermont Avenue
cases.address: 62 Nethermont Avenue, North White Plains, NY
cases.applicant: Owners Lindsay & Dmitry (architect Rocco Delano; applicant's father Jim New sold them the lot)

timeline.summary: The applicant proposed a new ~4,865 sq ft single-family residence, positioned six feet off the south side line to preserve a future subdividable building lot. Neighbors raised concerns about rock excavation/hammering near a ~100-year-old adjoining home, house size/neighborhood character, and tree removal, while other neighbors and the applicant's father spoke strongly in support. The board debated at length whether to require protection beyond the standard chipping permit given the hammering's proximity to the neighbor. It ultimately closed the hearing and granted the resolution as amended, adding conditions that a seismic monitor be placed on the neighbor's (Pinella/'Davis') foundation and that the applicant pre-drill (line drilling) to reduce vibration.

cases.name: 850 North Broadway
cases.applicant: Property owner (not present)

timeline.summary: Work was done on the back of the building without a permit and now needs to be legalized, along with several site plan issues. With the applicant absent, the planner explained that a basic site plan (addressing refuse, parking, lighting, and safety requirements, similar to the 4 KSL Court approach) will be needed before the board can approve a site plan. No action taken.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Road
cases.applicant: Ralph (project engineer) for a new single-family residence

timeline.summary: Application for a new single-family residence on a 2.5-acre vacant lot within an approved subdivision, connecting to sewer with a proposed well and front/rear stormwater mitigation. The board opened the public hearing but Carthy noted the landscape plan was missing from the package and declined to close the hearing. A neighbor at 6 Hollow Place had submitted a letter raising tree-removal and screening concerns. The hearing was adjourned to a future meeting, to be reopened once the landscape plan is submitted and ARB approval is obtained.

cases.name: 3 Israel Townsend Hill (32 Orchard Drive subdivision)
cases.address: 3 Israel Townsend Hill, North Castle, NY
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello, Federal Engineering, for the property owner

timeline.summary: Site improvements for an existing single-family dwelling that will remain, including a new driveway, septic system, and well replacing former systems; 17 trees proposed for removal consistent with the prior subdivision approval. cases.name: EV Charging Local Law (Level 3) Referral
cases.applicant: Town Board (referral of a proposed local law)

timeline.summary: A town-board referral on a proposed local law to permit currently-prohibited Level 3 EV charging, with an open question of whether Level 3 spaces should count toward off-street parking (a draft cap of no more than 20%). Carthy argued the board should encourage the town to reduce barriers and count the charging spaces within the parking requirement rather than requiring them in excess. Steven Sauro repeatedly cautioned about unintended consequences, including the town becoming a highway 'road stop' and businesses using chargers as a profit loophole. After an extended debate, the board declined to add a substantive recommendation and voted to send the referral back to the town board as written.

cases.name: Short-Term Rental Law (town board referral)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Board)
cases.lastStatus: reviewed and returned to Town Board without formal comment

trajectory.status: reviewed and returned to Town Board without formal comment

timeline.status: reviewed and returned to Town Board without formal comment
timeline.summary: The Town Board referred its proposed short-term-rental law (a zoning-chapter amendment) to the Planning Board for input. The board discussed the framework at length: primary-residence requirement, the 30-day threshold, operating permits and building-department inspections, occupancy tax, quiet hours, and the provision barring a short-term rental on the same lot as an accessory dwelling unit (ADU). Views split on whether the law is too cumbersome (risking noncompliance) versus appropriately detailed for enforceability, but there was broad agreement its practical effect is to discourage short-term rentals. The board reached consensus to send it back to the Town Board with no substantive comment.

cases.name: 6 Massaro Court (formerly 54 Curtis)
cases.applicant: Michael Stein, Hudson Engineering
cases.lastStatus: public hearing closed; approved with conditions (as amended)

trajectory.status: public hearing closed; approved with conditions (as amended)

timeline.status: public hearing closed; approved with conditions (as amended)
timeline.summary: This was the final lot of a three-lot subdivision (two prior lots approved in January), seeking site plan and steep-slope approval to build a two-family dwelling with retaining walls, substantial grading, and a comprehensive stormwater system. Discussion focused on a condition (condition 6) requiring the grading plan be revised to eliminate a seven-foot exposed basement to the town engineer's satisfaction, and on a retaining wall shown 'by others' sitting on the property line. Michael Pollack, citing a similar issue in his own professional practice, suggested making explicit that maintenance of the wall is this property owner's obligation to avoid future disputes. The board closed the public hearing (no public spoke) and granted the resolution as amended per Pollack's suggestion.

Adam Kaufman opened a policy discussion on how the board handles extensions of time. The board agreed to place extensions at the top of future meetings so professionals can dispatch them quickly, while a participating professional argued the published agenda order should not bind the chair (comparing it to a courtroom). Adam also proposed adding whereas clauses to extension resolutions stating whether another board (e.g., the ZBA) had a required approval and its status, so lapses are clearly documented. The board and staff endorsed the changes.

meetings.meetingSummary: A long, full-agenda North Castle Planning Board meeting held by Zoom covering eight items: a new single-family home site plan at One Gion Lane (approved with conditions), a tree-removal/landscaping permit at 100 Hunter Drive (approved), an amended site plan/wetlands legalization at One Kent Place (approved), and several early-stage matters referred or held for further work: Buff's Flower Garden nursery special-permit amendment, a warehouse expansion at 7 New King Street, a parking-variance interpretation at 428-436 Main Street, a scenic-road house renovation with pool at 20 Manus River Road, and the Summit Club (former Brentwood Country Club) residential-component site plan. Recurring board themes were process/quality-control of draft resolutions, screening and deer-resistant plantings, wetlands/stormwater, parking, and special-permit/zoning questions.

cases.name: One Gion Lane - new single-family home

cases.summary: Neighbor-notification meeting on a proposed ~3,800 sf home (5,900 sf including garage/decks) on a constrained R2A lot; neighbors raised driveway headlights, privacy, screening and stormwater concerns. After a long board debate about the large number of open items on the draft resolution and how much should be delegated administratively, the board closed the notification meeting and approved the resolution as amended, requiring a more deer-resistant screening plan in place of arborvitae.

Emailed neighbors (Castellucci, others) asked about visibility from Gene Curry, stormwater runoff, erosion and wetlands; staff said runoff is directed away and there are no wetland impacts.
