cases.name: 100 Hunter Drive - tree removal and landscaping
cases.applicant: Dean Pushcar (landscape designer) for owner
cases.summary: Neighbor-notification hearing on removal of 18 (net ~15 on-property) mostly poor-condition trees on a former estate lot in the R1A district, with a robust replacement plan of ~47 trees including green giant arborvitae, white spruce and shade trees. Chairman Carthy recused himself and Michael Pollack presided. A neighbor sought maximum privacy screening. The board found the plan much improved, closed the notification portion and adopted the resolution as amended (excluding right-of-way trees).
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Mr. Sawney, across the street, expressed reservations about the earlier variance process and asked that the maximum possible screening be provided to restore privacy, noting the new house towers over existing trees.

memberPositions.stance: Presided; supportive, noted plan substantially improved and screening addresses concerns
memberPositions.evidence: As acting chair he ran the hearing, noted the site is bare and the plan fills in the borders, and moved it toward approval.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; saw a systematic criteria for removals and a real step forward for privacy
memberPositions.evidence: Noted removed trees are designated poor/thin/invasive and the ~47 replacements create privacy and screening for the new home.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; applicant did an extensive job mitigating neighbor concerns
memberPositions.evidence: Said the applicant has done an extensive job trying to mitigate all the concerns of the neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; agreed the planting layout is extensive
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed with Steve's comment and called it a pretty extensive planting layout, then made the motion to adopt.

cases.name: One Kent Place - Maury (legalization of sheds/coolers/patios)
cases.applicant: Andrew Nester, JMC (for One Kent Place Inc.)
cases.summary: Public hearing on an amended site plan and wetlands permit to legalize work (new sheds, coolers, patios) done without prior approval in the CB district; variances were already obtained from the ZBA and the applicant had appeared before the conservation board and ARB. No public comment. The board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution, with a portion of patio/wall over the property line and part of a shed to be removed.

memberPositions.stance: Sought clarification on the encroachment areas being removed
memberPositions.evidence: Asked about the pink and gray shaded areas; applicant explained the gray patio/wall over the line and part of a shed will be removed.

memberPositions.stance: Presided; moved to close the hearing and adopt the resolution
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motions to open, close, and adopt the resolution after confirming JMC had no issues.

cases.name: Buff's Flower Garden - nursery special permit amendment
cases.applicant: P. Daniel Hollis (attorney) and Joseph Rina (engineer) for the property owner
cases.summary: Applicant sought amendment of a 1980 special permit for a nursery operation, adding a small retail farm stand, a rebuilt family residence, two horses/barn, expanded garage with offices, and planting areas, with the matter to be referred back to the town board as lead agency. The board discussed conflicts with the old permit (planting near wetlands/wells, building heights, retail prohibition) and traffic-safety concerns at the entrance, and agreed to schedule a joint work session with the conservation board rather than act tonight.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Jeffrey Brown, who lives across the street and knows the family, spoke to say his attendance should not be seen as negative; asked about wholesale truck deliveries and how public comment would proceed.

memberPositions.stance: Cautiously open but wants operational detail, safety and a work session before recommending
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board needs to report operational aspects to the town board and proposed a work session with the conservation board to work it out.

memberPositions.stance: No objection to a small, reasonable retail area if the Banksville Road turning issue is solved
memberPositions.evidence: Said off the top of his head he has no objection to a small reasonable retail area provided the turn-in/turn-out onto Banksville Road is satisfied.

memberPositions.stance: Concerned about activity and chemicals in the wetland buffer
memberPositions.evidence: Said he doesn't take DEC's stance as a blank check and wants to understand what chemicals go into the wetland-buffer planting areas.

cases.name: 7 New King Street - warehouse expansion (Lord/Santamaria)
cases.applicant: P. Daniel Hollis (attorney) and Joe Rina (engineer) for the Santamaria/Lord company
cases.summary: Applicant proposed squaring off and adding ~6,000 sf to an existing warehouse (former hunt/rod-and-gun club) used to store maintenance materials for the owner's real-estate portfolio, on a PFOA-affected, bottled-water property. Discussion centered on whether warehouse is a permitted use in the IND-AA district; the board and staff agreed the cleanest path is a petition to the town board to make warehouse a permitted use rather than chase a nonconforming-use argument. Staff also flagged parking counts, wetland-buffer disturbance and a drainage easement to be eliminated.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; thinks it silly the applicant must argue the use and wants the zoning cleaned up
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board should straighten out the IND-AA district to include warehouse use and that having to consider it is a little silly.

memberPositions.stance: Pragmatic; asked why not simply make it a permitted use and let the board handle site plan later
memberPositions.evidence: Asked why they have to match warehouse criteria rather than just make it a permitted use and deal with site plan in the future.

cases.name: 428-436 Main Street - parking variance interpretation
cases.applicant: P. Daniel Hollis (attorney) for the property owner
cases.summary: Discussion of whether a 1996 ZBA parking variance for this pre-existing nonconforming mixed-use building was a blanket approval covering any future use. Counsel Baroni and staff disagreed with the blanket reading, advising the applicant either to return to the ZBA for any additional variance or to show that the currently proposed all-retail mix is no more intense than the 1996 uses (supported by a 1996 appraisal). The board agreed the appraisal plus resolution gives a benchmark to move forward.

memberPositions.stance: Facilitated a path forward using the 1996 appraisal as a benchmark for the use mix
memberPositions.evidence: Concluded the board has something to work with and a benchmark, and directed the applicant to submit a use schedule then and now.

cases.name: 20 Manus River Road - house renovation, pool and cabana
cases.applicant: John Needham (owner) with Pete Gregory (engineer)
cases.summary: Applicant presented a renovation within the existing (slightly reduced) footprint of a 1972 four-bedroom house on a scenic road, adding a 12x20 pool and a 276 sf cabana clear of wetlands, wetland buffer and steep slopes, plus relocating overhead electric underground. The board discussed the retaining wall, pool siting (rear vs side yard), and treated the utility work as a minor administrative wetlands permit; next steps are ARB review then a public hearing with a draft resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Clarified scenic-road trigger and low visibility; broadly comfortable
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the application is before the board because of the scenic road corridor and that the house is set 300+ feet back and not very visible.

memberPositions.stance: Satisfied the pool is effectively in the rear yard with no negative scenic-road impact
memberPositions.evidence: Distinguished this from a prior side-yard-pool problem and confirmed the pool won't negatively impact the scenic road.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; advised evaluating the retaining wall's structural integrity now
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested having a structural engineer look at the back wall while the work is being done, in the owner's best interest.

cases.name: Summit Club (former Brentwood Country Club) - residential component
cases.applicant: Mark Winegarten (attorney), Jeff Mandel (principal), Ken Anderson (architect), Paul Sisak (JMC engineer) for Summit Club Partners LLC
cases.summary: Applicant updated the board on the 73-unit residential component (7 AFFH units), reporting they eliminated the seventh building and its roadway and folded the AFFH units into the six existing buildings, consolidated amenities into a single relocated clubhouse (with a subdivision-line shift), and detailed guest golf cottages, on-site water district and sewage plans. Debate focused on overflow accessory parking within the buffer (which the applicant argued is code-permitted and offered to land-bank), screening adequacy, traffic on Route 22, and finalizing the water plan; the residential component is progressing toward a public hearing once the water plan is firmed up.

memberPositions.stance: Fairly satisfied with the residential layout; wants water and AFFH resolved before hearing
memberPositions.evidence: Said he's fairly satisfied with the building layout and roads and framed getting the water plan finalized before opening the public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious; flagged the 685-page late submission and pressed on traffic study and well interference
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the materials came Friday night, and asked whether traffic on Route 22 and neighboring-well interference were studied (EIS confirmed).

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of overflow parking; earlier worried residential lots have too few spaces
memberPositions.evidence: Recalled his prior concern that six or seven spaces per building isn't enough and said the overflow parking could be properly screened.

memberPositions.stance: Probed clubhouse relocation, curb-cut access to the accessory lot, and cottage counts
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the amenities building was eliminated/clubhouse relocated and confirmed the accessory lot has no separate curb cut.

themes.note: Screening plans and deer-resistant plantings dominated the Gion Lane and Hunter Drive items.
Parking counts, overflow lots in buffers, and the 428 Main variance recurred across multiple items.
Buffer disturbance, DEC oversight and chemicals in planting areas raised on Buff's, 7 New King, Manus River and Summit Club.
Nursery special-permit criteria and the warehouse permitted-use text amendment were central.
Extended debate over too many open items and how much should be handled administratively vs by the board.
Neighbors at Gion Lane and Hunter Drive worried about proximity, headlights and lost privacy.
Infiltration/dissipation and erosion control discussed on Gion Lane and Manus River.
Summit Club water district and PFOA-driven bottled-water issue at 7 New King.
Summit Club folded its seven AFFH units into the six existing buildings, resolving a prior concern.

meetings.meetingSummary: A special (non-public) work session with two applicants. First, the Manelbaum family and PODS walked the board through the storage operation and two loading/unloading layouts for a proposed PODS facility at 94 Business Park, addressing board and adjoining-neighbor concerns about noise, forklift back-up alarms, diesel exhaust, screening and visible pods; the board felt progress was made and asked for an interior staging/capacity plan. Second, the Summer Club golf-course-community residential development on Route 22 discussed outstanding water, sewer, affordable-housing (AFFH), phasing and recreation-fee issues, with the board pressing the applicant to reconcile the town water/sewer director's comments before approval and declining to close the public hearing anytime soon.

cases.name: PODS storage facility - 94 Business Park
cases.applicant: Manelbaum family / PODS
cases.summary: Work session in which the applicant's team and a PODS representative explained the operation and proposed two options (pass-through loading on the far south side vs. rear loading with a sound wall) to keep noise and loading away from the adjacent assisted-living facility. The board asked for a schematic showing interior staging and capacity and felt the meeting made progress.
cases.publicComment: Two adjoining neighbors spoke: Michael (assisted-living owner) said he was quite satisfied, felt a sound wall was unnecessary, and suggested plantings to screen the side loading; Aaron (original park developer) objected to loading appearing on the south side facing Business Park Drive and worried empty pods parked overnight would be visible, noting other neighbors also have concerns.

memberPositions.stance: Constructive; wants interior staging demonstrated before moving forward
memberPositions.evidence: Framed the outstanding issues as outdoor storage and loading/unloading and repeatedly asked the applicant to provide a schematic showing the interior staging area, straight drive aisles and building capacity so pods aren't unloaded outside.

memberPositions.stance: Wants to understand sound propagation and guaranteed interior staging
memberPositions.evidence: Asked to hear how sound would carry the length of the building before deciding whether a sound wall was worth exploring, and confirmed the interior-staging requirement was understood 'loud and clear.'

cases.name: Summer Club golf-course-community residential development (Route 22)
cases.applicant: Summer Club (golf-course community; represented by attorney Janet and engineers JMC/WSP)
cases.summary: Work session on the residential component (6 buildings, ~73 units plus amenities) of a golf-course-community floating zone. The board and town staff catalogued outstanding items - water system design, wastewater/SCADA, conservation easement, AFFH units and phasing, over-55 restriction, recreation fees, and a newly added golf maintenance building - and pressed the applicant to reconcile the town water/sewer director's comments before approval. The board made clear the public hearing (continuing Nov 14) would not close soon.

memberPositions.stance: Wants minimal conditions but key technical issues resolved before approval
memberPositions.evidence: Pushed to group conditions and get the applicant and town water/sewer director 'on the same page,' stressed that Sal's approval must precede (not be a condition of) approval, and repeatedly raised the need to tie the golf amenities to the residential build so the zoning doesn't fail.

memberPositions.stance: Insists the water/sewer items be substantially resolved before approval
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'we've got to get them, especially on the water stuff... we've got to get the bulk of these,' and argued that splitting the residential from the golf club compromises the town's position and that a baseline must be agreed.

themes.note: Town director Sal raised serious unaddressed comments (fire lines, dead-end main, SCADA/mag meters); applicant had not revised plans, a key blocker.
Two site layouts, forklift back-up alarms, sound wall and diesel exhaust discussed; board and adjacent neighbor generally receptive.
Applicant wanted many items as conditions to close the hearing fast; board wanted a shorter condition list and issues resolved up front.
Board worried that building condos before the golf clubhouse/amenities could cause the golf-course-community zoning to fail; needs a mechanism to guarantee amenities.
Concern that pods not be stored/staged or parked outside where visible; plantings proposed for the south side.
Agreement in principle exists via recorded covenant but exact unit locations and phase treatment still need to be shown on plans.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (Carthy chairing, with Jensen and Sauro present, Ruisi on Zoom, Pollack absent) approved the Feb 12 minutes and worked through a long agenda of subdivisions, site plans and wetland permits. Public hearings were held on the 32 Orchard Drive 5-lot subdivision (held open, hydrogeologist to be engaged), the 14 Tall Woods Road pool/wetland permit (approved), the contentious 23 Bedford Banksville Road office/storage site plan with the self-storage building now removed (held open amid heavy neighbor opposition), and the 40 High Street two-lot subdivision (approved with a negative declaration). The board also took up discussion items including the Airport Campus townhouse project nearing final approval, new-home site plans at 4 Armonk Heights and 99 Byram Ridge, wetland/golf-path work at 92 & 94 Round Hill, a mixed-use renovation at 12 Bedford Road, a special-use-permit amendment for the 448 Bedford Road nursery school, and granted several extensions of time.

cases.name: 32 Orchard Drive subdivision
cases.applicant: Whitney Singleton (Singleton, Davis & Singleton), on behalf of applicant
cases.summary: Public hearing on a five-lot (four new) subdivision of a ~13-acre R-1A parcel; extensive neighbor concern about steep slopes, stormwater, septic and well/aquifer impacts led the board to keep the hearing open, engage the town's hydrogeologist, and keep the lots under Planning Board (not RPRC) jurisdiction so each future house gets a public hearing.
cases.publicComment: Multiple neighbors (Mr. Mark of 5 Eden Hunt Place, Dan Kahn, Tom Lanahan for 33 Orchard, Jeff Scott of 21 Orchard, and former board member Michael of 14 Orchard) opposed or questioned the project, citing steep-slope development, water runoff and erosion, septic vs. tying into the nearby Orchard sewer line, well/aquifer drawdown, and lack of early notice; several urged the board to 'pump the brakes.'

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of the process but responsive to neighbors; kept hearing open and added safeguards
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed keeping the subdivision under Planning Board jurisdiction, agreed to engage a hydrogeologist, and said 'we're going to pump the brakes' and keep the public hearing open.

cases.name: 14 Tall Woods Road in-ground pool and wetland permit
cases.applicant: Peter Gregory (DTS Providence), engineer; Seth (mitigation plantings)
cases.summary: Continued public hearing on an in-ground swimming pool with stormwater mitigation and a pool draw-down/irrigation storage system in an R-2A wetland-buffer area; after discussion of a rain garden, roof-runoff rerouting and relocating pool equipment indoors, the board closed the hearing and adopted the draft resolution.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke on this application.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; suggested moving the pool further from the house but moved to close and approve
memberPositions.evidence: Noted he did the site walk, asked whether the pool could move further from the house, then made the motion to close the hearing and adopt the resolution.

cases.name: 23 Bedford Banksville Road site plan and wetland permit (self-storage removed)
cases.applicant: Tony Vinciano (Vinciano), attorney; Peter Gregory, engineer
cases.summary: Public hearing on a site plan for occupancy of an existing ~15,500 sq ft multi-tenant office/storage building plus removal of the existing contractors' yard, with the previously proposed self-storage building now withdrawn from this application; the board declined to vote, citing possibly non-permitted storage/woodworking-metalworks uses and requiring a building-inspector opinion, and kept the hearing open.
cases.publicComment: Strong neighbor opposition: Peter Noora (6 Conyers/Calgary Park Drive), George (petition organizer), Richard Ferguson (17 Hobby Farm Lane), and Lauren Pinkis (Conyers Farm) argued the building has no community value, plans are incomplete (no lighting plan, 21+ open items), Banksville is not an industrial park, and urged the board not to approve anything and to require a full environmental review of the whole project.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical; unwilling to approve while building uses may be illegal, wants building-inspector input
memberPositions.evidence: Asked 'are the uses in the building kosher for the district?' and got 'hung up' on approving a site plan with questionable existing uses, directing the applicant to meet the building inspector and return.

memberPositions.stance: Pragmatic/market-driven; agreed with counsel's caution but framed it as an enforcement issue and defended market forces
memberPositions.evidence: Said he tends to agree with counsel Roland but flagged it as an enforcement issue, and argued 'you have to understand the market... the town people want what the market will bear'; a public speaker addressed him as 'Stephen.'

cases.name: 40 High Street two-lot subdivision
cases.applicant: Corey Salman (Zarin & Steinmetz), attorney; Peter Gregory, engineer
cases.summary: Public hearing on a two-lot subdivision of a ~5.8-acre R-1A parcel (lots of 1.25 and 4.59 acres); after confirming the frontage area is a drainage ditch rather than regulated wetland and reviewing stormwater and septic, the board closed the hearing, adopted a negative declaration, and approved the preliminary and final subdivision plats as amended, with a note added that future homes return to the Planning Board.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors Dan Benincasa (5 Canado) and Danielle Gamar (44 High Street, shares the driveway) raised concerns about house/septic placement, wetlands they believed protected the area, and well/aquifer impacts after a prior dry well; the board explained the site-specific analysis found the front area to be a non-regulated drainage channel.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; disclosed a business relationship with the owner but did not recuse, moved approvals
memberPositions.evidence: Disclosed his business relationship with the property owner (cleared with town attorney), then moved to approve the preliminary and final subdivision plats as amended.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved the negative declaration
memberPositions.evidence: Carthy said 'Steve, you want to take it from here?' and Steve responded 'I'll move that we adopt a neg declaration.'

memberPositions.stance: Constructive/supportive; proposed the plan-note condition and flagged duplicative resolution items
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested adding a note on the plan requiring future homes to return to the board ('That's a good idea, Jim') and noted conditions 18-20 were duplicative of 15-17.

cases.name: Airport Campus (113 King Street) townhouse development
cases.applicant: Airport Campus (applicant represented by counsel; planner Adam preparing resolutions)
cases.summary: Wrap-up discussion of a multifamily townhouse project with a clubhouse; the board reviewed draft findings statement and site plan/subdivision resolutions, resolved engineering/water-sewer conditions, discussed adding first-floor-bedroom and 45 dBA noise conditions, and flagged a school-bus routing/sight-line concern on Cooney Hill Road, aiming for final action on the 11th pending ARB approval.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of moving to final approval but wants the school-bus sight-line issue resolved
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed for a conversation with Byram Hills about the bus's right-turn exit and sight lines on Cooney Hill Road and asked to attend it, while agreeing the project is in good shape for the 11th.

cases.name: 4 Armonk Heights Road new single-family home
cases.address: 4 Armonk Heights Road (corner of Fairway and Armonk Heights Road)
cases.applicant: Angela Gavino (owner/developer)
cases.summary: Early site-plan review of a proposed ~7,000 sq ft home (with a barn removed from the plan after wetlands-consultant concerns); the board asked the applicant to reduce disturbance, consider tiered grading on steep slopes, stake out the house, and set up a Planning Board and Conservation Board site walk.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Jennifer Nippo (32 Fairway, immediately downslope) opposed the size and hillside location of the home and described past stormwater flooding of her basement, urging a different location; the applicant said she would pipe and spread the town drainage to help mitigate the neighbor's water problem.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious/neutral; wants a site walk, staking and Conservation Board referral before proceeding
memberPositions.evidence: Said he drove by, told the applicant to stake out the house and driveway and coordinate a site walk, and to address staff memos and the Conservation Board.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road wetland permits (golf holes / access paths)
cases.applicant: Jerry Tortarella (Hocherman Tortorella & Wexler), attorney; Tim Allen (Bibbo Associates)
cases.summary: Introductory review of two related wetland applications: shifting/reworking golf putting greens and access paths on 92 (originally permitted administratively in 1999) and remediation of path work behind a pool on 94 that had drawn a building-department violation resolved by plea; treated as a Type II action, the board directed a site walk and referral to the Conservation Board, with a functional wetland analysis to follow.

memberPositions.stance: Neutral; wants a site walk and Conservation Board review before acting
memberPositions.evidence: Said he drove by the site and that 'this really sounds like the conservation board needs to dig in here,' agreeing to meet the applicant on-site.

cases.name: 12 Bedford Road mixed-use renovation (office + residence)
cases.applicant: John Jay Scarla Jr. (architect)
cases.summary: Review of a plan to renovate a historic structure into a law office in the front and residential duplex in the rear, remove the barn/shed, and build a rear parking lot; the board worked through driveway width, buffer/screening and clearance so delivery vehicles won't hit the building, and directed the applicant to LPC (certificate of appropriateness), ARB, and possibly the ZBA before scheduling a public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: Broadly favorable but wants driveway/parking clearance and screening resolved
memberPositions.evidence: Raised concern that a UPS/sprinter delivery truck could hit the building at the narrow rear driveway and asked whether the drive could be screened and shifted, while calling it in keeping with the neighborhood.

cases.name: 448 Bedford Road special use permit amendment (CMA Hillside nursery school)
cases.applicant: Steve Veneruso (Veneruso, Curto, Schwartz & Curto), attorney; Tom Curto/Carroll, architect
cases.summary: Introductory review of a request to amend a 1983 special use permit (which allowed two classrooms) to legalize the six classrooms the ~30-year-old nursery school actually operates, with added egress; the board explained the parallel special-permit track through the Town Board and directed the applicant to compile the outstanding items from staff comments before referral.

memberPositions.stance: Neutral/process-focused; probed for deficiencies and how oversight would work
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether there were any major deficiencies or hurdles on staff's list that would block going to the Town Board (e.g., parking or outdoor play area), which Carthy framed as a question about keeping oversight.

cases.name: Birken property, 99 Byram Ridge Road new single-family home
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch (LPN Engineering); Taylor Seguinza, architect
cases.summary: Review of a single-family house (replacing a demolished home) on a ~1.34-acre R-1A lot with no wetlands and no variances required; after twice at the RPRC, the applicant detailed stormwater mitigation (subsurface pipe network, two rain gardens, infiltration trench) and the board directed a site walk to review five-foot retaining walls and neighbor sightlines, plus a neighbor-notification public hearing.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke, but the RPRC requested a neighbor-notification meeting given the neighborhood's long-standing stormwater concerns; a neighbor is to receive screening.

memberPositions.stance: Mildly supportive; wants a site walk on the walls/driveway and a public hearing scheduled
memberPositions.evidence: Said he remained concerned about the walls, driveway and what the neighbor would look at, directed the applicant to stake the house and walls for a site walk, and agreed to schedule the public hearing.

cases.name: Extensions of time (215 Business Park Drive, 124 Mount Kisco Road, Hidden Oaks subdivision)
cases.address: 215 Business Park Drive; 124 Mount Kisco Road; Hidden Oaks
cases.summary: The board granted routine extensions of time for 215 Business Park Drive, 124 Mount Kisco Road, and the Hidden Oaks subdivision (the latter reported nearly complete with the plat picked up for county filing).

themes.note: Central to nearly every application (Tall Woods, 40 High St, Byram Ridge, Armonk Heights, Orchard); board generally satisfied mitigation is being addressed.
Wetland permits, buffers and delineations recurred (Tall Woods, 23 Bedford Banksville, 40 High St, Round Hill, Armonk Heights).
Repeated neighbor worry about septic-vs-sewer, well drawdown and shared aquifers, especially at 32 Orchard and 40 High St; board agreed to consult a hydrogeologist for Orchard.
Slope disturbance debated at 32 Orchard, Armonk Heights and Byram Ridge; board notes regulations permit disturbance when erosion is controlled.
Repeated complaint that neighbors learned of projects late (Orchard, Banksville, Armonk Heights); board emphasized keeping items under its jurisdiction for future public hearings.
Dominated the 23 Bedford Banksville hearing where office/storage/woodworking uses may be non-conforming; board declined to approve.
Raised at 32 Orchard (66 trees, 11 over 24 inches) and Round Hill; mitigation via landscaping and conservation easements discussed.
Segmentation/lead-agency and Type II determinations discussed at 23 Bedford Banksville, 40 High St (neg dec) and Round Hill.
Airport Campus school-bus sight-line/right-turn exit on Cooney Hill Road prompted a request to consult Byram Hills transportation.
12 Bedford Road renovation requires LPC certificate of appropriateness and ARB review.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the February 26 minutes and noted three applications (Harris, ~4/36 Main Street, 12 Maple Avenue) had come off the agenda. It reopened and then adjourned the public hearing for 11 Whipperwill Lane, focusing on private-road widening, an emergency-vehicle turnaround, tree loss and a promised landscape plan. It adopted the SEQRA findings statement and the preliminary and final subdivision resolutions for the Airport campus at 113 King Street (site plan withheld pending ARB approval). It introduced and referred the 10/20 Round Hill Road lot-line realignment to the ZBA (accessory-apartment variances) and Conservation Board, and worked through contaminated-fill removal, wetland/swale restoration and driveway-pier height on the Tripling Lane application, referring the piers to the ZBA.

cases.name: 11 Whipperwill Lane residential development
cases.summary: Applicant's team (attorney Corey Salomon and engineer Ralph) presented a switch to the smaller 5,800 sq ft home, private-road widening within the right-of-way, an emergency-vehicle turnaround, and commitments negotiated with neighbors; the board pressed for an engineered survey of the road improvements and a detailed landscape plan before approval, then adjourned the reopened public hearing.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; the applicant relayed neighbor requests (smaller home, added screening, limited work hours 9-6, porta-potty kept distant, no removal of additional mature trees).

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of progress but insists on an engineered survey plan of the road improvements and a robust landscape plan that satisfies neighbors before approval
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board will want an engineer's plan and urged the applicant to bring back an impressive landscape plan and keep working with the neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Sought clarity that the road widening stays within the private right-of-way and would not require easements or tree removal
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the widening was in the public/right-of-way and whether easements from neighbors would be needed; a later speaker referenced 'like Jim just asked.'

cases.name: Airport campus subdivision, 113 King Street
cases.summary: The board adopted the SEQRA findings statement (consistent with the town board's) and approved the preliminary and final subdivision resolutions as amended, dated March 11, 2024; site plan approval was withheld because the applicant has not yet obtained ARB approval. Members debated the roughly 70 conditions but staff confirmed most were routine engineering items.

memberPositions.stance: Concerned about the large number of conditions in the preliminary and final resolutions
memberPositions.evidence: The town planner noted 'Jim has expressed some concerns regarding the number of conditions' in the resolutions of approval.

memberPositions.stance: Shared concern about ~70 conditions and questioned the urgency of signing off now
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'like Jim, I'm kind of concerned about ... 70 conditions ... I don't think we've ever signed off on one,' and asked where the urgency was.

memberPositions.stance: Moved the approvals and wanted the tax-certiorari discontinuance held in escrow until approvals and statutes of limitation expire
memberPositions.evidence: Continued to hold the stipulation of discontinuance in escrow pending approvals and made the motions to adopt the findings and subdivision resolutions.

cases.name: Hoberman lot-line realignment, 10 & 20 Round Hill Road (Rolling Hill subdivision)
cases.applicant: Robert and Jill Hoberman
cases.summary: Applicant team (Corey Salomon, engineer Rich Williams, architect Zachary Harwin) introduced a lot-line realignment of 2006 lots 4 and 5 creating a ~16-acre estate/family compound plus a smaller home, with no new lots; discussion centered on expanding the clearing-and-grading limit (4.7 to ~5.94 acres) to balance ~20,000 yards of cut, steep slopes, septic, and the environmentally sensitive Mianus River headwaters. The board scheduled a site walk and referred the detached accessory-apartment (ADU) variances to the ZBA and the application to the Conservation Board.
cases.publicComment: No general public spoke; the Conservation Board liaison confirmed the referral over the 10+ acre parcels was appropriate.

memberPositions.stance: Cautiously receptive but wants a site walk and respect for the prior board's environmental delineations; questioned filling sensitive areas just to balance earthwork and moved to refer ADU variances to the ZBA
memberPositions.evidence: Urged going out to see the site and suggested exporting fill might be the better environmental solution than filling areas the earlier board wanted preserved; moved to send the applicant to the ZBA.

memberPositions.stance: Engaged on the comparison of original vs. proposed clearing-and-grading limit lines and their side-to-side expansion
memberPositions.evidence: Worked through the red/blue/purple clearing-and-grading overlay, confirming where proposed limits expanded versus the original.

cases.name: Tripling Lane residence site plan / wetlands
cases.summary: A previously seen application where the applicant (engineer Rick/Rich) agreed to remove roughly 704 cubic yards of contaminated fill; the board worked through how to remove and replace fill along an existing retaining wall, re-establish the wetland swale connecting lots 2, 4 and 6, and address a floor-area (basement/garage) dispute. The Conservation Board liaison challenged leaving the wall and importing clean fill instead of restoring natural grade. The board referred the over-height driveway piers to the ZBA and asked for an interim/sequencing grading plan.
cases.publicComment: Conservation Board liaison Vincent relayed that the Conservation Board (and resident Jane Black) understood the site would be restored to natural grade with fill exported, and questioned leaving the retaining wall and importing clean fill; noted 170 trees were removed and the original wetland could not be relocated on re-digging.

memberPositions.stance: Drove a remove-inspect-refill procedure for the contaminated fill and floated removing part of the wall to restore the wetland swale; moved to refer the pier height to the ZBA
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed removing all fill, inspecting/certifying export, then stockpiling and replacing clean fill, and suggested pulling ~100 feet of wall to re-establish the natural water course; moved to send piers to the ZBA.

memberPositions.stance: Agreed with the proposed fill-removal and refill procedure

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the March 11 minutes and then handled several land-use items: a re-approval public hearing for a lapsed lot line change at 246 Massaro Court, the town/Verizon municipal parking lot project at 23 Whippoorwill Road East (subdivision, site plan, wetlands and tree-removal permits), and a two-lot subdivision on Orchard Drive with a lengthy well/groundwater discussion. The board also reviewed the Summit Club maintenance-building site plan (held pending a special use permit), gave early review to improvements at 16 Davis Drive (site walk to be scheduled), granted an extension for Eagle Ridge, and adopted a standing Wednesday 8:30am time slot for site walks.

memberPositions.stance: moved to grant the extension
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to grant the Eagle Ridge extension of time.

themes.note: Central to the parking lot and Orchard Drive items; neighbor flooding fears and runoff onto town roads.
Below-code mitigation ratio on the parking lot, resolved by adding an inspection condition.
Extended concern that new wells could impair neighbors' wells with no clear remedy.
Town lot parking gains plus a golf-club-wide parking waiver/variance question at the Summit Club.
Regulated-tree counts folded into several permits.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved a site-plan legalization at 600 North Broadway, then after long debate gave conditional approval (4-1, Ruisi opposed) to the Remix restaurant at 12 Maple Avenue, whose valet/shared-parking plan was tied to a community benefits agreement and a future parking district. The board adopted a negative declaration and site/wetlands approval for the 23 Bedford-Banksville Road cleanup and a conditional master site-plan approval for the Airport Campus townhomes. It also referred the Saint Nersess Seminary addition (46 Bedford Road) and 12 Bedford Road to the ZBA for variances, kept the 11 Whippoorwill Lane hearing open over tree-removal and turnaround concerns, and scheduled a site walk for the 8 Cole wetland/steep-slope proposal.

cases.name: Silver Lake Realty Company, 600/606 North Broadway
cases.applicant: Silver Lake Realty Company (Jim Fleming, architect)

cases.name: Remix restaurant, 12 Maple Avenue
cases.applicant: Remix (Tony Vinesiano, attorney; Stefan, owner)
cases.summary: Continued public hearing on a restaurant with an off-street parking variance relying on valet and shared/leased parking at 12 and 20 Maple plus the American Legion; the board closed the hearing and approved the site plan 4-1, adding conditions requiring a town-board community benefits agreement and incorporating the H&H traffic-consultant letter.
cases.publicComment: One emailed letter from resident Michael Ferry opposed closing the hearing, arguing the plan is ~75% short of required parking, will congest Maple Avenue per the police chief, sets a bad precedent, and shifts parking costs to taxpayers; he asked for an independent traffic study. memberPositions.stance: Opposed; parking variance premature and unfair to other businesses
memberPositions.evidence: Voted no, warning overflow would fill the CVS and other lots and that granting the variance is imprudent with ~400 new rooftops coming into town.

memberPositions.stance: Torn but ultimately supportive; moved approval with CBA and traffic conditions
memberPositions.evidence: Repeatedly said he was 'torn' about the plan's dependence on valet and likely CVS-lot overflow, but made the motion to support the resolution with the amendments.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; found the town traffic consultant's review persuasive
memberPositions.evidence: Said it was very helpful to have the town's traffic consultant weigh in with clear recommendations and seconded the resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; voted yes
memberPositions.evidence: Voted yes on the roll call for the resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; relied on the independent traffic consultant
memberPositions.evidence: Voted yes; the board leaned on the point that they were entitled to rely on their outside traffic consultant's largely positive findings.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved three public-hearing applications: the Harris pool/patio in a wetland buffer at 9 Sterling Road North, the Birken teardown/rebuild at 99 Byron Ridge Road (which drew extensive stormwater/erosion complaints from downstream neighbor Dan Longo), and the Rosenthal expansion with accessory-apartment special permit at 10 Creamer Road. The board also handled several non-hearing items: referring the 17 New King Street unpermitted canopy to the ZBA for setback and parking variances, sending the 103 Miller Road scenic-road renovation to the ZBA/ARB, and scheduling site walks for the San Car pool relocation (with illegal-fill concerns) at 26 Carolon Place and two Red Brook Glen subdivision lots.

memberPositions.stance: supportive but defers technical stormwater judgment to the town engineer

memberPositions.stance: cautious; urged proving parking to avoid two ZBA trips
memberPositions.evidence: Asked the applicant to confirm adequate parking so they would not have to go to the ZBA twice.

Board scheduling multiple field visits for pending non-hearing applications.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (Chair Carthy plus members Pollack, Sauro, and Jensen joining remotely) approved the April 25 minutes and worked through a full agenda of largely returning applications. Items included a zoning-text/special-use recommendation for light manufacturing at 23 Bedford-Banksville Road, a site-plan amendment to the Bristol assisted-living EMT condition at 90 Business Park Drive, a wetlands-impacting pool/sport-court swap at 8 Cold Drive, a remediation site plan for a stalled Conyers Farm-area construction project, and updates on 601 Bedford Road (Embassy Club), 34 Cream Road, the Canyon Club golf-course special permit, and rooftop solar at a Lafayette Avenue auto shop. Most items were referred onward (Conservation Board, ZBA, town board) or set for future public hearings.

cases.name: 23 Bedford-Banksville Road (light manufacturing / storage)
cases.applicant: Anthony (applicant's attorney) / property owner
cases.summary: The board reviewed a petition, referred by the town board, to rezone the split-zoned parcel entirely into CBB and add a special-use permit allowing existing wood-processing and pre-cut metal/aluminum assemblage uses; the board voted to recommend adoption with added limits (use confined to roughly the rear 50% of the building not fronting the road, ground floor only, with a separate entrance).
cases.publicComment: A resident (Martin/Marty) questioned what materials (glues, solvents, varnishes, curing products) would be used, how waste is removed, and watershed/environmental impacts, and argued the tenants have operated in violation for years so their stewardship credibility is limited.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of recommending the permit but acknowledged legitimate community concern about manufacturing near a residential/watershed area
memberPositions.evidence: Said there is 'reasonable concern in the community for what is like manufacturing in a very residential neighborhood' and that 'high end' means nothing for pollution, yet moved the recommendation forward.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious; pressed that the whole building could become a factory and pushed to cap the manufacturing area and location
memberPositions.evidence: Played out the scenario that the office component could be eliminated and 'it could all be like my factory,' prompting the floor-area/location limits added to the recommendation.

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable with the amended recommendation
memberPositions.evidence: When asked, said 'I'm good with that.'

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; liked the improvement
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'No, I'm fine with what I heard... I like how this is improved.'

cases.name: The Bristol at 90 Business Park Drive (assisted living EMT condition)
cases.applicant: HSR / Bristol at Armonk (attorney Nick Capadora; Amy Silver-Maguire, COO, Ultimate Care)
cases.summary: The applicant sought to replace the 2012 site-plan condition requiring a 24-hour on-site EMT (which they say conflicts with New York State law) with a detailed emergency-care policy aimed at eliminating non-emergency calls to the Armonk Fire Department; the board directed staff and counsel to draft an amended site-plan resolution with an accountability mechanism, to return for a public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable relying on the Bristol and Armonk FD's joint policy, focused on building an accountability/repercussion mechanism
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board isn't getting into operational medical details but 'we are getting it from Bristol and Armonk together. I'm comfortable relying on that.'

memberPositions.stance: Cautious about the board defining medical/emergency protocols; noted the original EMT condition stemmed from the board's own misunderstanding
memberPositions.evidence: Said defining potentially life-threatening emergency protocols is 'beyond our skill set' and that the original condition reflected the board's lack of understanding of the regulatory scheme.

cases.name: 8 Cold Drive (pool / sport court amended site plan)
cases.applicant: Nizar Masu (attorney Corey Salomon, Zarin & Steinmetz; wetland expert Steve Moreno; landscape architect Richard Quigley)
cases.summary: The homeowners asked to amend a 2021 approval to swap the pool and sport-court locations, which would disturb a small (~900 sq ft) marginal wetland/drainage pocket, remove about 26 trees, and cut into steep slopes, offset by a proposed 2.5:1 mitigation wetland, a rain garden, and robust reforestation; the board voiced real concern about disturbing a wetland for a recreational amenity and referred the wetland question to the Conservation Board with 'no promises.'

memberPositions.stance: Probing/skeptical; pressed on fill volume, the culvert/drainage, and whether the pool bottom sits on fill
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether it is cut-and-fill and how much fill for the vanishing-edge pool, and questioned the culvert sizing and where the pool bottom sits.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious; flagged that the Conservation Board should review the impact of altering watercourses, not just the wetland
memberPositions.evidence: Built on Michael's point that the two watercourses meet and noted the Conservation Board 'looks at the impact of altering watercourses as well.'

cases.name: Conyers Farm-area remediation site plan (Kudrill property)

cases.name: 34 Cream Road (amended site plan / wetlands permit update)
