cases.summary: A rooftop-solar site plan surfaced that the building's current auto-service use was never approved by the Planning Board (it had been approved as a tree-service base of operations); the board asked the applicant to demonstrate conformance with the town code's auto-repair/body-shop requirements so a legal site plan can be granted before permitting the rooftop solar.

themes.note: Central to 8 Cold Drive, the Conyers Farm remediation, and 34 Cream Road; board especially wary of disturbing wetland for a recreational amenity.
Recommendations/reviews on 23 Bedford-Banksville light manufacturing, 601 Bedford Road, and the Canyon Club golf course.
Unlocatable leaching field at 601 Bedford Road and updated county septic flow regulations discussed on the Conyers Farm item.
Narrowly tailored special-use criteria to legalize existing wood/metal uses at 23 Bedford-Banksville while limiting proliferation.
Bristol assisted-living EMT condition replaced with an emergency-care policy plus an accountability mechanism.
~26 trees and steep-slope disturbance at 8 Cold Drive, offset by reforestation.
ARB required strict fire-restoration to original appearance at 601 Bedford Road; ARB approvals noted on other items.
Golf-club parking credit for on-site residents referred to the ZBA.

meetings.meetingSummary: A long, largely non-hearing agenda run by acting chair Steven Sauro with Chairman Carthy joining after the first item. The board approved a rock-crushing permit at 7 Hemlock Hollow with conditions, referred several applications to the ZBA (Mianus River Gorge barn, 16 Davis Drive, and an accessory-apartment conversion), gave extensive design feedback on a steep hillside house/pool on Kites Road, moved the Tripling wetland/site plan toward a public hearing, and granted extensions of time for 124 Old Mt Kisco Road and the Shell station at 375 Main Street. It also debated a parking-district approach for the Maraki Tavarna restaurant at the CVS center (450 Main St, adjourned) and declined to accept the as-built changes at 909 North Broadway as minor field changes.

cases.name: 7 Hemlock Hollow rock crushing
cases.summary: Applicant (engineer Ralph Alfonzetti of AB Engineering) sought a rock-crushing permit to process ~1,000-1,200 yards of foundation rock on-site for reuse; the board approved it subject to a 10-day maximum, 9am-4:30pm hours, and voluntary neighbor notification by mailing.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive if neighbors are protected
memberPositions.evidence: Presiding, asked about dust suppression and hours and said he was okay with it as long as they try to protect the neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Worried the noise could be insufferable for the nearest neighbor
memberPositions.evidence: Raised that crushing could be very noisy and insufferable for the nearest neighbor, but accepted the 10-day cap.

memberPositions.stance: Supports with formal neighbor notification by mailing
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested the applicant send a proof-of-mailing letter to neighbors within the required radius stating the crushing hours.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge Preserve barn, 99 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Mianus River Gorge (Preserve)
cases.summary: The Gorge proposes an accessory barn to the land steward's house; because it exceeds 25% of the main house floor area it needs a ZBA variance, so the board referred it to the ZBA to run in parallel while stormwater staff comments are addressed.

memberPositions.stance: No issues, refer to ZBA
memberPositions.evidence: Said he had no issues with either barn iteration and moved to send the applicant to the zoning board of appeals.

cases.name: Gobino residence, Kites Road (new house, pool, pool house)
cases.applicant: Angela Gobino
cases.summary: Owner/developer presented a new house with pool and pool house on a steep hillside requiring extensive regrading and tiered retaining walls (cutting ~6,800 yards and importing ~7,800 yards of fill); the board urged him to rotate the pool, reduce wall tiers, and engage a landscape architect, and he agreed to revise and return.

memberPositions.stance: Wants to help; suggested rotating the pool 90 degrees
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed turning the pool perpendicular to better fit the grade and reduce cut-and-fill while still achieving the applicant's goal.

memberPositions.stance: Blunt that the plan is unimaginative; push to hire a landscape architect
memberPositions.evidence: Said proposing a pool at 470 over a 448 grade shows the design does not comprehend construction costs and urged spending on a good landscape architect now.

cases.name: Tripling site plan / wetland determination
cases.summary: Applicant reported the ZBA granted variances (curb-cut width, pier height) and soil testing witnessed by the town consultant found no hydric soil / no wetland at Four Trip; the board, satisfied with the resolved grading and swale recreation, agreed to set a public hearing for the next meeting.

cases.name: 16 Davis Drive covered parking / driveway
cases.summary: Imported fill tested clean; the application involves a covered parking area, driveway work near a federally-regulated (Army Corps class II) wetland buffer, land-coverage exceedance, and ~11,000 sq ft of steep-slope disturbance. The board referred it to the ZBA for coverage and noted conservation board (wetlands permit) and ARB steps remain.

memberPositions.stance: Flagged the ~11,000 sq ft of steep-slope disturbance
memberPositions.evidence: Referenced the planner's memo noting almost 11,000 square feet of steep-slope disturbance tied to the fill.

memberPositions.stance: Concerned the 20-foot back-out area is too shallow
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the back-out area is only about 20 feet deep and would not work for a car turning.

cases.name: Maraki Tavarna restaurant, 450 Main Street (CVS shopping center)
cases.summary: Change of use for a restaurant space at the CVS center; the applicant was not present so the item was adjourned, but the board held a long policy discussion about the cumulative parking-variance requests in the Armonk hamlet and whether the property should join or form a parking district rather than seek repeated variances.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical of granting more variances; questions the owner's incentive to join a district
memberPositions.evidence: Asked what economic incentive the landowner has to join a parking district when the lot already works, and said the board should not keep granting variances over and over.

memberPositions.stance: Explored the economics of a stand-alone parking district for the property
memberPositions.evidence: Discussed that owners pay into a district by assessed valuation and raised whether CVS could simply designate its own lot a parking district.

cases.name: Accessory apartment conversion (office/garage)
cases.summary: Applicant seeks to convert an existing approved office/garage structure to an accessory apartment; because the structure was not built prior to 1984 it needs a ZBA variance, so the board referred it to the ZBA (applicant absent) to avoid losing a month.

cases.name: 124 Old Mount Kisco Road extension of time
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for the approved application at 124 Old Mount Kisco Road (paid extension).

cases.name: Shell gas station, 375 Main Street extension of time
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for the Shell gas station; the applicant is still awaiting DOT permits for work in the state right-of-way and reconsidering scope amid an ownership change.

cases.name: 909 North Broadway as-built field changes
cases.summary: The applicant built a taller retaining wall pulled forward of the approved location, changed screening/landscaping, omitted parking-lot lighting and compactor bollards, and presented it as an as-built; the board declined to treat these as minor field changes and directed the applicant to return with a plan and presentation, possibly with a site visit.

memberPositions.stance: Opposed to the deviations, especially lost buffer and floodlighting toward homes
memberPositions.evidence: Objected that the parking lot abuts residential properties and that eliminating the buffer and adding lighting blasting across the lot toward neighbors is a stretch.

memberPositions.stance: Won't accept as field changes; make the applicant come back and be accountable
memberPositions.evidence: Said rather than calling them minor field changes the applicant should return, present, and reconcile what was approved versus what was built.

themes.note: Central to the Kites Road hillside house and the 909 North Broadway as-built wall.
Multiple items (Gorge barn, 16 Davis, accessory apartment) referred to the zoning board.
Long policy debate on cumulative parking variances in the Armonk hamlet.
Tripling wetland determination and 16 Davis wetland buffer.
Raised on the Gorge barn, Kites Road, and Davis Drive.
Board pushed back on 909 North Broadway building differently than approved.
Concern about floodlighting toward residential neighbors at 909 North Broadway.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (opened and largely presided over by Steven Sauro as acting chair while Chair Carthy arrived late) approved the site development plan and tree-removal permit for 11 Whipperwill Lane after a public hearing, and granted a three-month extension of time for the related 'Two Trip Lane' violation cleanup. The board also approved the site plan and wetlands permit for the 45 Bedford Road 'Gateway' residential project (34 units with affordable-unit breakdown). Additional items included a referral on a filled-in pond/wetlands violation at 35 Whipperwill Road East (sent to the Conservation Board), a postponement of 50 Main Street (Maraki Taberna, no one appeared), and a recommendation to the Town Board to merge a foreclosed rear parcel on Windmill Road into the front lot with no resubdivision.

cases.name: 11 Whipperwill Lane (single-family home / lane improvements)
cases.applicant: Ralph Alfonzetti (applicant/engineer), rep. by attorney Corey Selm of Zarin & Steinmetz
cases.summary: Public hearing on the revised plan addressing four prior items (lane improvements, relocated turnaround, tree removal, private agreement with neighbors); board closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree-removal permit as amended to add a no-parking restriction on the turnaround and relocation of two trees.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor representative Randolph reported a private agreement reached that morning but flagged conflicting surveys and driveway-turnaround use by workers; neighbor Ira Weiss (11 Stone Hollow Way) raised strong concerns about preserving the screening trees on the slope, blasting damage/pre-blast surveys, and increased drainage/runoff since prior tree clearing.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved approval as amended
memberPositions.evidence: As acting chair he ran the hearing and moved to approve the site development plan and tree-removal permit for 11 Whipperwill Lane 'as amended,' adding a no-parking turnaround condition and tree relocation.

memberPositions.stance: No objection to the no-parking condition
memberPositions.evidence: Asked 'do you have any objections to that, Michael?' he replied 'No,' assenting to the added parking restriction.

cases.name: Two Trip Lane (extension of time on violation remediation)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer)
cases.summary: Board discussed a requested extension of time tied to a prior notice of violation; the building inspector felt a year was unnecessary, and after discussion the board granted a three-month extension, mainly to allow the required Town Board submission.

memberPositions.stance: Granted a three-month extension
memberPositions.evidence: As acting chair, stated 'I'll grant the extension of time for two trip lane for three months,' balancing the inspector's concern against the applicant's Town Board timeline.

cases.name: 45 Bedford Road - 'The Gateway' Residential Project
cases.applicant: Tony Viviano with Mike Tucker
cases.summary: Applicant reported completing the required off-site mitigation (Town Board license along Maple/municipal lot, modified deed and CBA); board resolved the affordable-unit count (30 market-rate plus 4 affordable of 34 total), reviewed stormwater/floodplain and wetland-mitigation conditions, then closed the hearing and approved the site plan and wetlands permit.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved approval of site plan and wetlands permit
memberPositions.evidence: As acting chair moved 'to approve the resolution for site plan and wetlands permit approvals for the Gateway Residential Project.'

cases.name: 35 Whipperwill Road East (filled-in pond / wetlands violation)
cases.applicant: homeowner, rep. by engineer Brian Hildenbrand
cases.summary: Referral from the RPRC on a homeowner who filled in a rear pond (cited for safety) and received a notice of violation; the applicant installed a pump system and now seeks a wetlands permit for the disturbance. Board directed the matter to the Conservation Board and Town Engineer/Building Inspector for review of floodplain/storage impacts before returning.

cases.name: Maraki Taberna - 50 Main Street
cases.applicant: Maraki Taberna
cases.summary: No applicant representative appeared; the item was carried to the next meeting, with staff to reach out beforehand.

cases.name: Windmill Road parcel (rear lot merger referral)
cases.address: Windmill Road (21 / rear parcel off Long Pond)
cases.applicant: Town Board referral (rear parcel owned by town after in-rem foreclosure; adjacent front-lot owner wishes to purchase)
cases.summary: Town Board referral seeking the board's planning recommendation on a town-owned foreclosed rear parcel; attorney Roland explained the history. Board recommended merging the rear parcel into the front lot with a covenant against resubdivision (rather than developing it), as far less controversial, and sent that recommendation back to the Town Board.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to recommend merger with no subdivision
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to recommend to the Town Board that the parcel be merged as a backlot with no further development (recorded: 'Michael made the motion').

memberPositions.stance: Seconded the merger recommendation
memberPositions.evidence: Recorded as seconding the motion ('Jim, seconded'); vote passed five ayes.

themes.note: Central to 11 Whipperwill hearing; neighbors worried about losing screening/slope trees and a poor-health 24-inch birch.
Runoff, infiltration systems, temporary sediment basins raised on Whipperwill and Gateway.
Gateway wetlands permit plus the 35 Whipperwill Road East pond-fill violation and floodplain-storage review.
Turnaround/easement disputes and conflicting surveys on Whipperwill Lane; backlot access on Windmill Road.
Gateway affordable-unit math resolved at 30 market-rate plus 4 affordable of 34 total.
Windmill Road recommendation to merge foreclosed rear parcel into front lot.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board held four public hearings and several discussion items on June 24, 2024. It adopted approvals for 103 Mianus River Road and 34 Creamer Road, kept the 4 Tripling Lane and 41 Mead Road hearings open pending Architectural Review Board approvals, and worked through discussion items on 9 Barnard Road (unpermitted fill testing), 1613 Old Orchard Street (driveway sight distance), and Maraki Tavern (parking expansion), plus an 11 Maple Avenue field change and an Eagle Ridge extension of time. Recurring themes were wetland mitigation, remediation of unpermitted work, ARB and outside-agency delays, and recording long-term monitoring/town access on site plans.

cases.name: 4 Tripling Lane
cases.summary: Public hearing opened on a site plan, wetland permit and tree removal application to legalize and remediate unpermitted work (fill, tree removal, house addition) ongoing since 2020. No public comment; the hearing was held open because the Architectural Review Board approval for the house addition is still outstanding, and the board adjourned the hearing to a future meeting.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared to comment on the application.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive but wants town monitoring access recorded on the site plan
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the resolution/site plan could include an access agreement letting the town periodically monitor the five-year restoration plan, and confirmed it should be noted on the site plan.

cases.name: 103 Mianus River Road
cases.applicant: John Swansburg
cases.summary: Public hearing on a scenic-roadway site plan to replace additions on the north end of the house within the same footprint, adding minimal building and land coverage. The applicant had ARB and ZBA approval and no public appeared; the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution.
cases.publicComment: No public comment; the board confirmed no one from the public was present for this item.

cases.name: 41 Mead Road
cases.summary: Public hearing on an amended site plan, wetland and tree removal permit to remediate a heavily disturbed wetland site where a prior owner built an unpermitted second story (increasing bedrooms beyond septic approval) triggering a stop-work order. The board could not close the hearing pending ARB approval and DEC/health permits, but voted to have the planner convey to the building inspector that it would not object to relief allowing at-risk interior four-bedroom work; item carried to July.
cases.publicComment: No public comment; discussion noted neighbors were supportive and wanted the project finished.

memberPositions.stance: Focused on the extent of site disturbance and how the excess fill and erosion would be remediated
memberPositions.evidence: Having attended the site walk, pressed the applicant to walk through how the large amount of disturbance and stray fill around the house would be corrected.

memberPositions.stance: Sympathetic to the applicant; floated ways to keep the project a compliant four-bedroom
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested the applicant could continue four-bedroom construction and reclassify extra rooms (e.g. attic space, artist studio) to fit the septic approval.

memberPositions.stance: Shared concerns about precedent and the health-department bedroom issue but saw mitigating circumstances in the town's imperfect process
memberPositions.evidence: Voiced caution about the health department and the added bedrooms while noting the town's review process was not perfect, creating mitigating circumstances.

cases.name: 34 Creamer Road
cases.summary: Public hearing on an amended site plan, wetland permit and tree removal for a single-family residence with driveway and pool in a wetland buffer, previously approved in 2018. A neighbor asked about remaining tree removal and screening; the board closed the hearing and adopted the resolution as amended, adding a long-term monitoring/access note on the site plan.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Mr. Dempsey (38 Creamer Road) asked whether tree removal was complete and about screening along the shared property line; the applicant explained roughly 90% of trees were already cut and an extensive two-to-one mitigation planting plan would provide screening.

memberPositions.stance: Proposed noting long-term monitoring/town access on the site plan so it carries to future owners
memberPositions.evidence: Recommended adding a note on the site plan allowing the town access for the five-year monitoring and maintenance, citing a past case where a new owner blocked access.

cases.name: 11 Maple Avenue
cases.summary: Discussion item treated as a field change: the required handicap access ramp was relocated from the front to the rear of the building. The board approved the field change so the building department could close out the permits.

cases.name: 9 Barnard Road
cases.applicant: Mr. Gentile
cases.summary: Discussion item where the board acts in an advisory capacity to the building department over fill imported without a permit. The applicant's attorney and consultant argued prior testing (with slightly elevated but acceptable lead) was sufficient, while the town's HES consultant recommended a more rigorous DEC Part 360 sampling protocol. The board directed the applicant to comply with the HES testing protocol before the fill could be allowed to remain.
cases.publicComment: No general public comment; the applicant's team (attorney, environmental consultant Mark Mulsbow) and town consultant Rich Baldwin/HES presented and debated the testing.

memberPositions.stance: Insisted the applicant follow the town/HES testing protocol before recommending the fill stay
memberPositions.evidence: Concluded the board should instruct the applicant to comply with the HES testing protocol in order to move forward.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical of the applicant's resistance to sampling; sensed the board simply needs the samples taken
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was getting the feeling that the board just wants the samples taken after so much back-and-forth.

memberPositions.stance: Probed whether unpermitted fill had also gone into the rear septic area
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether any fill was imported into the backyard near the septic system, following up a question raised in a prior meeting.

cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.applicant: Marlene Doran
cases.summary: Discussion of a new house on a vacant Quarry Heights lot where the driveway cannot meet the 200-foot sight distance requirement, requiring a ZBA variance. The board questioned the claimed clear sight line to the east and asked the applicant to return with a sight-distance profile and dimensions before being referred to the ZBA.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical of the claimed eastern sight line; wants a verified profile before the ZBA referral
memberPositions.evidence: Said he visited the site over the weekend and could not see, doubting a vehicle would be visible given the grade, and directed the applicant to prepare sight-line profiles.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to refer the applicant to the ZBA for the sight-distance variance
memberPositions.evidence: Made a motion to send the applicant to the ZBA, before the board decided more sight-line information was needed first.

cases.name: Maraki Tavern (Maple Avenue shopping center)
cases.summary: Discussion of a restaurant expansion into an adjacent retail bay requiring roughly 15 additional parking spaces. The planner floated forming a Maple Avenue parking district, which the board and applicant viewed as a non-starter since the property owner would give up a parking asset for little benefit. The board referred the applicant to the ZBA for the parking variance without making a formal recommendation.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of the successful business but candid about real parking shortages there
memberPositions.evidence: Called it one of his favorite restaurants and described having to fight for a spot over on the CVS side when it is crowded.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge
cases.summary: Procedural item: the board granted an extension of time for the Eagle Ridge application with no discussion.

themes.note: Central to 4 Tripling Lane, 41 Mead Road and 34 Creamer Road; board supportive of restoration but firm on mitigation.
Recurring across 41 Mead Road, 9 Barnard Road and 4 Tripling Lane; board wants prior owners' violations corrected.
ARB, DEC and health-department timing blocked closing hearings on 4 Tripling Lane and 41 Mead Road.
Board repeatedly resolved to record town monitoring access on site plans so it binds future owners.
Bedroom increases outstripping septic approvals raised at 41 Mead Road and probed at 9 Barnard Road.
Part of permits on 4 Tripling Lane, 41 Mead Road and 34 Creamer Road; mostly resolved via mitigation.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the June 24 minutes and heard several items. It reviewed the Hillside Church nursery school special use permit (legalizing an expansion from two to six classrooms) and recommended the town board issue the permit while referring the applicant to the zoning board for an outdoor-recreation-space variance. The board also began hearing the Breezemont day camp special use permit at 60 Cocks Avenue, and reviewed and recommended that the town board adopt proposed battery/energy-storage legislation. A public hearing for a property on Mead(?) Road was rolled over to the next meeting.

cases.name: 41 Mead Road public hearing
cases.summary: The scheduled public hearing was rolled over to the next meeting and not heard.

cases.name: Hillside Church nursery school, 448 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Hillside Church (represented by attorney Stephen Venner)
cases.summary: The board reviewed a special use permit amendment to legalize the nursery school's long-standing expansion from two to six classrooms; it recommended the town board issue the permit and referred the applicant to the zoning board for an outdoor-recreation-space variance.
cases.publicComment: Applicant reported families are in favor and no negative community feedback had been received; no public spoke at the meeting.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved to recommend the town board issue the permit and refer to zoning board
memberPositions.evidence: As chair he made the recommendation to the town board to issue the special use permit and moved to send the applicant to the zoning board for the variance.

cases.name: Breezemont Day Camp, 60 Cocks Avenue
cases.applicant: Gordon Josie (owner/director) and Walter (co-director), Breezemont Day Camp
cases.summary: The board took up the special use permit for the Breezemont day camp, an existing legal non-conforming use seeking to make it a permitted use so future improvements are possible; the applicant began explaining planned upgrades before the recording cut off.

cases.name: Battery/energy-storage legislation review
cases.applicant: Town Board (referral for legislation review)
cases.summary: The board discussed proposed battery/energy-storage zoning legislation, state efforts to override local zoning, and the public-utility definition, then recommended the town board adopt the legislation.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved to recommend the town board adopt the legislation
memberPositions.evidence: As chair he summarized the board's task and made the motion recommending the town board adopt the legislation.

themes.note: Central to both the Hillside Church nursery school and the Breezemont day camp items.
Board recommended the town board adopt enabling legislation; concerns about state override and public-utility status.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the July 8 minutes, then closed a continued public hearing and approved the amended site plan, tree-removal and wetland permit for 41 Meat Road (an existing house being brought into conformance with a six-bedroom septic and wetland-buffer mitigation). The board reviewed 3 Cedar Hill Road, a corner-lot addition on a scenic road, and sent it to the ARB before a future hearing. It also took up 22 Whippoorwill Road, a house under construction whose foundation was built six inches too high with a porch changed from piers to a poured wall, prompting neighbor concerns and a scheduled board site visit. The board granted extensions of time for the Summer Club at Armonk and 40 High Street.

cases.name: 41 Meat Road
cases.summary: Continued public hearing on an existing house being brought into conformance; the board reviewed updated architectural plans (bedroom count reduced to six to match a six-bedroom septic), retaining-wall and mitigation conditions, and pending DEC and health-department approvals, then closed the hearing and approved the amended site plan, tree removal and wetland permit.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors appeared; the chair confirmed there was no public present for this hearing.

memberPositions.stance: Probed how approving the resolution actually helps the applicant, but supportive of moving forward
memberPositions.evidence: Asked how passing the resolution helps when the applicant is still awaiting health-department and DEC approvals.

memberPositions.stance: Focused on sequencing of conditions; identified the DEC items as the true gating factor
memberPositions.evidence: Observed that with items five, twelve and the curb cut handled, the gating factor was DEC-related conditions six and seven.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to approve the amended approvals
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to approve the site plan, tree removal and wetland permit approvals for 41 Meat Road as amended.

cases.name: 3 Cedar Hill Road
cases.summary: A corner lot fronting on the scenic East Middle Patent Road requires Planning Board site plan approval for a first- and second-floor addition; the board discussed screening/visibility and a wetland delineation update and directed the applicant to the ARB before returning for a public hearing and resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Raised possible enhanced screening but comfortable advancing the application to the ARB
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested looking for screening opportunities without removing trees, then directed the applicant to make its ARB application and come back.

cases.name: 22 Whippoorwill Road
cases.summary: A house under construction had its foundation built six inches too high and its front porch changed from piers to a poured wall, causing plan discrepancies that pushed it from the RPRC to the Planning Board. The board and neighbors raised concerns about front-yard grade, mass and retaining walls, and stormwater; the board scheduled a site visit, will bring the applicant back in August, and plans a September public hearing.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Steve McLaughlin (24 Whippoorwill) objected that there was no public hearing before the project was approved; a landscaper/excavator neighbor across the street raised stormwater and infiltrator-on-rock concerns and feared runoff eroding his property; the 22 Whippoorwill neighbor's privacy concern was addressed with a proposed property-line planting.

memberPositions.stance: Acknowledged community concern over the after-the-fact construction and pushed for a board site visit before any decision
memberPositions.evidence: Noted people are upset by what looks from the street like an imposing structure and insisted the board go out and look before approving.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical the drawings reflect what was built; pressed on stair configuration and missing dimensions
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the built stair reverses on itself closer to the street than the submitted plans depict and that the porch is not dimensioned.

memberPositions.stance: Found the representations made to the RPRC inconsistent with the as-built house and questioned the late as-built survey
memberPositions.evidence: Said the representation made to the RPRC is not consistent with what is there now and called that problematic, and pressed on when the as-built foundation survey was done.

cases.name: Summer Club at Armonk
cases.summary: The board granted two extensions of time for the Summer Club at Armonk, one for the subdivision and one for the site plan, with no concerns raised.

cases.name: 40 High Street
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for 40 High Street; a member asked why the extension was requested but no specific reason was provided beyond an attached letter.

themes.note: Both 41 Meat Road and 22 Whippoorwill involved construction that did not match approved plans.
Retaining wall suitability and steep front-yard grade were central to 41 Meat Road and 22 Whippoorwill.
22 Whippoorwill neighbors objected to lack of a public hearing and to stormwater and privacy impacts.
41 Meat Road hinged on a six-bedroom septic with pending DEC and county health approvals.
Wetland buffer mitigation at 41 Meat Road and a wetland delineation update at 3 Cedar Hill.
Screening discussed for the scenic-road addition at Cedar Hill and to soften mass at Whippoorwill.
A neighbor challenged infiltrator installation and runoff onto his property at 22 Whippoorwill.
Routine extensions granted for the Summer Club at Armonk and 40 High Street.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the July 22 minutes and moved through a full agenda: two site-plan items were closed and approved (the River Gorge accessory barn on a scenic road, and 4 Trip Lane), the Bristol/Armonk Fire Department non-emergency-call agreement was adopted, and several items were discussed without final action (22 Whipple Well Road East retaining-wall/grading, the 1700 Old Orchard Street/Jenny Clarkson slope remediation, St. Nersess Seminary at 46/86 Bedford Road, the Hoberman lot-line realignment at 111 Round Hill Road, and a new 73 Whipple Well Road two-lot subdivision sketch plat). The board also granted an extension of time for the airport campus. Recurring themes were after-the-fact remediation of unpermitted work, stormwater/grading details, landscaping and screening, and environmental protection of reservoirs and the Mianus headwaters.

cases.name: River Gorge accessory barn
cases.summary: A straightforward accessory barn on a scenic road that had already cleared the ZBA, ARB and engineering review returned for final action; the board found no neighbors present, closed the public hearing and approved the draft resolution quickly.

memberPositions.stance: supportive, ready to approve
memberPositions.evidence: Noted it was a straightforward project, no neighbor issues, and moved to close the hearing and approve the resolution.

cases.name: 4 Trip Lane (Frederick Paul/Bolander)
cases.applicant: Frederick Paul
cases.summary: A long-running application (started 2020) involving unpermitted work, tree removal and fill returned after obtaining ARB approval; the board reopened and closed the hearing, confirmed gross-floor-area was well under the maximum, amended the resolution to remove conditions 3 and 4, and approved it.

memberPositions.stance: cautiously supportive, wanted the gross-floor-area loose end closed
memberPositions.evidence: Raised concern that an open gross-floor-area question could send the applicant back, but was reassured the house is well under the maximum and moved to approve.

cases.name: 22 Whipple Well Road East retaining wall / grading
cases.summary: Following a site walk, the board pressed the applicant on unclear grades, the height and consistency of a veneered retaining wall, stormwater infiltration units and screening; it asked for site sections, an as-built survey, and options showing one wall versus a second tier plus a robust landscape plan before proceeding.
cases.publicComment: The adjoining neighbor (Steve) said the new structure looms over his driveway and asked for taller screening/plantings that would mature high enough to block the windows; he noted a gap between what the applicant proposed (~12 ft trees) and his goal and said he would pay to plant on his own property.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical; insisted on aesthetic consistency and a robust landscape plan
memberPositions.evidence: Argued you must be consistent, that a veneered wall with large boulders 'doesn't work,' and urged the applicant to present a robust landscape plan mitigating the mass.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical; wants actual numbers and an as-built survey before deciding
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board shouldn't be guessing and needs the actual grades, site sections and a corrected surveyor-signed as-built plan.

memberPositions.stance: declined to add substantive comment
memberPositions.evidence: When asked if he had anything to add, replied he was fine.

cases.name: The Bristol at 90 Business Park Drive - Armonk Fire Department non-emergency call agreement
cases.applicant: The Bristol
cases.summary: The board adopted an amended resolution plus an emergency-care policy and flowchart establishing a procedure to reduce non-emergency calls to the Armonk Fire Department, with the fire department to report back to the planning board biennially for accountability.

memberPositions.stance: questioned whether the planning board (vs. the building inspector) was the right body for reporting, but ultimately satisfied
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the board wanted to be in the position of receiving reports rather than referring to the building inspector; accepted the Chair's rationale that it creates biennial accountability.

memberPositions.stance: supportive; moved to adopt the resolution and documents
memberPositions.evidence: Said all parties were happy and moved to adopt the resolution, flowchart and emergency-call process.

memberPositions.stance: supportive of the planning board being the review body
memberPositions.evidence: Said he thought it was the right place for the fire department to report back.

cases.name: Jenny Clarkson property, 1700 Old Orchard Street - slope remediation
cases.summary: Construction/demolition fill placed without permits had washed across Route 22 into the reservoir; the applicant proposed removing roughly 18 inches of C&D material with full-time inspection and re-grading a basin/swale. DEP and the Conservation Board signed off, but the board declined to place unresolved technical items in a resolution and directed the applicant's engineer to work out details offline with the town engineer before a hearing.
cases.publicComment: George Trepo of the Conservation Board reported the board studied the origin of the fill and the runoff into the reservoir over three or four site visits and was satisfied with the proposed remediation.

memberPositions.stance: cautious; unwilling to adopt conditions until facts are agreed
memberPositions.evidence: Said there were significant unresolved items and he was reluctant to throw them into a resolution as conditions, preferring the town engineer and applicant reach agreement first.

cases.name: St. Nersess Armenian Seminary, 46 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: St. Nersess Armenian Seminary
cases.summary: The applicant combined a previously two-building proposal into a single addition to the married-students building to solve sanitary-line elevation problems, having secured a side-yard variance and ARB approval; the board reviewed grading, septic/well capacity, runoff and a proposed rain garden and agreed to schedule a public hearing (targeting the second September meeting) once the SWPPP is submitted.

memberPositions.stance: supportive but insisted the SWPPP be in hand before any resolution
memberPositions.evidence: Made the point that it would be silly to look at a resolution without the SWPPP in hand.

memberPositions.stance: supportive; called it a nice project, wants engineering details finished
memberPositions.evidence: Praised the project and campus and set up advancing to a public hearing after the engineering is worked out.

cases.name: Hoberman lot-line realignment, 111 Round Hill Road
cases.applicant: Robert Hoberman
cases.summary: A lot-line realignment (no new lots, type-II SEQRA) combined with site plan and a special permit for an over-800-sq-ft accessory apartment; the applicant showed reduced clearing/grading, 108 proposed trees, and requested amending the 2002 clearing-and-grading limit line. The board agreed to a replanted buffer near property lines, voted to remove the required cistern (fire department won't maintain it) in favor of bedroom sprinklers, and set a public hearing for September 9.
cases.publicComment: Applicant/owner Robert Hoberman (a fireman) argued the cistern would not save a house before fire trucks arrive and preferred sprinklering bedrooms as an exit strategy; he also noted reduced clearing/grading preserves more land toward the Mianus feed.

memberPositions.stance: engaged and cautious about environmental impacts, especially the Mianus headwaters and buffers
memberPositions.evidence: Recalled the site walk and voiced concern about protecting the stream feeding the Mianus and whether extending grading down the slope was appropriate.

memberPositions.stance: supportive; questioned why the 2002 clearing/grading line should change and endorsed removing the cistern
memberPositions.evidence: Probed the rationale for revising the prior board's clearing/grading limit and moved the item toward a public hearing while agreeing to drop the cistern requirement.

cases.name: 73 Whipple Well Road two-lot subdivision (Wellness Estates LLC)
cases.applicant: Wellness Estates LLC (Alice Geske)
cases.summary: A sketch-plat discussion for a two-lot subdivision of an 8.8-acre R2A parcel containing a pond, watercourse, wetlands and steep slopes; frontage and the desire to preserve a 2005 septic system drove the irregular lot shape. The board found no major issues, discussed whether a better layout was possible, touched on the open-space/recreation-fee requirement, and encouraged the applicant to submit a preliminary application.

memberPositions.stance: neutral/inquisitive; probed the lot shape and open-space requirement
memberPositions.evidence: Asked why the subdivision looked the way it did and whether a better two-lot layout was possible if a new septic were built, and questioned the open-space/park treatment.

memberPositions.stance: accepting; agreed the layout works despite looking funky
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed with the assessment that the plan works fine once developed and did not see a major issue.

cases.name: Airport campus - extension of time
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for the airport campus approval on a routine motion with no discussion.

themes.note: Grades, infiltration units, basins and rain gardens were central to most engineering discussions.
Recurs across 4 Trip Lane, 22 Whipple Well and 1700 Old Orchard, where fill/tree removal/construction occurred without permits.
Buffers, hedges and robust plantings raised for 22 Whipple Well, the seminary and Hoberman.
Hoberman lot line, 73 Whipple Well subdivision, and related SEQRA/open-space treatment.
Wall height, veneer consistency and a possible second tier dominated the 22 Whipple Well discussion.
Septic capacity and public-well setbacks shaped the seminary and 73 Whipple Well layouts.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the August 5th minutes and moved through a full agenda: it held a public hearing and adopted the site plan for the Maraki Taverna restaurant expansion, opened and adjourned a hearing for 46 Bedford Road, and approved the 111 Round Hill lot-line realignment subdivision plus the associated 10 and 20 Round Hill Way site plans (eliminating fire cisterns in favor of second-floor bedroom sprinklers). It granted a 12th extension of time for 124 Old Mount Kisco Road, discussed the Breezemont/60 Cox Avenue day camp legalization (scheduling a site walk), and referred the San Car Residence pool project at 26 Carolyn Place to the Zoning Board over a gross-land-coverage overage.

cases.name: Maraki Taverna restaurant expansion
cases.applicant: Maraki Taverna (represented by Chris Crocco)
cases.summary: The board held the public hearing on the expansion of the restaurant into the adjacent space, confirmed the applicant had obtained its off-street parking variance from the ZBA, and adopted the site plan resolution.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke at the hearing; the chair relayed a neighbor's concern about the shared dumpster and outdoor storage at the rear of the building and asked the applicant to keep the area clean to reduce rodents.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of approval; asked applicant to address neighbor's rear-of-building cleanliness concern
memberPositions.evidence: Relayed that neighbors would appreciate a prodigious effort to keep the back clean to reduce rodents, then moved to close the hearing and adopt the resolution.

memberPositions.stance: No objection to this applicant but flagged the broader downtown parking demand as a larger issue
memberPositions.evidence: Noted a theme of restaurants expanding via variances and asked whether the town will have to solve for larger parking demand, saying it was his major substantive comment when the board reviewed this before.

cases.name: 46 Bedford Road (seminary on Route 22)
cases.summary: The board opened the public hearing, found no neighbors present, and adjourned the hearing to the next meeting.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public were present.

cases.name: 111 Round Hill Road lot line realignment (111 Round Hill Realty LLC)
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Realty LLC (Cory Salmore, Zarin & Steinmetz)
cases.summary: The board held the public hearing and adopted preliminary and final subdivision/lot-line-change resolutions for 10 and 20 Round Hill Way, treating it as a SEQRA Type 2 action since no new lots are created, and amended the resolutions so the applicant's offered fire sprinklers apply only to second-floor bedrooms in lieu of the eliminated cisterns.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke on the lot-line item directly; a neighbor letter about clearing and grading beyond previously approved limits was acknowledged and the applicant agreed to add screening.

memberPositions.stance: Presided and moved approvals; sought to amend the sprinkler condition to second-floor bedrooms only
memberPositions.evidence: Recounted that the cisterns were removed because no one would maintain them and the applicant offered second-floor bedroom sprinklers, then moved to amend and adopt the subdivision resolutions.

cases.name: 10 Round Hill Way site plan
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Realty LLC (Cory Salmore, Zarin & Steinmetz)
cases.summary: The board held the public hearing and adopted the site plan resolution as amended, requiring a substantial re-vegetated buffer on the regraded slope between the pool and the neighbor's property line and second-floor bedroom sprinklers.
cases.publicComment: A neighbor from 15 Gifford Lake Drive (Ulla-pack) asked about the number of trees being removed (a few hundred), grading and stormwater runoff/soil erosion, septic placement relative to downhill groundwater and wells, and wildlife impact; the applicant and planner explained replanting, county Health Department septic oversight, and the 10-acre conservation easement.

memberPositions.stance: Wanted coordination between landscaping and stormwater design and was concerned about undermining trees
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the stormwater plan shows many outlets and asked that landscaping and the SWPPP be coordinated so plantings do not undermine trees.

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable making the added screening/buffer a condition of approval
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was comfortable making it a condition that the applicant re-vegetate the regraded slope to the property line.

cases.name: 20 Round Hill Way site plan
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Realty LLC (Cory Salmore, Zarin & Steinmetz)
cases.summary: The board held a brief public hearing with no public comment, confirmed the clearing and grading limit line was not significantly changed and no wetland permit was needed, and adopted the resolution as amended for second-floor bedroom sprinklers.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke.

memberPositions.stance: Seconded the motion to close the public hearing
memberPositions.evidence: Chair noted 'Steve seconded it' on the motion to close the public hearing for 20 Round Hill Way.

cases.name: 124 Old Mount Kisco Road extension of time
cases.applicant: Represented by Cory Salmore
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time (noted as roughly the 12th) after the applicant explained focus had shifted to other projects that are now wrapping up so work can proceed on 124 and 130.

cases.name: Breezemont day camp legalization (60 Cox Avenue)
cases.applicant: Breezemont day camp (Walter, with engineer Dan Holt)
cases.summary: Referred back from the Town Board, the board discussed legalizing the existing day camp via site plan, focusing on the required 15-foot landscaped screening buffer adjacent to residences and summer vehicle parking/traffic; no approval tonight, and a site walk was scheduled (the 18th) before setting a public hearing.
cases.publicComment: A recurring neighbor across the road is expected to submit a letter of concern; no public spoke at this discussion.

memberPositions.stance: Suggested a board site walk to understand the cluttered plan and parking flow
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether it makes sense to walk the site and take a walk around to make sure the board understood the buffer, tree screening, and vehicle circulation.

memberPositions.stance: Wanted the plan to clearly note the 15-foot buffer and parking areas before approval
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed the applicant to note on the plan where parking is happening and to specifically call out the 15-foot perimeter buffer and any supplemental screening, and said they would not approve it tonight.

cases.name: San Car Residence pool (26 Carolyn Place)
cases.applicant: San Car Residence (Ralph Oppenzetti / architect Lutto Delio)
cases.summary: The board discussed the proposed rear-yard pool and cabana with removal of illegally placed fill and legalization of existing house issues, then debated whether the gross-land-coverage overage requires a variance and voted to refer the applicant to the Zoning Board of Appeals, deferring a public hearing until any variance is resolved.

memberPositions.stance: Supported referring the project to the ZBA to resolve the land-coverage overage before any hearing
memberPositions.evidence: Framed the plan for referral to the ZBA and to consult the building inspector, moving to send the applicant to the zoning board for its gross land coverage overage if needed.

themes.note: Recurring focus at Round Hill Way and the Breezemont day camp on buffers and re-vegetation adjacent to neighboring residences.
Round Hill removals of a few hundred trees offset by hundreds of proposed plantings.
Cisterns eliminated because maintenance responsibility was unresolved; applicant offered sprinklers limited to second-floor bedrooms.
26 Carolyn Place referred to the ZBA over a gross-land-coverage overage.
Neighbor letters and comments on clearing/screening at Round Hill and expected letter on the day camp.
Ongoing town engineer review of the SWPPP and coordination with landscaping at 10 Round Hill Way.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board worked through a full agenda: it closed the public hearing and approved the site plan for the seminary addition (married-student quarters and a dean residence) at 46 Bedford Road, and kept open the public hearing for the mixed-use office/residence conversion at 12 Bedford Road after extensive opposition from a neighbor and missing engineering, landscape, and lighting plans. It also continued the long-running 9 Barnard retaining-wall and soil-testing matter (favoring a tiered wall), advanced the Summer Club golf-course maintenance building toward a public hearing, granted extensions of time for the Massaro Court subdivision and Eagle Ridge, reviewed an already-built front-yard retaining wall at 22 Whippoorwill Road East, steered a Main Street parking-variance applicant toward the ZBA and a future parking district, referred 18 Carolyn Place to the RPRC, and approved moving conditions to pre-CO for 14 Middle Patent Road.

cases.name: Seminary / St. Nurses addition, 46 Bedford Road
cases.summary: Continuation of the public hearing for a two-story addition creating married-student quarters and a retired-dean residence at the rear of a former barn; with no public present the board closed the hearing and adopted a resolution approving the site plan.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; the applicant's architect (Robert Stancy) and engineer (Rich Cordone) presented and noted drainage would be redirected to the on-site stormwater basin to reduce runoff toward Seymour Place.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; satisfied drainage concerns addressed and moved to close hearing and approve
memberPositions.evidence: Chair moved to close the public hearing and adopt the approval resolution, noting the Seymour Place drainage concern was addressed.

memberPositions.stance: Asked whether there is a cap on the number of residences and wanted the limit read into the resolution
memberPositions.evidence: A member (addressed by the Chair) asked Adam if there is a limit on residences at the property and to read the special-permit condition aloud.

cases.name: 12 Bedford Road mixed-use conversion (office + residence)
cases.applicant: property owner (attorney/solo practitioner)
cases.summary: Public hearing opened for converting a historic house into a front office plus rear apartment; a neighbor voiced extensive opposition and the applicant's plans lacked current engineering, an updated eight-space parking layout, and landscape/lighting details, so the board kept the hearing open pending revised submissions.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Michael Ferrari (owner of 16 Bedford Road, manager of 20 Bedford Road) strongly opposed, citing the narrow 11.5-foot driveway, parking deficiency, self-created hardship, missing landscaping/engineering plans, lighting, and delivery-truck safety; he urged keeping the hearing open. The applicant/owner rebutted at length, calling the objections a bullying tactic by a would-be buyer and stressing the small scale and historic-preservation intent.

memberPositions.stance: Somewhat sympathetic but insists on complete engineering, landscape, and lighting plans before closing; kept hearing open
memberPositions.evidence: Chair pressed for updated plans showing eight spaces, a landscape plan and lighting analysis, and moved to keep the public hearing open.

memberPositions.stance: Engaged on the grass-crete pull-off detail and asked the applicant to illustrate it on the returning plan
memberPositions.evidence: Steve said John answered most of his points but asked about the grass-crete pull-off and requested it be illustrated when the plan comes back.

cases.name: 9 Barnard (Nye and Barnard) retaining wall
cases.applicant: Joe Gentile
cases.summary: Continued discussion of an existing over-height retaining wall built without a permit and the associated fill/soil testing; the board reaffirmed its preference for a tiered wall set back from the neighbor and directed HES and the applicant's environmental firm to coordinate on-site sampling, carrying the matter to the next meeting.
cases.publicComment: Owner Joe Gentile spoke angrily, saying delays were largely caused by the board, that he had spent roughly $90,000 and submitted six plans, and that he built the wall for his family's safety. A neighbor (Tom) asked about the status of the HES soil testing and urged it also cover imported fill in the rear yard.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical; views the process as a deliberate delay tactic and firmly favors a tiered wall set back from the neighbor
memberPositions.evidence: Said the wall was built without a permit and the applicant is protracting the process, and that the board was firm in preferring a tiered wall set back from the neighbor's property.

memberPositions.stance: Favors a tiered wall on blank-slate design logic and wants the HES soil-testing protocol completed
memberPositions.evidence: Explained the tiered-wall consensus came from asking how they would design it from scratch, and asked to confirm the soil testing would follow the HES protocol.

memberPositions.stance: Supported a two-tiered wall
memberPositions.evidence: The Chair noted Michael had expressed the wall should be two-tiered.

memberPositions.stance: Wants the matter resolved; somewhat sympathetic to the applicant but agrees the board would have required a tiered wall
memberPositions.evidence: Urged putting it to rest, directed Adam to resurface prior tiered-wall plans and HES to set the sampling protocol on site.

cases.name: Summer Club golf course maintenance facility
cases.applicant: Summer Club (JMC engineering)
cases.summary: Review of the site plan for the golf-course maintenance building under the existing special-use permit; with few outstanding items the board directed the applicant to schedule a public hearing and move toward site-plan approval.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; directed the applicant to schedule the public hearing and move forward
memberPositions.evidence: Chair told the applicant to schedule the public hearing and move forward after confirming few items remained.

cases.name: Massaro Court 3-lot subdivision
cases.applicant: Bernardo and Philomena Luciano (Hudson Engineering)
cases.summary: An approved but unfiled subdivision with a lot-line change; the board granted an extension of time and gave informal direction to let the town engineer get the plat signed, deferring several site-specific conditions to later site-plan review rather than reopening the resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of getting the plat signed and handling site-specific conditions at site-plan review; moved the extension
memberPositions.evidence: Chair moved to grant the extension of time and endorsed deferring the half-dozen site-specific conditions to site-plan review.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; seconded the extension of time
memberPositions.evidence: Chair noted Michael seconded the request for an extension of time.

cases.name: 22 Whippoorwill Road East front-yard retaining wall
cases.applicant: owner/builder (Vladimir Levin, architect)
cases.summary: Review of a front-yard retaining wall and regrading that the owner had already begun building; the board was uneasy about the wall being constructed before approval but agreed it was likely the right solution and asked the applicant to return with site and landscape plans for a public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: Disconcerted the wall was built before approval but agrees the roughly 15% graded solution is appropriate
memberPositions.evidence: Chair questioned how the wall was being built without approval but acknowledged the six-foot-over-40-foot (15%) grade is not steep and is likely the right solution.

cases.name: Main Street building parking variance (CBA-2 district)
cases.applicant: George Calcutini (representing owner)
cases.summary: Applicant sought flexibility to allow any permitted CBA-2 use, effectively raising the parking variance from about 20 to 32 spaces so tenants would not need to return for amended approvals; the board was reluctant to shift the parking burden onto the street, pushed the idea of joining a future parking district, and recommended the applicant go to the ZBA for two additional apartment spaces.

memberPositions.stance: Reluctant to grant a large variance shifting parking to the street; favors conditioning on joining a parking district and sending applicant to the ZBA
memberPositions.evidence: Chair said the applicant is asking for a lot, that it seems unreasonable for the community to bear the added spaces, and steered toward a parking-district condition and a ZBA trip for two spaces.

memberPositions.stance: Suggested tabling the matter and sending the applicant to the ZBA for the two apartment spaces
memberPositions.evidence: The Chair referenced 'Roland's point' to table this and have the applicant go to the ZBA for the extra two spaces.

cases.name: 18 Carolyn Place additions and retaining wall
cases.applicant: homeowner (John Williams, Hierarch Design)
cases.summary: Proposed side additions, porches, patio resurfacing and regrading with an over-six-foot retaining wall; once it emerged the tall wall was existing rather than new, the board concluded the matter belonged at the RPRC with an administrative wetlands permit and referred it back, carrying over the submission.

memberPositions.stance: Concluded planning-board review was unnecessary and referred the application to the RPRC as the faster path
memberPositions.evidence: Chair reasoned the applicant could go to the RPRC with an administrative wetlands permit and be done faster, and directed the referral.

cases.name: 14 Middle Patent Road condition amendment
cases.applicant: applicant (Sarah O'Shea, attorney)
cases.summary: Applicant requested moving three conditions to be satisfied prior to the certificate of occupancy so the building permit could issue and construction proceed; with the building inspector's concurrence the board granted the change.
cases.publicComment: Applicant's attorney Sarah O'Shea explained the three conditions should become pre-CO conditions to allow the permit to issue and keep construction on schedule.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved to grant the change once the building inspector was satisfied
memberPositions.evidence: Chair said he had no problem as long as the building inspector was okay and moved to grant the change in the resolution.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge extension of time
cases.applicant: Eagle Ridge
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for Eagle Ridge, which is working through a brownfield designation for orchard-related soil before potentially advancing a different development.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved to grant the extension of time
memberPositions.evidence: Chair made the motion to grant the extension of time, noting the applicant is addressing the brownfield/orchard soil.

themes.note: Central to 9 Barnard, 22 Whippoorwill, 18 Carolyn and Massaro; recurring concern about over-height walls near property lines and tiered solutions.
Driveway/parking deficiencies at 12 Bedford Road and a 20-to-32 space variance request on Main Street drew board skepticism.
Board repeatedly declined to close hearings without full engineering, landscape and lighting submissions.
HES/Sterling coordination on fill sampling protocol dominated the 9 Barnard discussion; also relevant to Eagle Ridge brownfield.
Landscape/screening plans requested for 12 Bedford, 9 Barnard and 22 Whippoorwill.
Board routed the Main Street applicant back to the ZBA and referenced prior variance history across items.
Redirection to stormwater basins at the seminary and mitigation questions at 12 Bedford Road.
Neighbor opposition featured strongly at 12 Bedford Road and 9 Barnard.
12 Bedford Road's historic-district status and preservation intent shaped the driveway/landscaping debate.
Several items turned on whether the correct body was the planning board, RPRC or ZBA, with 18 Carolyn Place referred out.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the September 23 minutes and held public hearings on four residential/commercial applications: a mitigation site plan for 22 Whippoorwill Road East (approved with conditions for rear landscaping and an easement agreement), and new single-family homes at 88 and 86 Old Byram Lake Road (both approved with tree removal permits). The board also reviewed the Summit Club maintenance-building site plan, granted two extensions of time (Two Trip Lane and the Ken Place/Verizon parking plan), gave concept direction on a new home with a Cobbler-side driveway, and held a long, contentious continued discussion of the unpermitted retaining wall at 9 Barnard Road that ended at an impasse. A recording gap (~00:47-01:00) obscures the tail of the Summit Club hearing.

cases.name: 22 Whippoorwill Road East
cases.applicant: Vladimir Levin, MAP Architecture (architect)
cases.summary: Public hearing on revisions to an as-built house that was constructed taller and with a foundation wall instead of porch piers; the board approved a mitigation plan using a tiered retaining wall with heavy plantings, adding two conditions (additional rear-yard evergreen screening and memorializing the neighbor-side/easement planting).
cases.publicComment: Neighbors raised concerns: Amy Erenson (23 Anatale St, behind) worried about tree removal and loss of rear screening; Suzanne (25 Whippoorwill East, across) said the house sits too close to the road and questioned drainage and the electric meter location; a direct neighbor emailed objecting to the pool location and the earlier lack of notice.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of approval with mitigation conditions
memberPositions.evidence: Moved to adopt the draft resolution as amended with two conditions: additional rear planting and review of the easement/planting agreement.

memberPositions.stance: Engaged on wall facing, grade and street-side screening; supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned the existing retaining wall facing, the slope from wall to street, and cited elevation markers (405/406) on the south elevation.

cases.name: 88 Old Byram Lake Road (new single-family home)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer/representative)
cases.summary: Public hearing for a new five-bedroom single-family home and removal of 18 regulated trees on a five-acre lot from the Red Brook Glen subdivision; the board found the plan conforming to what was contemplated during the subdivision and approved the site plan and tree removal permit with conditions for wetland-buffer demarcation and a foundation landscaping plan.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke on this application.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to adopt the approval; supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed adopting the site development plan and tree removal permit approvals for 88 Old Byram Lake Road.

memberPositions.stance: Framed the lot as a conforming plan; supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Characterized it as a standard conforming plan consistent with what the board contemplated during the subdivision review.

cases.name: 86 Old Byram Lake Road (new single-family home)
cases.applicant: Ralph (applicant's engineer/representative)
cases.summary: Public hearing for a new five-bedroom home and removal of 23 regulated trees on an adjacent Red Brook Glen lot; the board approved the site plan and tree removal permit, discussing stormwater infiltration systems, existing screening to the neighbor, and boundary trees before adopting the resolution.
cases.publicComment: No public speakers noted; the town engineer (John) recommended directing stormwater to the rear infiltration system that discharges to the wetlands rather than the road.

memberPositions.stance: Read the notice and moved adoption; supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice and proposed adopting the site plan and tree removal permit approvals for 86 Old Byram Lake Road.

cases.name: Two Trip Lane (extension of time)
cases.summary: The board granted an additional three-month extension of time at the request of the building inspector, noting the applicant is due before the town board Wednesday.

cases.name: Summit Club maintenance building
cases.applicant: David Lombardi, JMC (professional engineer for the Summit Club)
cases.summary: Public hearing opened on a 7,220 sq ft maintenance building with chemical storage, fueling, and wash-water recycling as the next phase of the golf course redevelopment; the board discussed an off-street parking variance (shared-parking credit between the golf and residential parcels) and separation of chemical from petroleum storage. A recording gap obscures whether a vote was taken, though staff and members were favorable.

memberPositions.stance: Questioned the off-street parking variance, then satisfied by the explanation
memberPositions.evidence: Asked why the applicant needs an off-street parking variance from the ZBA and accepted that the same 65 spaces need not be duplicated at both the club and residential units.

memberPositions.stance: Viewed it as a low-impact maintenance facility; supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the maintenance facility is tucked behind the site with few site-planning issues and that fuel storage is between the engineer and building department.

memberPositions.stance: Pressed on separation of chemical from petroleum storage
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned whether the response addressed separation of the chemical storage from the petroleum storage and asked the professionals if it was satisfactory.

cases.name: New home concept - Cobbler-side driveway (High Street area)
cases.summary: Concept-level discussion of a new home where the board weighed driveway access from the Cobbler side versus High Street; given existing screening on the neighbor's property, the board directed the applicant to proceed developing the home with the Cobbler-side driveway and return with a refined landscaping and tree-removal plan.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of the Cobbler-side driveway; suggested shifting the driveway entrance
memberPositions.evidence: Noted existing screening on the neighbor's property makes the Cobbler driveway more doable and suggested shifting the driveway entrance to soften the slope.

memberPositions.stance: Directed applicant to proceed on the Cobbler side and perfect the plan
memberPositions.evidence: Gave direction that the applicant develop the home with the driveway on the Cobbler side as presented and return with the plan.

cases.name: 9 Barnard Road (unpermitted retaining wall)
cases.applicant: Anthony Gentile (owner); reps Andrew Broadnik, Paul Diamond, and surveyor Elliot Senor
cases.summary: Continued discussion of a stone retaining wall built without a permit (~150 ft long, a section over 6 ft, up to ~9 ft near the street). The board reiterated its 18-month-old April 2023 direction to step the existing wall back and cap it at four feet with a tiered second wall and plantings, while the applicant pushed a grade-and-bury alternative and ultimately declined to prepare new plans, asking the board to deny the six submitted plans. The board declined to issue denials (which would force fill removal) and left it at an impasse, with soil-contamination testing still outstanding.
cases.publicComment: The adjacent neighbor opposed clear-cutting and berming, wanting the wall stepped back to reduce the ~9 ft height she faces and disputing that she previously had water problems. Tom D'Agostino (40-year Barnard Road resident) objected to imported fill (estimating ~488 cubic yards), potential contamination, habitat loss from clear-cutting, and noted the watershed drains to Byram Brook; he was appalled at the applicant's Article 78 threat.

memberPositions.stance: Reiterated the step-back/regrade directive; skeptical of the applicant's bury-the-wall alternative but willing to see it
memberPositions.evidence: Directed the applicant to follow the April 2023 direction to step the wall back four feet and regrade, cautioning nothing had happened in 18 months.

memberPositions.stance: Preferred the tiered step-back wall; called the grading option convenient for the applicant, not the best
memberPositions.evidence: Said the grade-over-the-wall plan is convenient for the applicant but not necessarily the best solution and premised any wall solution on the fill/soil staying.

memberPositions.stance: Analyzed the six plans and endorsed the two-tier stepped-back wall; skeptical of burying the unpermitted wall
memberPositions.evidence: Walked through the wall heights/lengths and said the right approach is the tiered two-wall solution from the April 2023 minutes.

memberPositions.stance: Called the unpermitted wall the 'elephant in the room' the board never would have approved
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board is obsessing over finishing touches while the massive unpermitted structure is the real issue that never would have been approved as presented.

cases.name: Ken Place / Verizon parking plan (extension of time)
cases.applicant: Verizon
cases.summary: The board adopted the draft resolution granting an extension of time for the Ken Place Verizon parking plan as procedural closing business.

themes.note: Central to both 22 Whippoorwill (resolved via tiered mitigation) and the contentious 9 Barnard unpermitted wall.
Recurring across nearly every case; board frequently conditioned approvals on planting plans and rear/side screening.
Key unresolved gating issue at 9 Barnard; testing protocol agreed but not yet performed.
9 Barnard wall built without a permit; impasse with talk of denials and Article 78.
Infiltration systems at the Byram Lake lots and runoff/drainage complaints at 9 Barnard and 22 Whippoorwill.
Neighbors repeatedly cited lack of prior notice and impacts; board acknowledged it is reconsidering notification for future homes.
Byram Lake lots sit within conservation easements requiring buffer demarcation.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the October 7th minutes and reviewed four items: an addition/driveway project at 16 Davis Drive (Goodis residence) needing a gross land coverage variance and stormwater/wetland-buffer work, the Little Sparrows nursery school / Hillside Church site plan at 448 Bedford Road with open parking-count and lighting questions, and two extensions of time (263 Bedford-Banksville Road and the Summit Club subdivision). meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board opened and closed a public hearing for the 8 Coal Drive pool project (site plan, tree removal, steep slope and wetlands permits) and adopted a resolution approving it after favorable conservation board and engineer review. The board also recommended the town board proceed with a special use permit for the Gavi mixed-use/residential project, discussed the 130 Old Mount Kisco Road two-lot conservation subdivision and referred it (with a positive recommendation) to the ZBA pending a code interpretation on frontage, granted a three-month extension of time for 176 Virginia Road tied to a site-plan compliance dispute, and reached consensus to notice a neighbor/public hearing for a pool at 12 Dellwood Farm Way (Hammond Ridge). Several agenda items (9 Barnard Road, Leisure Farm Drive area, and another item) were removed or only briefly touched.

cases.name: Gavi - first-floor residential in commercial zone

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (Monday before Thanksgiving) approved the Little Sparrows Nursery School site plan at 448 Bedford Road with conditions, and handled a mix of introductions, referrals, and extensions. It heard a first introduction of a residential-to-commercial conversion at 154 Lafayette Avenue tangled up in code violations, reviewed a large recreational-amenities plan for the Shapiro residence at 8 Rosanne Drive (referred to the ZBA and conservation board, with sport-court lighting a flashpoint), and worked through fence/propane and pond-restoration matters at 88 Byron Ridge Road and 35 Whippoorwill Road. It granted extensions of time for 40 High Street and 113 King Street and spent extensive time on the contentious 'as-built' field-change request for the John's/Magnotta North Broadway shopping-center site plan, pushing the applicant to improve landscaping.

cases.name: Little Sparrows Nursery School (Hillside Church), 448 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Little Sparrows Nursery School / Hillside Church

memberPositions.stance: Wants a candid, comprehensive fix across all the owner's lots

meetings.meetingSummary: The Planning Board's final 2024 meeting worked through a light but full agenda. It approved an amended site plan for a pool/clearing-limit revision at 4 Leisure Farm Drive, approved the site plan for the office conversion at 12 Bedford Road, and re-approved the expired 32 Orchard Drive five-lot subdivision (neg dec plus preliminary and final). It kept the 47 High Street home-rebuild and the Gavi restaurant expansion hearings open, took up the new National Lawn Sprinkler flex-warehouse at 76 Virginia Road (declaring itself lead agency amid concerns over roughly 70 feet of rock excavation, retaining walls, and ~2,000 truck trips), reviewed parking and screening for the Breeze Mountain camp, and discussed the preliminary two-lot subdivision at 73 Whippoorwill Road.

cases.summary: A public hearing was opened and then immediately adjourned to the next meeting; the Chair indicated he would recuse himself and the board noted it was short-handed tonight.

32 Orchard re-approval and the third-lot/deed-restriction question at 73 Whippoorwill.

12 Bedford historic house approvals and Miller Hill Revolutionary-War county park adjacent to 76 Virginia Road.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board's first meeting of 2025 approved several residential applications: an amended clearing/grading limit line for a pool at 12 Delwood Farm (Chair recused), a site plan with tree, steep-slope and wetlands permits for a three-car garage at 16 Davis Drive, and a new-house site plan at 47 High Street (approved over one dissent amid heavy neighbor opposition to a driveway on Cobblers Lane). The board also discussed a wetlands mitigation/cleanup case at 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (held for a site walk and a February public hearing), adopted the resolution for the 15/22 apartment site plan, took a preliminary look at a mail-hauling business at 111 Lafayette Avenue, granted a subdivision time extension for Eagle Ridge, and debated a new 'procedural approvals' workflow.

memberPositions.stance: Confirmed the driveway grade and ADA/handicap parking slope comments were resolved
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the Kellard Sessions comments on driveway grade and handicap parking were addressed to satisfaction before voting.

memberPositions.stance: Seconded the motion to adopt the resolution
memberPositions.evidence: Seconded the Chair's motion to adopt the resolution for 15/22.

cases.name: 111 Lafayette Avenue - mail-hauling business office (preliminary site plan)
cases.applicant: Property owner operating a postal mail-hauling business
cases.summary: Preliminary discussion of converting the property into the main office/operations base for a bulk-mail hauling business; the board needed floor plans, truck-parking layout, storage and access details and directed the applicant to meet with the town planner and engineer before proceeding.

memberPositions.stance: Raised the application-processing-restrictions law regarding curing violations before proceeding
memberPositions.evidence: Asked the process question about the ordinance requiring violations to be cured before an application can move forward (planner noted it applies per-site).

memberPositions.stance: Directed the applicant to meet with the planner and town engineer and submit the required information

cases.name: Eagle Ridge - final subdivision extension of time

memberPositions.stance: Moved to approve the final subdivision extension of time
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to approve the extension of time for Eagle Ridge.

themes.note: Central to 16 Davis Drive; infiltration pond, dry wells and trench drains framed as improving longstanding runoff onto neighbors.
Dominated 47 High Street; strong neighbor opposition to a Cobblers Lane driveway over visibility and safety, one board dissent.
92/94 Round Hill 2-to-1 mitigation and monitoring; buffer restoration also at 16 Davis and 12 Delwood.
Arborvitae screening at 16 Davis, tree counts at 12 Delwood, planting/mitigation at Round Hill.
Debris/fuel-shed cleanup drove the board to hold Round Hill open; violations discussion at 111 Lafayette.
Steep-slope permits and regrading at 16 Davis and 12 Delwood; driveway grade at 15/22 and 47 High Street.
