Outstanding full-cutoff parking-lot lighting plan condition at 15/22.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board (three members present) approved the January 13th minutes and handled four items: a first site-plan review of a house expansion/rehab at 700 Bedford Road (referred to the ZBA and ARB), a zoning text-amendment referral for 23 Bedford Banksville Road recommending rezoning to the more restrictive CBB district (positive referral, 3-0), a restart of the expired single-family-house approval at Forge Legewood (board agreed to schedule a new public hearing), and a Summer Club subdivision request for an extension of time plus early tree removal of 72 trees for marketing purposes (both supported). The meeting was largely procedural and cooperative.

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road house expansion/rehab
cases.applicant: Joseph Casiotas (owner), represented by Elvis of Delhi Engineering
cases.summary: First appearance before the Planning Board for a vertical and horizontal expansion (about 5,000 sq ft) of an existing single-family house plus a carriage house; the board reviewed site-plan, drainage/curb-cut and landscaping comments and referred the applicant to the ZBA (setback variance for the carriage house) and the ARB before returning.

memberPositions.stance: supportive, steered applicant to ZBA and ARB and encouraged the improved design
memberPositions.evidence: Guided next steps to ZBA/ARB and closed with 'Congratulations. Good luck with it.'

memberPositions.stance: curious/neutral about the demolition and scope of the project
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the house was 'totally gone right now, you guys leveled it,' noting he drives past it daily.

cases.name: 23 Bedford Banksville Road zoning text amendment
cases.summary: The town board sent back draft language to rezone the property to CBB instead of GB (to bar the more intensive warehouse/self-storage use), and the Planning Board discussed whether narrowing permitted uses could have unintended consequences before making a positive referral back to the town board, 3-0.

memberPositions.stance: reluctant, worried the CBB change would preclude reasonable future uses like high-end car storage and create unintended consequences
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was 'a little reluctant,' warned of unintended consequences, and questioned whether a gated high-end auto-storage use would be wrongly precluded.

memberPositions.stance: pragmatic and supportive; a future beneficial use could always petition for another zoning change
memberPositions.evidence: 'If there becomes a use that makes a lot of sense and is neighbor friendly... they can always petition for another change.'

memberPositions.stance: facilitated the discussion and summarized that the change further restricts permitted uses
memberPositions.evidence: Restated the sentiment that the amendment would 'further restrict the types of uses' and moved the item to a vote.

cases.name: Forge Legewood single-family house (expired approval restart)
cases.summary: A previously approved new single-family house whose resolution had expired; the applicant was told not to attend, and the board agreed to schedule a new public hearing and re-approve, discussing new practice of addressing conditions before signing and revisiting the phased planting/tree-replacement plan in the wetland buffer.

memberPositions.stance: gave the board's blessing to schedule the hearing and re-approve since nothing in the plans had changed
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed to open the hearing but not close it until conditions are addressed prior to signing.

cases.name: Summer Club subdivision - extension of time and tree removal
cases.applicant: Summer Club subdivision applicant
cases.summary: The board supported the applicant's request to remove 72 interior trees early (before building permits) for marketing/staging of the first phase of townhouses, with stump grinding and wood-chip stabilization, and separately granted a 90-day extension of time for the final subdivision plat while health-department (sewage, water withdrawal/system) approvals are pending.

memberPositions.stance: cautious about early tree clearing setting a precedent and leaving a cleared site if the project stalls, but ultimately understanding
memberPositions.evidence: 'There is a worry... they get started early... tree clearing... and then something happens' and 'I just worry about setting a precedent.'

memberPositions.stance: inclined to help the applicant; the trees would come down anyway and the request is reasonable
memberPositions.evidence: 'I'm inclined to help them out. I don't think the applicant would ask just to take three trees down.'

memberPositions.stance: supportive of accommodating the applicant while confirming the trees would be removed regardless and stabilization would occur
memberPositions.evidence: Framed the issue as one of timing and moved the tree-removal support and extension motions to votes.

themes.note: Most items were procedural steps rather than substantive hearings.
Early removal of 72 trees at Summer Club and prior removal/replanting at Forge Legewood.
GB vs CBB text amendment for 23 Bedford Banksville Road drew debate over unintended consequences.
Board discussed its newer practice of requiring conditions addressed before the chair signs plans.
Raised at 700 Bedford Road (likely not needed) and Forge Legewood buffer disturbance.
Grading, erosion control and drainage comments on the 700 Bedford Road site plan.
Summer Club extension driven by long-pending sewage and water approvals.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the January 27 minutes and worked through a full agenda of public hearings and referrals, spending significant time debating a new procedure to 'tighten up' resolutions so applicants do not leave with approvals that still carry many unmet conditions. It approved a special use permit for an accessory apartment at 298 Bedford Banksville Road and granted extensions of time for 124 Old Mount Kisco Road and 40 High Street. Several subdivisions (130 Old Mount Kisco Road, 73 Whippoorwill Road) were held open for plan revisions and condition cleanup, the contentious 92/94 Round Hill Road golf-green and pool application drew heavy neighbor opposition and was kept open pending research, a utility-burial waiver at 4 Alpine Drive was effectively refused, an outdoor container-storage request at 200 Business Park Drive was discouraged, and 76 Byron Ridge Road was referred to the Conservation Board.

cases.name: 4 Ledgewood Place - re-approval of expired residence site plan
cases.applicant: 4 Ledgewood Place LLC
cases.summary: Public hearing for re-approval of an expired site plan, wetlands permit, and tree removal approvals for a new four-bedroom residence; with no public present the board declined to vote on the resolution because 17 conditions remain unsatisfied, opting instead to have the applicant address them with staff and return for administrative approval.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared for this application.

memberPositions.stance: Won't sign off on resolutions with many outstanding items; have applicant address conditions first
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the board decided not to approve resolutions with a significant amount of outstanding items and that the applicant should get them done and come back.

memberPositions.stance: Was inclined to look past it since previously approved, but agreed with Ruisi's procedural approach
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was looking past the open items because it had been pre-approved but was amenable and agreed to give the new procedure a try.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to approve the updated resolution before the procedural concern was raised
memberPositions.evidence: Moved to approve the updated resolution for construction of the residence at 4 Ledgewood Place.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious about delaying applicants but willing to try the new procedure
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was ingrained in the old ways and did not want to be onerous or throw roadblocks at applicants.

cases.name: 298 Bedford Banksville Road - accessory apartment special use permit
cases.summary: Public hearing on a special use permit to legalize a detached accessory apartment in a structure previously approved as an office; the required ZBA variance had been obtained, the board found the resolution concise, and it approved the special use permit subject to a water test and showing required parking.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared for this application.

memberPositions.stance: Moved to approve the special use permit
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to approve the special use permit for the accessory apartment at 298 Bedford Banksville Road.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; noted the office use struck him as more inconsistent with zoning than the apartment
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned why the variance was needed and remarked the prior approved office seemed more inconsistent with the zoning than the accessory apartment.

cases.name: 130 Old Mount Kisco Road - conservation subdivision
cases.applicant: Frank Madonna
cases.summary: Public hearing on a conservation subdivision of an oversized, steep mountainside lot with a conservation easement placed over the mountainside; a neighbor raised drought and well-water concerns, and the board directed the applicant to revise the conservation-easement line (to let a future buyer add a pool) and resubmit, keeping the hearing open.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor Robin Lovell (environmental scientist) raised concerns about drought and well/drinking-water capacity, saying she had to deepen her well; the applicant's engineer said the Westchester County Health Department has jurisdiction over the single proposed new well. Another attendee asked about construction timing, staging, and fill.

memberPositions.stance: Favors the conservation layout over the conventional one; open to redrawing the easement line for a pool
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the conventional subdivision would be far more environmentally concerning and directed the applicant to redraw and resubmit the conservation line to allow a pool.

memberPositions.stance: Pressed for clarity on the plan (garage/house depiction) and the combined acreage
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned the integrated plot plan about the garage and house locations and confirmed the 3.2-acre parcel comprises lot one, lot two, and the conservation easement.

cases.name: 124 Old Mount Kisco Road - extension of time
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for this application after the applicant's engineer submitted materials the same day.

cases.name: 40 High Street - extension of time
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for this application, which is awaiting review at the county Health Department.

cases.name: 73 Whippoorwill Road - two-lot subdivision
cases.applicant: Wellness Estates LLC (Alex Geske)
cases.summary: Public hearing on subdividing an 8.8-acre lot into a 5.5-acre Lot A and a 3.3-acre Lot B; the applicant's engineer addressed the 11 staff comments (school-bus pickup area, road-widening reservation, no-further-subdivision note, archaeological survey), the board kept site-plan jurisdiction over future development, and it asked the applicant to tighten the 21-condition resolution for later administrative approval.
cases.publicComment: One neighbor from across the street, who received the hearing notice, asked that the developers keep the existing view in mind; the board explained a condition requires the future house to return for site-plan review with public notice.

memberPositions.stance: Asked two resolution questions (contiguous vs. contagious typo; scope of the archaeological survey condition) and questioned the number labeling
memberPositions.evidence: Flagged the 'contagious/contiguous' typo and asked that the archaeological-survey condition note that further compliance beyond a survey may be required depending on results.

memberPositions.stance: Wanted the board to retain site-plan jurisdiction over the future house
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the application should come back to the planning board for site-plan adjudication rather than proceeding straight to the RPRC.

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable with the subdivision; wants the resolution cleaned up before voting
memberPositions.evidence: Told the applicant to take the resolution home and button it up so the later vote would be cleaner, and noted a house-numbering point (room for a 71).

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road - golf green, tees and pool renovation
cases.applicant: Michael Lehrer / Round Hill Landco
cases.summary: Combined public hearing on site plan, wetlands, and tree-removal permits for a golf green/tees on 92 and a pool renovation and access path on 94, following a building-department violation for pool work and path creation without permits; multiple neighbors and two attorneys objected on safety, wetlands, tree-clearing, and commercial-use grounds, and after an executive session the board kept the hearing open and asked staff to research the approval history while the applicant addresses neighbor concerns.
cases.publicComment: Strong neighbor opposition: Kalindi Bah (98 Round Hill, since 1990) cited wetland disturbance, chlorine/chemical runoff, wildlife harm, encroachment/tree-felling, and lack of pool fencing near grandchildren; attorney Jennifer Gray for Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill) argued the golf tees are not a permitted accessory use, violate setbacks, endanger his glass-walled home with errant balls, and raised SEQRA segmentation concerns; Edelman detailed safety, privacy (a $16,000 split-rail fence removed without consent), and environmental worries; Anthony Pippo and Robert (100 Round Hill) raised noise, tree-clearing of ~1.5 acres, bonfires, a long-standing dumpster, and fears of commercialization; another neighbor worried about the property becoming a commercial showcase.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical; sees legitimate neighbor concerns, worries about safety and commercial-scale use, wants approval history researched
memberPositions.evidence: Said the neighbors have very legitimate concerns, that four tees seem to cross from residential toward commercial use, and directed staff to research the file history while leaving the hearing open.

memberPositions.stance: Focused on the 'gating' legality question - whether the green/tees required a permit or approval and whether they are a lawful accessory use
memberPositions.evidence: Called the permitting/legality of the green a gating factor and asked town counsel for input on the legality and process.

memberPositions.stance: Probed the outstanding citation and wanted existing conditions compared to the approved site plan
memberPositions.evidence: Asked about the nature of the citation and said he was curious how existing conditions stack up against the approved site plan.

cases.name: 4 Alpine Drive - utility burial waiver request
cases.applicant: Dave Cicarni
cases.summary: The applicant sought relief from Town Code 355-17 requiring new utility service to be placed underground, wanting instead to run overhead wires from a pole he had already erected across the street; despite sympathy for his practical and cost arguments, the board found no basis (no hardship, no precedent) to waive the statute and the town engineer remained firm that the service must go underground.
cases.publicComment: The applicant Dave Cicarni argued the neighborhood is entirely overhead-wired, that his pole is set ~20 feet onto his property, and that no future situation would require another over-street crossing.

memberPositions.stance: Sympathetic to the applicant but feels bound by the statute; found no hardship or precedent to grant relief
memberPositions.evidence: Said he tried to find relief and agreed with the applicant's logic but could not simply disregard a legitimate town statute with no precedent to waive it.

memberPositions.stance: Suggested boring under the road as a possible alternative to trenching the pavement
memberPositions.evidence: Raised the option of boring under the ground rather than ripping up the recently paved street.

cases.name: 200 Business Park Drive - outdoor storage of construction trailers
cases.applicant: PTSD Northeast
cases.summary: With the applicant absent, the board discussed a request by a healthcare-construction firm to store 40-yard containers/trailers behind a professional office building; citing extensive prior outdoor-storage concerns in that area, members were strongly disinclined to allow containers and suggested the applicant instead propose an enclosed structure meeting setbacks, parking, and FAR.

memberPositions.stance: Opposed to outdoor container storage; suggested the applicant present an enclosed structure instead
memberPositions.evidence: Said he could not imagine the board entertaining the container-storage application and suggested an outdoor structure/garage as an alternative.

memberPositions.stance: Against containers; noted a structure would still have to meet setbacks, parking, and FAR
memberPositions.evidence: Said putting containers out there is not a good idea in any shape or form and that a structure would need setbacks, parking, and FAR.

cases.name: 76 Byron Ridge Road - Lizzero residence expansion in wetland buffer
cases.applicant: Lizzero
cases.summary: Referred from the RPRC, this expansion of an existing lakeside house sits partly in a state-regulated wetland buffer; the engineer described the septic (a county no-objection letter was sought), stormwater Cultec chambers and a rain garden, a wetland mitigation/planting plan, and a reworked driveway with screening, and the board referred the application to the Conservation Board while asking that all resolution conditions be addressed promptly.

memberPositions.stance: Generally receptive but concerned about the lakeside area and driveway; wants Conservation Board input
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned the lawn-to-naturalized ratio near the lake and whether the house could be relocated, then directed the application to the Conservation Board.

memberPositions.stance: Probed stormwater treatment and the floor-area calculation
memberPositions.evidence: Asked where the water goes after the Cultec system and whether it is filtered before reaching the lake, and questioned the added floor area figure.

themes.note: Recurring debate across multiple items about tightening resolutions so applicants don't leave with approvals carrying many unmet conditions.
Central to Round Hill, Byron Ridge, Old Mount Kisco, and Ledgewood; frequent mitigation and buffer concerns.
Heavy neighbor opposition at Round Hill and a view concern at Whippoorwill.
Multiple subdivision items including a conservation subdivision and a straightforward two-lot split.
Whether backyard golf tees/greens are a permitted accessory use and the errant-ball safety risk dominated the Round Hill hearing.
Board sought to retain site-plan review over future development at Whippoorwill and the conservation subdivision.
Cultec chambers, rain gardens, and runoff treatment discussed at Byron Ridge and referenced elsewhere.
County Health Department jurisdiction, drought/well capacity, and septic continuation raised at several properties.
Tree-removal permits and unauthorized clearing (notably at Round Hill) recurred.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board held two public hearings and reviewed several site plan and extension items. The board reached an impasse on the long-running 9 Barnard Road wall-legalization application and directed a resolution of denial, then re-approved the 2 Massaro Court lot line change for a third time. It also discussed the Whippoorwill Club tree removal (scheduling a site visit and hearing), the Shapiro sport-court/lighting site plan, and a large rock-excavation warehouse proposal at 76 Virginia Road (referred to the ZBA for an FAR variance), and granted routine time extensions for 215 Business Park Drive, 12 Maple Avenue, and the airport campus project.

cases.name: 9 Barnard Road wall/fill legalization
cases.applicant: represented by Leno Sherretta (Blakely Plattenschmitt) and engineer Paul Diamond
cases.summary: Public hearing on legalizing an existing ~7-year-old unpermitted wall, fill, grading, tree removal and shed; the applicant proposed adding ~8 cubic yards of fill and four trees to lower the wall exposure below six feet rather than tiering it. The board rejected this, found itself at an impasse because the applicant refused to tier/reduce the wall as previously directed, closed the public hearing, and directed staff to prepare a resolution of denial for the next meeting.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors opposed. Tom Dagestino (13 Barnard Rd) urged denial unless the wall is reduced 4 feet and tiered per prior board direction. Aurora Banisak (11 Barnard Rd) described severe basement flooding, drainage redirected onto her property, septic damage, and construction debris in the fill since the 2016 site stripping, arguing landscaping does not fix the unpermitted wall.

memberPositions.stance: Strongly opposed; wall should be reduced and tiered, not kept
memberPositions.evidence: Called the wall 'an abomination' for the neighbor, said the applicant ignored code and never did required testing, and would not support any solution that keeps the wall.

memberPositions.stance: Opposed; backfilling to claim lower height is a contrived solution
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board must judge it as if nothing was built, the wall should be tiered/set back, and backfilling the base is 'a contrived solution' that changes nothing about height, drainage or neighborhood impact.

memberPositions.stance: Opposed to the plan as submitted
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed Larry and Michael said it well and stated he 'would not be in favor of moving this.'

memberPositions.stance: Opposed; never received the requested tiered plan, concerned about stormwater
memberPositions.evidence: Wanted to see the tiered/lowered-wall plan requested since April 2023 and voiced concern about stormwater runoff and a pipe daylighting onto the neighbor's property.

memberPositions.stance: Chair; declared an impasse and moved toward denial
memberPositions.evidence: Said the board was never presented an adequate plan, is at an impasse, and is in a position to deny the site plan; closed the public hearing and directed a resolution of denial.

cases.name: 2 Massaro Court lot line change
cases.applicant: represented by Nick Lishari, Hudson Engineering
cases.summary: Public hearing on a previously approved lot line change (no new lots) whose approvals had twice expired; the board held the hearing with no public present and re-approved it a third time, passing the negative declaration, preliminary and final subdivision plat resolutions so the plat can be signed and two-family houses built.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; read the hearing notice and confirmed no substantive changes
memberPositions.evidence: Read the notice of public hearing and questioned whether any regulations had changed or conditions rose to a level requiring amendment, concluding it was essentially the same plan.

cases.name: Whippoorwill Club tree removal, 148 Whippoorwill Road
cases.applicant: Whippoorwill Club, represented by Jim Ryan (formerly JMC) and superintendent Paul Gonzalez
cases.summary: The club sought approval to remove 54 trees (37 near holes 15 and 16) as part of a course restoration, plus removal of two trees within a man-made pond's wetland buffer. The board asked to see the site before deciding, scheduled a Wednesday site visit and set a public hearing for the March 24 meeting; the two buffer trees could be handled administratively if deemed minor wetlands.
cases.publicComment: Neighbors Andrew Schaffler (5 Meadow Hill Place) and Brian Blum (1 Meadow Place), whose yards back onto holes 15 and 16, welcomed the added replantings but argued ~8 replacement trees for 37 removed is insufficient, raised downhill flooding fears from tree loss, and asked that new evergreens be placed where they get enough sunlight and screen their properties.

memberPositions.stance: Chair; wants a site visit before acting, focused on holes 15/16 near neighbors
memberPositions.evidence: Said holes 15 and 16 concern him due to proximity to neighboring properties and that the best way to understand impacts is to go out and see the marked trees.

memberPositions.stance: Recused due to a conflict
memberPositions.evidence: Stated he had a conflict and recused himself from discussion and any vote, turning his camera off for the item.

cases.name: Shapiro residence sport courts, 8 Rolling Drive
cases.applicant: represented by Cory Salomon (Zarin & Steinman), Paul Sci-Sack (JMC), architect Matt Barenz, lighting expert Steven Ballow
cases.summary: Continued discussion of proposed tennis, padel and turf sport courts plus an activity building on a 17+ acre property, with ARB, conservation and zoning board sign-offs in hand. The central issue was court lighting; the applicant's lighting expert described dark-sky, house-side-shielded fixtures with no light trespass past 50 feet, and the board asked for a method to verify performance after installation before setting a public hearing next month.

memberPositions.stance: Cautiously receptive but wants post-installation verification of lighting
memberPositions.evidence: Asked that if approval is based on lighting representations, there be a review or test after installation to confirm the leakage/light levels actually match what was proposed.

memberPositions.stance: Chair; supportive of the plan but wants accountability on lighting claims
memberPositions.evidence: Called it a beautiful plan on a gorgeous property, agreed it is well screened, and framed the task as creating accountability between the lighting representations and reality before the hearing.

cases.name: 215 Business Park Drive extension (former CarQuest warehouse)
cases.summary: The board granted a routine one-year extension of time for a previously approved ~45,000 sq ft warehouse/office addition (original 2017 approval), noting the approval has now been extended for roughly six years and that new DEC stormwater work will be required.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road, National Law/Sprinkler warehouse & office
cases.applicant: National Law (John Luciano), represented by attorney Tony Vinesiano and engineer Daniel Gomez (SES)
cases.summary: Discussion of a new warehouse/office complex on a vacant rock-outcrop lot requiring a large rock cut (~30,000+ cubic yards), anchored/gunite-stabilized walls up to 60 feet, and stormwater detention. The board raised concerns about FAR (interior warehouse parking counting as floor area), the scale and duration of excavation, blasting vs chipping, and mid-job stoppage risk; it referred the FAR variance to the Zoning Board of Appeals and asked for a full construction/excavation/geotechnical package.
cases.publicComment: Vincent Gardiano, the conservation board representative and a civil engineer, offered technical input on the top-down supported-excavation sequence (gunite, tie-backs) and noted blasting can be faster and safer than prolonged chipping; not a formal objection.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical of the scale; questions why so much excavation for this site
memberPositions.evidence: Said he keeps asking 'why here,' that the amount of work and moving 30,000 yards of rock 'seems overwhelming for the area' and overpowers the existing topography.

memberPositions.stance: Concerned the excavation could stall mid-job and leave a dangerous unfinished cut
memberPositions.evidence: Raised that other town projects started excavation and never finished, and worried this rock cut could proceed slowly or pause, given it is a different skill set from the applicant's core business.

memberPositions.stance: Chair; open but wants a construction/excavation plan and enforceable timeframe
memberPositions.evidence: Stressed a mid-job stoppage would be dangerous, pressed for a schedule, penalties and geotechnical/engineering plan, and moved to refer the FAR variance to the ZBA.

memberPositions.stance: Engaged; told applicant the board needs the full construction package
memberPositions.evidence: Chair addressed him confirming the applicant heard the board's request for construction, excavation, geotechnical and landscaping plans before proceeding.

cases.name: 12 Maple Avenue site plan modification & extension
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time together with a field-change notification for a facade modification (fewer windows, metal roof extended to the building edge, and photochromatic skylights) that had already been reviewed by the ARB.

memberPositions.stance: No comment on the change; had voted against the plan previously
memberPositions.evidence: Chair reminded him he voted against the plan last time; Larry said he had nothing to add and participated in the vote.

cases.name: Airport campus project extensions
cases.applicant: represented by Max Millie (Cuddy & Feder)
cases.summary: The board granted a standard 90-day subdivision extension and a one-year site plan approval extension for the airport campus project while staff finishes reviewing the filed subdivision and site plans for signature.

themes.note: Dominant topic via the 9 Barnard Road impasse and the 76 Virginia Road stabilized rock-cut walls.
Central to 9 Barnard neighbor flooding complaints and to 76 Virginia detention/runoff design.
76 Virginia Road's large rock cut raised concerns about scale, duration and safety.
Whippoorwill Club's 54-tree course restoration; board deferred pending site visit.
Board reluctant to reward after-the-fact work at 9 Barnard Road.
Routine grants for 2 Massaro, 215 Business Park, 12 Maple Ave and the airport campus.
Key issue for the Shapiro sport courts; board wants post-installation verification.
Two buffer trees at Whippoorwill and wetland setback at the Shapiro property.
76 Virginia interior warehouse parking counts as floor area, referred to ZBA.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the March 10 minutes and then worked through two reopened public hearings and several other items. Most of the meeting focused on 92 and 94 Round Hill Road (backyard golf greens/tees built in a wetland buffer, whose applicant failed to appear) and Whippoorwill Club (tree removal and a raised tee box on holes 15/16), both of which drew strong neighbor opposition and were adjourned with the hearings held open. The board also adopted a resolution for 9 Barnard Road, took up the Goldman pool at 15 Stony Brook Place, referred a mail-truck parking application to the ZBA, made a positive special-permit recommendation and granted a site-plan extension for 23 Bedford-Banksville Road, and granted an extension of time for 111 Round Hill Road.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road (backyard golf greens/tees)
cases.applicant: property owner (Lehrer/Ware) - representative did not appear
cases.summary: The reopened public hearing proceeded even though the applicant's representative failed to appear and the application had not changed since the last meeting; neighbors reiterated safety and wetland concerns and the board discussed how to constrain the greens and tees before adjourning the hearing.
cases.publicComment: Attorney Jennifer Gray (for the Aetalmans/Beydlemans at 88 Round Hill) and neighbors from 98 and 100 Round Hill strongly objected: golf tees are a lethal safety hazard near homes, kids and the road; the 1999 permit referenced greens not tees; the use may exceed a customary/incidental accessory use; the work is already built as a flagrant violation; and the wetland is being degraded by wide cleared paths and heavy equipment.

memberPositions.stance: Deeply concerned about safety; questions whether hitting golf balls this close to neighbors should be allowed at all
memberPositions.evidence: Said he finds it hard to believe the board would allow a permitted use that puts a green right against a neighbor's property and that the safety factor makes him ask whether it is in the town's and neighbors' best interest to let this exist.

memberPositions.stance: Wants the previously approved site plans as a baseline to quantify what changed; skeptical the use is truly accessory given its scale
memberPositions.evidence: Asked for the approved site plans to compare against existing conditions to quantify variations, and argued that a use consuming an entire open acre and its scope/scale can convert an otherwise accessory use into a predominant one.

memberPositions.stance: Pragmatic; thinks the fix belongs in the site plan rather than policing behavior, and notes the building inspector deems it a permitted accessory use
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the tees being present or not is more behavioral than real and won't necessarily change the outcome, and reported the building inspector interprets this as a permitted accessory use customary to a single-family house.

memberPositions.stance: Seeking a workable solution; wants greens to comply with the side yard setback and was disappointed the applicant did not appear
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed that at minimum the greens should respect the side yard setback and said he would tell the applicant's representative it was very disappointing to skip a public hearing when neighbors showed up.

cases.name: Whippoorwill Club, 148 Whippoorwill Road (holes 15/16 tree removal and raised tee box)
cases.applicant: Whippoorwill Club (rep. James Ryan; engineer Anthony Nestor, JMC)
cases.summary: The club presented revised plans to remove trees and add a raised 16th tee box, sand trap and screening plantings, but the board directed it to submit a comprehensive amended site plan (with elevations and fill quantities) before approval and adjourned the hearing held open.
cases.publicComment: Abutting neighbors Andrew Schaffler (5 Metal Hill Place) and Brian Blum (1 Metal Hill Place) opposed the scope: 70-80 trees really coming down, a raised tee box moved ~100 ft closer causing noise and privacy loss, runoff risk, and mislabeling it 'restoration'; they urged a fuller plan and one-for-one tree replacement. cases.name: 9 Barnard Road

meetings.meetingSummary: The April 14, 2025 North Castle Planning Board meeting opened by honoring retiring long-serving member Jim Jensen, leaving a four-member board. It approved Oamic Ingredients' amended site plan for its chemical warehouse at 6 Leviola Court and approved a conservation subdivision at 130 Old Mount Kisco Road, and granted a time extension for Eagle Ridge. It held open a contentious public hearing for the Roseann Drive (Bracemont) estate over lit tennis and padel courts, with the board largely opposed to the lighting and neighbors objecting to noise and light. It also discussed the 76 Virginia Road warehouse requiring a major rock cut, deciding the town should hire its own geotechnical engineer, referred a 28 Lock autobody solar/addition to the ZBA, and referred a pool at 18 Long Pond Road (Novick) to the Conservation Board.

cases.name: Oamic Ingredients amended site plan, 6 Leviola Court
cases.applicant: Oamic Ingredients (Nella Morad)
cases.summary: The board held and closed the public hearing on an amended site plan renewing/finalizing a previously approved 2022 resolution for a flavor-and-fragrance chemical warehouse and distribution use; after confirming no changes to approved chemicals or quantities, it adopted a negative declaration and the resolution.

memberPositions.stance: Optimistic and supportive; wanted assurance the operating plan is kept current

memberPositions.stance: Supportive but pressed that stored chemicals cannot vary from what was already approved
memberPositions.evidence: Insisted the SDS sheets and chemicals must match the approved list, then moved to accept the negative declaration for the Oamic application.

cases.name: Bracemont estate, 8 Roseann Drive

cases.publicComment: Multiple neighbors (Tony Alexander of 2 Perry Court, Bill O'Brien of 61 Cox, Francesca Milano of 21 Byron Lake, Katija Papewala of Byron Lake) opposed the project, citing noise from tennis play, light visibility across Byron Lake, loss of quiet/bucolic enjoyment, wetlands disturbance, and lack of enforceable time limits.

memberPositions.evidence: Questioned why anyone needs to play at 9 p.m. and raised noise pollution when the community is trying to rest, while acknowledging it is an exceptional 18-acre property.

memberPositions.evidence: Said the marginal benefit to the homeowner is outweighed by the detriment to the community from light and evening noise, though the tennis court itself is a permitted use.

memberPositions.stance: Not supportive of the lighting; agreed with the other members

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable moving the subdivision ahead
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was comfortable moving this ahead and made the motions to adopt the negative declaration and subdivision resolutions.

memberPositions.evidence: Warned it is on the applicant to document the roughly 81-year-old easement and asked whether the reduced lot area still yields satisfactory GLC and FAR.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; seconded the negative declaration
memberPositions.evidence: Seconded the motion to adopt the negative declaration for the subdivision.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge subdivision (time extension)

cases.name: National Alarm/Sprinklers warehouse, 76 Virginia Road

cases.publicComment: Hill/Miller Park residents (including Pam Feddowich) raised concerns about destabilizing the hill, blasting vibration harming homes, and Miller Hill's Revolutionary War historic significance; residents asked whether they could also hire their own engineer.

memberPositions.evidence: Put on his 'old business hat' and called the rock work overkill, noting the building would be surrounded by three walls of rock.

cases.name: Autobody shop solar and rear addition, 28 Lock

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board reviewed eight applications plus routine business on April 28, 2025. The dominant item was a continued public hearing on the Whippoorwill Country Club amended site plan and tree-removal permit, where neighbors and the Conservation Board strongly opposed removing roughly 54 trees near the 15th and 16th holes; the hearing was kept open. The Sankar residence wetlands/pool-legalization hearing was closed but no resolution was adopted pending outstanding conditions. The board referred three residential projects (1613 Old Orchard, 50 East Middle Patent, 167 Miamis River Road) to the Zoning Board of Appeals, discussed several other items needing more information, and granted a Summer Club time extension.

cases.name: Sankar residence, 26 Carillon Place

memberPositions.evidence: Said the board wants all conditions addressed and a clean resolution to come back before they approve it.

memberPositions.stance: Comfortable that pool screening is intact
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the screening for the pool is intact and he had no problem with that aspect.

cases.publicComment: Neighbors Brian Blum (1 Meadow Hill Place) and Andrew Shafler (5 Meadow Hill Place) argued the tree removal was unnecessary and alternatives (shifting tee boxes/sand trap) were not considered; Bob Colton urged one-for-one or greater tree replacement; Vince Ferrandino of the Conservation Board called the trees significant and stressed proper native-species mitigation and canopy spacing. The club's Steve Russell (grounds committee) defended removing the cart path as a major reduction in disturbance.

memberPositions.stance: Deferred to hearing neighbor input before commenting
memberPositions.evidence: When asked if he wanted to raise anything, said he would rather hear from the neighbors first.

memberPositions.stance: Wants a comprehensive plan for all three parcels and violations resolved before proceeding

memberPositions.evidence: Recalled it as a beautiful, unique piece of property and asked whether the footprint stays the same.

memberPositions.evidence: Made the recommendation/motion to send the applicant to the ZBA.

The board also approved prior minutes and adjourned.

meetings.meetingSummary: The board opened with an informational presentation by Westchester County Airport Advisory Board chair Nick Hartman (introduced by member Michael Pollack) on the environmental and safety concerns of building dense residential development near the county airport. It then held a public hearing and approved a site plan for a day camp at 60 Cox Avenue, and reopened/closed a public hearing and approved an amended site plan and tree-removal permit for the Whippoorwill Club at 148 Whippoorwill Road. Several other items were advanced in discussion (a pool/garage at 12 Seymour Place East referred to the ZBA, a pool-in-buffer application by Goldman and an accessory-apartment remodel of the Sauro residence at 8 Lions Road both moving toward public hearings, and a canopy/loading-dock plan for U-Haul at 1 Virginia Road), and extensions of time were granted for 40 High Street and the 45 Bedford Road Gateway residential project.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of the improvement; questioned mandatory ARB review and raised sidewalk gaps
memberPositions.evidence: Called the rear work a great improvement and asked whether the board had discretion to waive ARB for such a minor commercial project, suggesting the town board could grant that discretion.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board held two public hearings and several discussion items. It granted conditional site-plan approval for a US mail-contractor's truck-parking/warehouse use at 111 Lafayette Avenue and approved the rebuild of a condemned house at 50 East Middle Patent Road. It approved a 10-week rock-crushing permit at 111 Round Hill Road over one dissent, reached a consensus against an amended curb-cut request at 75 Hickory Kingdom Road (to proceed via public hearing toward likely denial), reviewed progress on 12 Seymour Place East and 700 Bedford Road, and discussed town policy on overhead vs. underground electric service affecting 4 Alpine and 21 Wood Wool Road.

cases.name: 111 Lafayette Avenue - US mail logistics truck parking/warehouse
cases.applicant: US mail contractor / logistics company owner (name not stated)
cases.summary: Public hearing on a site plan to allow overnight commercial truck parking accessory to a warehouse/office building; the board worked through the parking table (9 office spaces required, 15 truck spaces, 24 provided), closed the hearing, and approved the resolution as amended to add conditions for a replacement fence and code-compliant lighting, plus floor plans to support the parking count.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke; the applicant and property owner presented and answered questions.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; treated overnight truck parking as reasonable incidental use of the warehouse and moved approval
memberPositions.evidence: Characterized the warehouse as the driving use with office incidental and moved to approve the resolution as amended to include the fence and lighting conditions.

memberPositions.stance: Constructive; pressed to reconcile the parking table numbers
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether the 24 total spaces included the 15 trucks and clarified that roughly 9 spaces are required while 24 are provided.

memberPositions.stance: Cautious but ultimately comfortable; flagged the no-exterior-lighting note

cases.name: 50 East Middle Patent Road - reconstruction of condemned house

cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke on the application.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; viewed it as a straightforward application
memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'as simple as they get' and confirmed the three-foot-higher structure still meets height requirements.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; moved approval
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was 'good' with the application and made the motion to approve the resolution.

cases.name: 12 Seymour Place East - garage addition and pool complex
cases.applicant: Paul (Lewis Goose / landscape architects)
cases.summary: Post-site-walk discussion of a garage addition and rear pool complex; the board had no substantive objections and directed the applicant to obtain a GLA (floor-area) variance from the ZBA before scheduling the public hearing at a July meeting.
cases.publicComment: No public comment; procedural discussion with the applicant's representative.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; no constructive objections, project well located
memberPositions.evidence: Said he had no constructive comments, called it a magnificent site and terrific project needing only the GLA variance.

cases.name: 75 Hickory Kingdom Road - request to retain original curb cut

The board reached a consensus against allowing it, noting the new driveway was justified only by the old one's unsafety, but a public hearing/neighbor notification is required before a formal denial. A board member recused himself citing a relationship with the applicant.
cases.publicComment: Michael Pollack spoke in his capacity as a Conservation Board member, arguing the board was misled and the old driveway should be shut down; no general public spoke.

memberPositions.stance: Opposed; the unsafe curb cut should be closed and the wetland incursion was justified only on safety grounds
memberPositions.evidence: Speaking as a Conservation Board member, said allowing the old curb cut after granting wetland-buffer relief for safety felt like being misled and the driveway should be shut down.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical; leaning toward denial of the amendment
memberPositions.evidence: Framed the item as presumably a denial of the proposed amendment requiring a public hearing, questioning why an unsafe curb cut would be permitted.

cases.name: 111 Round Hill Road - rock crushing permit
cases.applicant: Cory Salomon (Zarin & Steinmetz) for the owner; Sean's Lawns (Nick Wendell) contractor
cases.summary: Application to add rock crushing/processing to a previously approved site with rock chipping. The board debated noise, duration (about 30 crushing days, ~4,000 yards of rock), proximity to homes, and the fact that the more disruptive chipping/hammering is permitted separately by the building department without a hearing. It approved a crushing permit with a 10-week window at code hours; the motion carried with one dissent, and the board flagged wanting future coordination of chipping/hammering with crushing approvals.
cases.publicComment: An attendee named Vincent recounted living near a prior rock-chipping operation that ran nonstop and was very disruptive even at a quarter-mile; concerns raised that applicants may understate impacts with no remedy for neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive of crushing as on-site resource reuse; moved approval but acknowledged chipping/hammering harms
memberPositions.evidence: Called crushing a wonderful way to use on-site resources and moved to approve the permit with a 10-week window, while noting the hammering is what burdens neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Supportive; chipping and crushing make sense, asked about haul-off and truck traffic
memberPositions.evidence: Said the chipping and rock crushing make sense given the huge site and asked how much material would be hauled off versus used on site.

memberPositions.stance: Cautiously supportive; focused on proximity to homes and a reasonable window
memberPositions.evidence: Pointed out two homes within 400 feet and supported giving latitude on the window while limiting detriment to neighbors.

memberPositions.stance: Skeptical/opposed; pressed on neighbor impact, lack of remedy and process gaps; cast the dissenting view
memberPositions.evidence: Rejected being 'resigned to this,' warned applicants can understate impact with no remedy for neighbors, and urged guardrails coordinating chipping/hammering with crushing.

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road - house reconstruction and drive-through garage

memberPositions.evidence: Said he was not convinced the plans were as up to date as they should be and that updated plans plus a more robust landscape plan are needed before scheduling the hearing.

cases.name: Overhead vs. underground electric service policy (4 Alpine / 21 Wood Wool Road)
cases.applicant: N/A (policy discussion; 4 Alpine applicant to be brought back)
cases.summary: General discussion clarifying town code on electric service in areas of existing overhead lines: burying service to the house is required, but a single utility pole at the property line for overhead service is discretionary, not mandatory. A board member acknowledged his prior stricter interpretation was incorrect; the board decided to put 4 Alpine back on the agenda and have the applicant return rather than amend the application on its own.
cases.publicComment: No public comment; internal policy/procedure discussion with the town engineer (John) and staff (Mary).

memberPositions.stance: Wants due process; bring the applicant back rather than amend on the board's own motion
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed the burial is discretionary not mandatory and directed that 4 Alpine be re-agendized with the applicant present to adjudicate on the record.

memberPositions.stance: Insisted the board cannot make or re-file the applicant's request for him
memberPositions.evidence: Argued it is not within the board's purview to make the application for the applicant and that the applicant should return before the board.

Central to both the rock-crushing permit and the wetland curb-cut denial.
Driving issue at 111 Lafayette; office vs warehouse parking-table reconciliation.
Board consensus against retaining the unsafe original curb cut at 75 Hickory Kingdom Road.

700 Bedford must upsize to 100-year storm design.
GLA variance for 12 Seymour and front-yard variance for 700 Bedford gate the hearings.

Code-minimum lighting conditioned at 111 Lafayette; landscape/lighting plan needed at 700 Bedford.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board approved the May 29 minutes and worked through six applications. It granted conditional approval to the Sauro residence addition/pool/accessory apartment (Steven Sauro recused as owner) and approved a wetlands-buffer pool at 15 Stony Brook Place, granted a 90-day extension of time for the contaminated Eagle Ridge brownfield subdivision, reversed course to grant utility relief for an Alpine Drive home, referred the 154 Lafayette Avenue lot-line/commercial application to the ZBA and Town Board, and reviewed the 825 North Broadway gas-station redesign before sending it to the Architectural Review Board.

memberPositions.stance: facilitated, moved to grant the 90-day extension while wanting ongoing updates

meetings.meetingSummary: The Planning Board devoted most of the evening to a continued public hearing on the 92 & 94 Round Hill Road golf features (a retained green, sand traps, and four tee locations) sought via after-the-fact wetlands and site-plan approvals, hearing extensive opposition from neighbor Barry Edelman's attorney on golf-ball safety and setbacks. After an executive session with counsel, the board signaled it would allow the single green with enhanced landscape/net mitigation but directed elimination of the two added tees (T3 and T4), then adjourned the hearing to the first September meeting. The board also opened and immediately adjourned the Mayanus River Gorge office-addition hearing (pending an amended special use permit from the Town Board), approved the U-Haul after-the-fact site plan with conditions, referred a Middle Patent Road accessory barn/apartment to the ZBA, and approved the Four Ledgewood draft resolution.
meetings.durationNote: Board held a brief executive session with legal counsel and the town planner mid-meeting on the Round Hill Road matter. Chair Carthy, Steven Sauro (read the Mayanus notice), and Michael Pollack (read the U-Haul notice) were clearly present and active.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.applicant: Michael Lehrer / Round Hill Land Corp (attorney Jerry Tortorella; engineer Tim Allen)
cases.status: public hearing continued/adjourned to first September meeting
cases.summary: Continuation of the hearing on after-the-fact wetlands and site-plan approval for golf features on two adjoining wetland-buffer properties: one retained (unfinished) green, two sand traps, a constructed tee box (T1) and three additional turf tee positions (T2-T4), plus paths and a shed. The applicant argued the tees are de minimis, non-structural, that no golf-ball incidents have occurred in 26 years, and that setbacks for pools/tennis courts do not apply. Neighbor Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) opposed through counsel, stressing safety of children/grandchildren, the green sitting only 8-16 feet from the shared line, trajectories aimed at his glass-walled house, intensification from two to four tees, and requesting a 30-foot setback, DEC review, and stronger screening. After an executive session with counsel, the board indicated it favors retaining the green with a robust landscape and net mitigation plan along the 88 line but wants T3 and T4 eliminated, and directed the applicant to pursue DEC and a building-inspector determination. Adjourned to the first September meeting.
cases.publicComment: Heavily contested. Attorney George Ellis and owner Barry Edelman (88 Round Hill Road) strongly opposed on safety, setback, intensification, and precedent grounds. Antonio (100 Round Hill Road) worried the owner, a golf-course builder, could drift toward commercial/large-group use. Heather Hart (87 Round Hill Road) spoke in support, saying she has never seen an errant ball or a 'facility' in five years. Another neighbor disputed her account, citing crowds and pickup trucks. Conservation Board member George Repel noted the jump from two to four tees is a more intensive use and floated reversing the tee/green orientation.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'an overreach for the planning board to start regulating this particular use in the backyard,' framed the issue as risk versus probability, but pushed to eliminate T3 and T4, keep within 1999 parameters, and require an 'extraordinary landscape plan and mitigation plan' with possible netting along the 88 property line.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on the existing green's setback (8 vs 16 feet) and whether it could be moved; said it is 'not a wise precedent... to approve a recreational use of any type on someone else's property' (T4 being on the separate 94 parcel), agreeing it is not prudent.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical
memberPositions.evidence: Non-committal pending confidential advice from counsel and the town planner; argued the 'kids playing catch' analogy 'breaks down' because of the permanence of the installation, likening it to a fixed pitching mound; suggested a reasonable-height black-mesh net along the property line as mitigation.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge
cases.applicant: Mianus River Gorge Inc.
cases.status: public hearing opened and adjourned without date
cases.summary: Public hearing to construct an office addition and a gravel parking lot on the 960-acre preserve property in the R4A zone. Steven Sauro read the public hearing notice. The town planner advised that the applicant must first obtain an amended special use permit from the Town Board before the Planning Board can proceed. With no neighbors present, the board opened and immediately adjourned the hearing without a date.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors present; chair declined to bring anyone in only to send them home.

cases.name: U-Haul, 1 Virginia Road
cases.applicant: U-Haul
cases.summary: After-the-fact site plan approval for a canopy and shed used for vehicle release/dispatch, plus an extended rear canopy and new rear loading ramps, in the IND-A district. Michael Pollack read the public hearing notice. The applicant had already obtained ARB approval matching the existing canopy in kind. Remaining conditions were largely minor (engineering comments, a lighting plan, and an FAR calculation the planner still needs). The board closed the hearing and approved the resolution, with the planner to confirm zoning compliance before signing.
cases.publicComment: No public speakers.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: As a land-use professional, wanted the resolution to add language showing compliance with applicable zoning or that the shed does not require a variance ('if it did require a variance, it would'), while deferring to the planner reviewing FAR to his satisfaction.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: 'I'm okay with it. I think you clean this up pretty quick,' expecting the open items to be resolved rapidly.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed the applicant could clean up the outstanding conditions quickly, moved to close the hearing and approve the resolution, and praised the completed facility.

cases.name: Salabarria/Matthews Accessory Barn - 58 Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Chris Salabarria & Carol Matthews (engineer Allen Pilch, ALP Engineering)
cases.status: referred (to ZBA; also ARB and Conservation Board)
cases.summary: Initial concept presentation to replace a 100-plus-year-old dilapidated barn/garage with a combined garage and accessory apartment, intended primarily to give the owners' wheelchair-using adult son accessible visits since the existing home has interior steps. The structure is beyond saving (crumbling foundation), so the project needs several variances and touches the wetland buffer with a small portion of an ADA ramp and stormwater mitigation, requiring Conservation Board review. The chair suggested the applicants consider whether the existing footprint is truly the best location. The board referred the applicant to the ZBA and agreed to refer to the Conservation Board.
cases.publicComment: Applicants noted neighbors are supportive; no formal public hearing held yet (one will be required).

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Warmly received the application ('that's a good reason'), encouraged the applicants to consider whether a better location than the existing footprint would help their variance case, and moved to refer them to the ZBA with a Conservation Board referral.

cases.name: Four Ledgewood
cases.summary: The board revisited a draft resolution for Four Ledgewood, originally approved in 2023 but lapsed amid health-department and other issues and recently re-approved. The applicant had returned with a tightened resolution that let the board remove a number of prior conditions. The chair expressed reservations about the underlying concept ('I'm not sure I love it') but the board approved the draft resolution.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Acknowledged the resolution had been tightened and conditions removed, but said 'I understand the point of this... I'm not sure I love it,' before moving to approve the draft resolution.

themes.note: Dominant issue on Round Hill Road; neighbors fear errant shots toward children and a glass-walled house, applicant cites 26 years without incident.
Debate over whether golf features are an 'other similar recreation facility' subject to the 30-foot R2A side-yard setback; referred toward a building-inspector determination.
Expansion from two approved tees (1999) to four drove board direction to eliminate T3 and T4.
Green and paths sit in the wetland buffer; DEC may now take jurisdiction under new statewide rules and a permit condition is expected.
Board wants a detailed landscape plan with staggered evergreens and possibly a mesh net along the 88 line, balancing safety against visual impact.
Middle Patent Road barn replacement aimed at accessible accommodation for a disabled adult son drew board sympathy.

staffInput.summary: Managed plan displays throughout; his July memo suggested setbacks should be required for the golf features. Advised that Mayanus River Gorge needs an amended special use permit from the Town Board first, that remaining U-Haul conditions (FAR, lighting) were minor and within his review, and confirmed no code bar to relocating the Middle Patent barn.

Explained that DEC is now taking jurisdiction on many wetland applications under new statewide rules and that a DEC determination should occur before the Planning Board acts, with a 90-day DEC timeline; recalled the Whippoorwill driving-range net precedent where neighbors objected to net visibility.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board, chaired by Christopher Carthy, handled five items: a change-of-use/parking referral for 70 Lafayette Avenue (BOCES computer-repair tenant), a repositioned swimming pool concept at 250 East Middle Patent Road, a new-house application at 700 Bedford Road focused on septic and dual curb cuts, a wetland-adjacent addition at 76 Fireman's Road heading toward a public hearing, and two extension-of-time approvals for the Summit Club subdivision/site plan. The board referred the Lafayette application to the ZBA, granted the Summit Club extensions, and set a site walk for 700 Bedford Road. Conservation Board liaison Vincent DeAnno pressed for mitigation conditions on the Fireman's Road plan.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present; meeting reopened at 7:06 after executive session. Michael Pollack flagged a scheduling conflict with the Sept 22 meeting (eve of Jewish New Year); board agreed to move it earlier.

cases.name: 70 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Trevor, on behalf of property ownership; BOCES tenant (computer intake/repair)
cases.summary: The applicant proposes a change of use from warehouse to warehouse plus work room for a BOCES computer intake/repair operation with about five employees in roughly 3,300 sq ft. Because the change of use compounds an existing off-street parking deficiency variance, the board referred the applicant to the ZBA. There was a side discussion about the building being labeled 56 while the town address is 70, and concern that the fire department could be misdirected. The board moved to send the applicant to the ZBA and anticipated scheduling a planning board hearing after a ZBA decision.

memberPositions.stance: neutral

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Neil and Vanessa Lucy (owners); attorney Michael Sirignano; Jerry Barrett (landscape architect) and Nicholas of Hudson Engineering
cases.summary: A pool application first seen ~5 years ago under prior owners (the Benises) returned with the Lucy family. After a site conversation with the chair, the team presented a sketch moving the pool 16 feet back and about 4 feet lower so it sits in the side yard rather than the front yard, eliminating the zoning setback variance but still implicating the scenic road overlay, a conservation buffer, and 25% slopes. The revised concept would tie the pool to the existing bluestone patio via a retaining/engineered wall (est. 6-8 ft) with a forward sitting wall. The board strongly endorsed the new direction and asked the applicant to formalize plans with landscape and wetland mitigation plans and return.

memberPositions.stance: supportive

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Property owner with engineer (new house on Bedford Road)
cases.summary: The applicant seeks approval for a new house, with open issues on whether the county health department will accept the existing septic, NYSDOT right-of-way/curb-cut requirements, and whether the board will allow two curb cuts where code prefers one. The board was skeptical of retaining two curb cuts and pressed the applicant to document line-of-sight from each and consider a single reconfigured curb cut. Members debated a conditional approval tied to a health-department 'no objection' letter for the septic. The board scheduled a site walk for the following week and clarified that a noticed public hearing still must be conducted before any approval.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the board has denied second curb cuts before ('we put our foot down on that'), questioned why the new house couldn't be designed around a single curb cut, and pushed for a site walk before proceeding.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Addressed as 'Steve,' floated using a parking court in lieu of a second curb cut to make the house 'as nice as it can be,' though the applicant said the site is too tight with rock and a well.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Addressed as 'Larry,' pressed for line-of-sight measurements from both curb cuts and noted the applicant's communication of documents to the health department 'could be a little clearer.'

cases.name: 76 Fireman's Road
cases.applicant: Alan Piltch, LP Engineering (addition to existing three-bedroom house)
cases.summary: The engineer updated the board on a ~941 sq ft addition to an existing three-bedroom house that requires wetland review. The project cleared the Conservation Board on June 24 with a satisfactory mitigation plan, a joint DEC permit application was filed, and DEC was set to verify the wetland boundary that Friday. The county health department will issue its 'no objection' for the existing septic only after DEC acts. With stormwater testing and a sight-line analysis still outstanding, the board agreed the plan looks good and set a public hearing for the next meeting (two weeks out). Conservation liaison Vincent DeAnno stressed that mitigation conditions (contingency plan, five-year buffer plan, cost estimate, and full mapping of invasive species) must be locked in and not slip through the cracks.
cases.publicComment: Vincent DeAnno (Conservation Board liaison) noted a lake association with 18 homeowners and a 30-foot easement, and past homeowners who failed to follow through on approved conditions.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'I think it looks good' and moved to schedule the public hearing for the next meeting, while acknowledging DEC approval will be a condition; agreed with DeAnno that conditions must be enforced rather than left to slip through the cracks.

cases.name: Summit Club
cases.applicant: Summit Club Partners
cases.summary: The board considered two extensions of time for the Summit Club: one for the final subdivision plat approval and one for the site plan (with steep slopes and tree-removal permit approvals). Staff explained the applicant is working through the approval process and is reportedly taking deposits/listing units for sale, with the county Board of Health notoriously slow on the substantial infrastructure (including a sewage treatment plant). The board granted both extensions of time.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed staff on how they know the project is progressing ('how do you know that') and noted nothing had come across the desk, but moved to grant both extensions of time.

themes.note: Central to 250 East Middle Patent, 700 Bedford, and 76 Fireman's Road (buffers, DEC permits, mitigation).
Health-department 'no objection' for existing systems is a gating condition on 700 Bedford and 76 Fireman's Road.
Board skeptical of two curb cuts at 700 Bedford; code prefers one and site walk ordered.
Scenic overlay/setback compatibility discussed for the 250 East Middle Patent pool.
25% slopes at 250 East Middle Patent and steep-slope permit at Summit Club.
Mapping scattered invasives cited as the hardest mitigation item at 76 Fireman's Road.
Traffic-safety sight lines from the 700 Bedford driveways still to be documented.
Pretreatment/separator capacity and rain garden discussed at 76 Fireman's Road.

staffInput.summary: Reintroduced each application, framed the open issues (parking variance, septic, curb-cut code language, scenic setback), and authored the review memos guiding board discussion.

Kellard's office (referenced via 'Rick'/KSCJ) engaged on soil/stormwater testing, septic separation, sight-line depiction on plans, and verifying that mitigation items are correctly placed on the drawings.

Reported the Conservation Board's conditional approval and strongly urged locking in mitigation conditions (contingency plan, five-year buffer plan, cost estimate, full invasive-species mapping) so approved items are not forgotten; cited past homeowners who failed to follow through.

meetings.meetingSummary: A light August agenda with no public hearings, opened by Chairman Carthy (who noted it was his wife's birthday). The board granted several extensions of time and a site-plan waiver, then reviewed site-walk applications and referred projects onward to the Conservation Board, ARB, and ZBA. Most items were routine, straightforward, and favorably received, with outstanding work limited to engineering comments and landscaping details.
meetings.durationNote: No public hearings held (76 Byram Ridge Road came off the agenda). Chair plus multiple members present and voting; quorum evident. Short meeting.

cases.name: Park Place / 11 New Kings Street
cases.applicant: 11 New Kings Street; attorney William Noll (Cuddy & Feder)
cases.summary: Applicant requested a two-year extension of site plan approval for the Park Place automated parking structure near the airport, the eighth such extension. Counsel reported building permit review is underway with construction plans filed and no changes to design or circumstances. Carthy asked whether it would return again or be built; counsel expected it well underway within two years. The board granted the extension.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to grant the extension of time for Park Place.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Asked whether it would be back before the board or built in the interim; wished counsel well and closed the item favorably.

cases.name: 135 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Request for a site plan waiver for a change of use in a ~23,000 sq ft office building, converting 3,000 sq ft from general office to dental office. Corey noted parking requirements are lower for the new use, so demand actually decreases. Carthy asked planner Adam Kaufman if he had concerns and he had none. The board granted the waiver.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed no concerns from staff and moved to grant the waiver of site plan.

cases.name: 124 Old Mianus Road
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Extension of time request. Corey reported additional comments received from the town engineer's office and the health department are being addressed, expecting to turn them around within about a week and a half. Carthy noted one item to review with planner Adam Kaufman offline. The board granted the extension.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Took the item at the chair's invitation and made the motion to grant the extension of time for 124 Old Mianus Road.

cases.name: 40 High Street
cases.applicant: Applicant represented by Corey (engineer)
cases.summary: Extension of time request. Corey explained they were close to finishing the milk hour/health department submission when their DOH reviewer left and a new reviewer issued additional comments on August 1, which they are now addressing. The board granted the extension of time.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Moved to grant the extension of time for 40 High Street after hearing the DOH reviewer turnover delay.

cases.name: 250 East Middle Patent Road
cases.applicant: Michael Cerniano covering for Jerry Barrett (applicant's team)
cases.summary: Following a site walk the prior week, the board reviewed a revised plan that pulls the structure a full 16 feet further from the road and roughly 18 feet lower in elevation, making it essentially not visible. Members found it favorably sited and no longer in the front yard. A wetland permit is triggered because the work is within 150 feet of the wetland, and discussion clarified the steep-slope (25%) regulation, with engineer John Kellard noting the rear yard is under 25% which narrows the review. The board voted to refer the applicant to the Conservation Board, targeting a September public hearing on return.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the board was anxious to move forward, confirmed it was favorably viewed at the site walk, and moved to send the applicant to the Conservation Board.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: A member observed after the site walk that it was 'pretty straightforward,' that it's 'not in the front yard anymore, which is a big part of the movement forward,' and 'it's sited well.'

cases.name: 700 Bedford Road
cases.applicant: Applicant (not present)
cases.summary: The board reviewed a recent site walk though no one appeared for the applicant. The property was described as effectively a blank slate showing existing conditions, and the board recommended the applicant hire a landscape architect to dial in the plan. The applicant is developing plans behind the scenes per prior feedback and is expected to return.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Explained the applicant is developing plans per feedback and that the board recommended hiring a landscape architect to refine the plan.

cases.name: 1613 Old Orchard Street
cases.applicant: Marlene Duran & Diane Rosenberg (owners); attorney Noel Wolfson (Hopperman Tortarella & Wexler); engineer Ralph
cases.summary: Counsel gave a full status recap of this long-running application (since January 2023) for a single-family residence on a vacant lot largely within the regulated wetland buffer. The footprint was reduced ~500 sq ft per Conservation Board conditions, and superimposed aerial coverage analysis showed building and impervious coverage fall within the range of surrounding lots. A driveway location with adequate site distances was designed with traffic engineers and a ZBA variance was granted in June. Engineer John Kellard raised remaining comments on basement elevation/drainage and unclear tree-removal designation; the board directed the applicant toward noticing a public hearing at the next meeting.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: A member commented favorably that the garage faces front as 'an attractive facade,' it's a center hall colonial 'in keeping with the area,' and the garage taking much of the footprint made the size 'reasonable.'

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: A member noted the Conservation Board is happy with the downsizing but that a fair number of engineering comments remain to be addressed.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Praised the recap as a 'perfect synopsis,' probed where the house falls in size relative to neighbors, and moved the applicant toward a public hearing.

cases.name: 32 Orto Drive (Israel Townsend Hill subdivision, Lot 1)
cases.applicant: 32 Orto Drive LLC; Andrew Vaccarello, B&J Engineering; colleague Matt (architect)
cases.summary: Site plan for a single-family dwelling on Lot 1 of a recorded subdivision over which the board retained jurisdiction. The ~2,900 sq ft footprint is fully zoning compliant with generous setbacks; it is about 700 sq ft larger than previously depicted with a slightly enlarged driveway in the same location, an on-site septic and well, a rain garden for the slight impervious overage, reduced downstream peak flows, and about 24 trees removed. Members discussed the landscaping/replanting plan and tree preservation, and the board directed the applicant to the ARB, asking that a landscape plan be brought along.
cases.publicComment: Recalled that neighbors had commented during earlier hearings, particularly regarding this lot; noted trees are being preserved so no issue was seen.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: A member said the plan 'looked pretty straightforward' with some changes from the original but nothing concerning.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on the landscape plan given ~24 trees removed, noting the ARB will want a replanting/landscaping plan and the board should review it too.

cases.name: 84 Business Park Drive
cases.applicant: Eric Lashins, 84 Business Park Associates LLC
cases.summary: A 60,470 sq ft office building on ~3.8 acres in the PLI zone with 242 existing spaces (4 per thousand). A newly signed lease with a medical user changes the parking formula, leaving the site four spaces short and requiring a four-space variance, though the applicant maintains ample parking exists. Members questioned the change of use and the medical share of the building, and several agreed the town's 4-per-thousand formula is antiquated. The board voted to refer the application to the ZBA.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Asked what the change of use was and how much of the building is medical, then directed the applicant to the ZBA to obtain the variance.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: A member volunteered to take it and proposed sending 84 Business Park Drive to the ZBA; members agreed the 4-per-thousand parking formula is antiquated.

themes.note: Central to 250 East Middle Patent Road and 1613 Old Orchard Street; both within regulated wetland buffers.
Four routine extensions/waivers granted quickly at the top of the meeting.
Office-to-medical/dental conversions drove the 135 Bedford and 84 Business Park items.
~24 trees at 32 Orto Drive and unclear removal designation at 1613 Old Orchard prompted landscaping-plan requests.
Change-of-use parking issues at 135 Bedford Road (waiver) and 84 Business Park Drive (ZBA variance); members called the town formula antiquated.
25% slope rule clarified for 250 East Middle Patent Road, narrowing the review scope.
Rain garden and reduced downstream peak flows proposed at 32 Orto Drive; basement drainage flagged at 1613 Old Orchard.

staffInput.summary: Consulted throughout; confirmed no concerns on the 135 Bedford Road waiver, flagged an offline item on 124 Old Mianus Road, and reportedly advised the applicant's engineer on tree-removal notation for 1613 Old Orchard Street.

Identified that 250 East Middle Patent Road's rear yard is under 25% slope, narrowing the review, which the chair praised. On 1613 Old Orchard Street raised basement-elevation/drainage concerns (agreed to lower the basement) and the need to clearly designate trees for removal on the site plan.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board handled four public hearings and three additional items. It approved a house addition/wetlands mitigation at 76 Byron Ridge Road, a warehouse-to-office conversion at 70 Lafayette Avenue (Marquis Associates), and a swimming pool along scenic East Middle Patent Road. The board also approved a new four-bedroom home at 1613 Old Orchard Street over neighbor and Conservation Board concerns about house size, wetland buffer impact, and stormwater/climate change.
