Extensive public comment opposed or questioned the project on catastrophic-slope-failure risk, historic preservation, water/sewer capacity, dust, truck logistics, and long-term (50+ year) maintenance liability, and Open Space chair Carrie Kayza detailed alleged misrepresentations in the applicant's environmental assessment form (SHPO consultation, air pollutants, critical environmental area). The board secured the applicant's consent to a no-blasting condition on the site plan and adjourned the hearing to gather more on the EAF, construction oversight, and a maintenance covenant/deed restriction.
cases.publicComment: Heavy and predominantly negative: residents George Keller (child safety at the cut, brown/sediment-laden well water and overtaxed century-old sewer), Kate Hall (fear of catastrophic slope failure onto the only untouched Revolutionary War battlefield in Westchester), Bonnie Fite (fear of an abandoned unfinished 'eyesore'), Doug Manston, Nora, and a powerful preservation plea from Cynthia Abbott-Coffman and Open Space chair Carrie Kayza (EAF deficiencies, SHPO not consulted, misquoted county/historical-society letters). Applicant repeatedly conceded points (no blasting, insurance, surveys, maintenance covenant).

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Defended the applicant's legal right to develop and the town's peer-review process ('the planning board is charged with protecting...'), drove the no-blasting condition onto the site plan, but candidly played devil's advocate that the board has no good answer to the public's 20-50-year maintenance/safety question 'not just tonight but for a lot of applications.'

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on who approves in-field design changes and how Simpson stays involved during construction; skeptical that two trucks on site handle ~2,000 truckloads; and stressed protecting the site 'in perpetuity' since the wall needs constant maintenance and 'is not something that's going to stabilize over time.'

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Asked about hours/duration rules for chipping and rock crushing and the county air-quality permit requiring water-spray dust control; called the exchange 'a very constructive and meaningful exercise' and said 'we've made a lot of progress' while wanting the EAF and the reviewer's construction role nailed down.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical
memberPositions.evidence: Highlighted resident Conservation-Board geotech expert Vincent DeAnno's 'amazing experience' and pointedly asked the applicant's engineer whether its submission would change 'at all' based on DeAnno's criticism (it would not).

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: When invited by the chair ('Tom?') to weigh in during board deliberation, deferred with 'I don't know,' offering no substantive position on this application.

cases.name: 92 & 94 Round Hill Road
cases.applicant: J. Fane (attorney Jerry); neighbor represented by attorney George Ellison (for Barry Edelman, 88 Round Hill Road)
cases.summary: The applicant's attorney appeared without the applicant, who was unavailable, and asked to carry the continued hearing to the second January meeting to allow time to review draft approval documents with the client over the holidays. He reported the client elected to remove retaining-wall segment 'T1' entirely and submitted revised plans reflecting that. The neighbor's counsel spoke constructively, praising progress and raising administrative cleanups (drawing revision dates, papering the T1 removal, an as-built condition, a null-and-void-on-alteration clause, and whether the T2 netting should also be netted on top). The board reopened, took the neighbor's comments, and re-adjourned to January 26, 2026.
cases.publicComment: Neighbor's attorney (George Ellison, for 88 Round Hill Road) was cooperative and complimentary, offering administrative suggestions rather than opposition.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Expressed mild frustration that the applicant was absent and he 'wanted to get done with this application,' but accommodated the adjournment, reopened to hear the neighbor, and agreed to explore netting on top of the T2 wall.

cases.name: 263 Bedford Banksville Road (equestrian property)
cases.applicant: attorney Jerry (J. Fane)
cases.summary: An extension-of-time request for a large equestrian property with a new residence, pool/pool house, renovated exercise barn, second stable, and garage with room quarters above. Counsel explained construction is proceeding in good faith without compliance issues but cannot finish within the original 18-month window, and sought clarification that the completion deadline runs co-terminus with the building permit. The board granted a one-year extension.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Moved to grant the extension after confirming the completion date is governed by the building permit, with no objection to the good-faith progress reported.

cases.name: 4 Vincent Lane (wetland restoration)
cases.applicant: Tom Savage; landscape architect Lewis Fusco
cases.status: public hearing closed; decision adjourned pending ARB approval of existing sheds/barn
cases.summary: A wetlands/site-plan application to modify a driveway and front walkway, remove astroturf golf areas and invasive wetland plants, and install native plantings, removing roughly 25,000 sq ft of lawn/hardscape and providing 40,000 sq ft of wetland mitigation. The Conservation Board had commended the project and the applicant addressed the town engineer's comments. The board closed the public hearing but could not adopt the resolution because two sheds and a barn built under earlier building permits never received Planning Board/ARB sign-off (a town-side glitch); it opted to send the applicant to the ARB and adopt at a later meeting without requiring the applicant to reappear.
cases.publicComment: No public spoke; Conservation Board had previously commended the project.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Proposed the workable path of letting the board finalize after the ARB step without dragging the homeowner back ('could we do it without the applicant even being here?... you don't have to show up'), which the chair credited as 'a good solution.'

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Sympathetic to the applicants ('people... trying to do the nicest things to a property') and frustrated at the town's own oversight, steering to a low-burden ARB-then-adopt process.

cases.name: Kent Place / Verizon Parking (subdivision & site plan)
cases.applicant: Verizon / Town of North Castle (Kent Place parking expansion)
cases.status: approved (negative declaration, site plan, preliminary and final subdivision resolutions adopted)
cases.summary: A re-approval of an already-built parking expansion whose original approvals expired because Verizon never signed the plat map; no changes to what was built. A long-time abutting neighbor (Suzanne) testified at length about Verizon's chronic lack of maintenance, tree removal without replacement, an unstabilized dirt frontage with U-turns and a porta-potty, a downed fence, and unfinished screening she paid ~$40,000 to remedy herself. The board acknowledged those are largely building-department property-maintenance matters, advised her to write the building department, and re-adopted all resolutions so the plat can be filed with the health department.
cases.publicComment: Abutting neighbor (Suzanne) was strongly negative about Verizon as a neighbor - poor maintenance, tree removal, downed fence, inadequate screening - and asked for additional trees; board noted most issues fall to the building department.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Acknowledged the neighbor's frustration and that 'Verizon was allowed to get a pass,' but directed her to the building department for the downed fence/maintenance and proceeded with the procedural re-approval of the already-built project.

cases.name: Single-family residence & pool (Angela, applicant) - cut/fill grading
cases.applicant: Angela (owner-applicant); engineer not present
cases.status: discussion only (direction given to respond to memos and schedule a public hearing)
cases.summary: A working discussion on a hillside single-family home with a pool, garage, and retaining walls where the applicant had already reduced imported fill and wall heights and relocated the pool per prior board feedback. New wetland flagging in the rear was coordinated between the applicant's wetlands engineer and the town's consultant (Dave). The planner questioned whether setting the first floor at 473 (vs. ~470.5 garage) could be lowered to reduce cut/fill and wall grading; the board directed the applicant's professionals to answer the planner's and town engineer's memos and then set a public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Worked through elevations and cut/fill with the applicant, credited her for having 'mitigated a tremendous amount' of walls and fill since the prior iteration, and pushed to answer outstanding memos and 'set a public hearing and move it along.'

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road (Wood Hollow Estates)
cases.applicant: owner/builder John Nickett; represented by Ralph Alpinsetti
cases.status: discussion only (public hearing to be scheduled; referral to ARB/RPRC)
cases.summary: A working discussion on developing a vacant 2.5-acre subdivision lot (no wetlands, sewer in the road) with a ~7,500-8,000 sq ft house comparable to neighbors, involving substantial cut and fill between a high and low grade. The planner suggested retaining walls to reduce cut, and the board explored slope steepness, a rock outcrop, and whether the design could include a walk-out basement under the current 30/38-foot height rules. The builder cited a nearly identical prior house he built on Terrace Circle; the board directed responses to the engineer's and planner's memos, a possible pre-submission meeting, and then a public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Engaged constructively on the cut/fill approach, walls vs. steeper rock cuts, and encouraged pursuing a walk-out basement ('less grading, I'm all in'), steering the applicant toward scheduling the public hearing after ARB/RPRC review.

cases.name: IBM EV charging station installation
cases.address: IBM corporate headquarters campus, North Castle
cases.applicant: IBM; Seth Waltzman (representative) and colleague Stephanie
cases.status: discussion only (Level 2 to be approved at January hearing; board voted to recommend Town Board permit Level 3)
cases.summary: IBM proposed installing EV chargers in its gated, security-restricted visitor lot - three Level 2 plus one dual Level 3 fast charger - but town zoning currently limits infrastructure to Levels 1-2, so Level 3 requires a Town Board law change (a use variance being too high a bar). IBM stressed conduit run mostly above ground with minimal disturbance and no new municipal power load. The board noted a Town Board discussion on amending the EV-charger definition was already on that Wednesday's agenda, scheduled the site-plan public hearing for January, and voted to send a memo recommending the Town Board permit Level 3 charging at this gated site (which removes the highway-motorist concern).

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the gated, 24/7-manned, restricted-access location defeats the Town Board's concern about motorists pulling off the highway for fast charging, and pushed the board to formally recommend the Town Board change the law to allow Level 3.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'what's in front of me right now makes all the sense in the world to put in a level three,' qualifying only that he was not privy to all the Town Board's reasons for the Level 2 cap.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Framed fast charging as 'a reasonable future use for the town,' and moved that the Planning Board send a memo encouraging the Town Board to change the law to allow Level 3 charging at this site.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Concurred with the recommendation, saying 'what Larry says makes a lot of sense.'

cases.name: 113 King Street (Toll / airport campus water tank - 'the enclave') field change
cases.applicant: applicant represented by attorney Maholic (Cuddy & Feder)
cases.summary: A field-change request after a CAD software error caused the water-tank foundation, pumping station, and generator to be built roughly 10 feet north of the approved location, with minor adjustments to spacing between the components; the generator remains six feet from the property line and everything stays zoning-compliant. With no board questions, the resolution was adopted.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: After confirming continued zoning compliance and that the board had no questions, moved to adopt the draft field-change resolution.

cases.name: 12 Bedford Road (extension of time)
cases.applicant: owner (driveway-to-rear project, near final approval)
cases.summary: A brief extension-of-time request for a project involving a driveway to reach the rear of the property, described as very close to final approval with the applicant anxious to proceed. The board granted the extension, then closed the Planning Board for 2025.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Moved to grant the extension of time for the near-final project before adjourning the board for the year.

themes.note: The 76 Virginia Road rock cut beside Miller Hill drove most of the meeting and most of the concern.
Impassioned public plea to protect the Miller Hill Revolutionary War battlefield and Miller House on the 250th anniversary.
Repeated worry about a 'living wall' needing perpetual maintenance and unanswered 20-50-year liability questions.
4 Vincent Lane restoration well received; new flagging coordinated on the Angela residence.
Residents cited overtaxed century-old sewer, brown well water, and rock-crushing dust at 76 Virginia Road.
Board unanimously recommended the Town Board allow Level 3 chargers at IBM's gated lot.
Several routine approvals: two time extensions, a water-tank field change, Verizon re-approval, ARB routing.

staffInput.summary: Active across nearly every item: pulled up plans and prior submissions; on 76 Virginia Road invoked his April 11 memo raising concern about the extensive slope removal and its threat to Miller Hill, and helped shape conditions (maintenance covenant, no-trucks-on-street, netting/ongoing-monitoring language, chipping/crushing hours); flagged the missing ARB approvals at 4 Vincent Lane; explained the 30/38-foot building-height rule at 7 Hollow Ridge; and laid out the Level 2 vs. Level 3 EV code limits and Town Board law-change path for IBM.

Carried open engineering-memo items on 76 Virginia Road and was asked to respond to the Open Space chair's EAF critique; on the single-family grading discussions signaled that detailed engineering follows once the board is comfortable with the site plan; coordinated wetland flagging with the applicant's engineer on the Angela residence.

Speaking as a Conservation Board member and geotechnically-trained resident (ASR garbled his surname as 'the anno'/'Jordano'), delivered the meeting's most detailed technical critique of 76 Virginia Road: poor upper-slope rock quality and slip planes, soil nails not seated in rock, undersized/under-strength anchors (grade-75 rebar, single vs. double corrosion protection, some under 25 feet), risk of secondary fractures, winter ice chunks breaking through netting into an unbarriered parking lot, line-drill bit drift, and the long-term 'living wall' maintenance burden potentially falling on the town. The applicant's engineers said his comments would not change their submission.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board handled a full slate of public hearings and discussion items on a January evening. It approved an amended site plan at 4 KSL Court and a wetlands mitigation resolution at 88 Byron Ridge Road, and after a lengthy debate approved a new single-family residence at 62 Nethermont Avenue with added conditions requiring seismic monitoring and pre-drilling to protect neighbors from rock hammering. Several other hearings (100 Buckout Road, 125 Business Park Drive, 2 & 4 Massaro Court) were opened and adjourned or approved with administrative conditions, and the board took up discussion-only items for a Coptic church accessibility walkway at 667 North Broadway and an after-the-fact legalization at 850 North Broadway.
meetings.durationNote: Member Lawrence Ruisi was absent (Carthy opened by noting Larry would not be joining). The board sat as four: Carthy, Sauro, Pollack, and Crispi. Carthy repeatedly referenced being 'one of four.' Quorum present.

cases.name: 4 KSL Court
cases.applicant: Property owner adding a landscaping-equipment tenant (engineer 'John' presented)
cases.summary: The applicant sought an amended site plan to add a second tenant (a landscaping equipment/vehicle storage use) to a warehouse building that had never received formal site plan approval. Changes included reworking parking to a one-way in/out layout with spaces designated for the principal building versus the tenant, and a new lighting design brought up to current dark-sky code. No members of the public appeared. The board closed the hearing and approved the amended site plan, with the lighting review satisfying condition number two.
cases.publicComment: No public present.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Called the resolution 'very clean' and moved to close the hearing and approve the amended site plan.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice and seconded the motions to close and approve.

cases.name: 62 Nethermont Avenue
cases.address: 62 Nethermont Avenue, North White Plains (Section 122.12-5-46), R-2F zoning
cases.applicant: Owners Lindsay & Dmitry (architect Rocco Delano; applicant's father Jim New sold them the lot)
cases.summary: The applicant proposed a new ~4,865 sq ft single-family residence, positioned six feet off the south side line to preserve a future subdividable building lot. Neighbors raised concerns about rock excavation/hammering near a ~100-year-old adjoining home, house size/neighborhood character, and tree removal, while other neighbors and the applicant's father spoke strongly in support. The board debated at length whether to require protection beyond the standard chipping permit given the hammering's proximity to the neighbor. It ultimately closed the hearing and granted the resolution as amended, adding conditions that a seismic monitor be placed on the neighbor's (Pinella/'Davis') foundation and that the applicant pre-drill (line drilling) to reduce vibration.
cases.publicComment: Heavily attended. Neighbor Pinella/Penella and Nora voiced concern about rock excavation impacts, house size, and loss of neighborhood character; the applicant's father Jim New, realtor Gail Norris, and applicant Dmitry spoke in support, arguing the house is compliant and rock is limited. Tone was earnest and at times tense but not hostile; the chair explicitly urged civility.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Drove the discussion that placing rock hammering six feet from the line to preserve a future building lot creates a 'collateral detriment' to the neighbor, and pushed for a higher level of protection than the standard chipping permit, saying 'I just don't know what I don't know in this case.'

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the application is zoning-compliant and reasonable and that this 'doesn't rise to a level where standard procedures should be usurped'; proposed the compromise of requiring line-drilling before chipping to steer the break and minimize seismic impact.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Initially cautioned the board was 'putting the cart before the horse' since the chipping permit and rock extent were unknown; later concluded Steve's proposed drilling/monitor condition 'would more than sufficiently protect any concerns that the code doesn't already protect.'

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Favored requiring a seismograph on the neighboring foundation to resolve the matter that night, and asked Adam to analyze what could be built on the reserved second lot if subdivided.

cases.name: 100 Buckout Road
cases.applicant: Nicholas Shri, Hudson Engineering, for the applicant
cases.summary: The applicant sought site plan, wetlands permit, and tree removal approvals for a new house. Because the engineer's review memo was far from resolved, the chair opened and adjourned the hearing. The applicant's engineer flagged disagreements on whether an NOI is required (under an acre of disturbance, not in the East-of-Hudson watershed), driveway drainage constraints between existing and proposed septic systems, staying under the one-acre wetland-buffer disturbance threshold, and rock removal on the south side for the sunroom/walkout. Missing ARB approval was also noted. The board directed the applicant to tighten the plans and reconcile the memo before returning.
cases.publicComment: No public present.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Advised the applicant to tighten the plans, meet with the town engineer, and 'button up that memo' before returning, calling it 'too much for the planning board to approve at this point.'

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice for the application.

cases.name: 88 Byron Ridge Road
cases.applicant: Property owner (with a pending sale); represented at hearing
cases.summary: This was an after-the-fact wetlands matter: additional disturbance occurred in the regulated wetland buffer during construction, drawing a notice of violation, and the originally approved 2022 mitigation plan had not been implemented for years. A proposed fence and 7,600 sq ft of 'no-mow' lawn had drifted into the record but were removed; the mitigation plan and fill removal have now been completed and observed by the town wetlands consultant, and the Conservation Board recommended approval. The board adopted the resolution as amended, adding a clarifying 'whereas' that the fence was removed and the placed fill was removed, with five-year monitoring beginning.
cases.publicComment: Conservation Board liaison Vincent DeAnno detailed the history and his concern over how the fence/no-mow lawn entered the memo; Jack, president of the Lake Association, said the neighborhood is satisfied so long as the mitigation plan stays in place and is monitored. Tone: initially concerned, resolved to satisfied.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Guided the clarifying amendment that the fence and placed fill were removed and moved the board to adopt the resolution as amended once the Conservation Board and Lake Association were satisfied.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice and moved/seconded on the resolution.

cases.name: 125 Business Park Drive
cases.address: 125 Business Park Drive, Lot 5 Westchester Business Park (Section 108.03-1-55), PLI zoning
cases.applicant: Owner of Lot 5, Westchester Business Park
cases.summary: The applicant sought reapproval of a previously approved but expired site plan for an approximately 9,390 sq ft warehouse and office building with associated parking and loading. The hearing was opened and immediately adjourned; no substantive discussion or public comment occurred.
cases.publicComment: No public present.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice; hearing opened and adjourned procedurally.

cases.name: 2 & 4 Massaro Court
cases.applicant: Developer of two two-family residences (engineer 'Rick' presented)
cases.summary: The applicant presented revised site/steep-slope plans for two two-family residences, addressing prior comments by adding a terraced retaining wall to soften the driveway wall's appearance, providing two dedicated parking spaces per unit, reworking side/rear grading, and clarifying overland footing-drain discharge. Outstanding engineering memo items (landscape plan revisions, planting detail, drain pipe sizes/inverts, peak flows) were deemed handleable administratively. The board approved the resolution for 4 Massaro Court that night; since the buildings are identical, 2 Massaro Court would be approved administratively at a future meeting once the applicant obtains ARB approval, without needing to return. The board flagged that any rock encountered on the up-hill site would require checking back.
cases.publicComment: No public present.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed outstanding memo comments could be handled administratively and structured the approval so #4 was granted and #2 would follow administratively after ARB, sparing the applicant a return trip; moved to approve.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice; the board (via the engineer's prompting) flagged the up-hill site as potentially rocky and requiring a chipping permit if rock is hit.

cases.name: Virgin Mary and St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church
cases.applicant: Virgin Mary and St. Monique Coptic Orthodox Church (Father Tedros and a church representative)
cases.summary: The church proposed a level sidewalk cutting across its own adjoining lot to give elderly and disabled parishioners accessible entry to the lower level of the church, avoiding numerous steps. No exterior changes to the building or the existing retaining wall are proposed, so the planner advised no ARB approval is needed and that existing non-conforming components would not require variances since nothing is changing. The chair explored whether an ADA ramp might serve better than the level walk, then directed the applicant to meet with the planner and schedule a public hearing.
cases.publicComment: No public comment; only the church applicants presented.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Engaged constructively on how best to serve elderly parishioners, asked whether an ADA ramp versus the level walkway would be more functional, and directed scheduling of a public hearing.

cases.name: 850 North Broadway
cases.applicant: Property owner (not present)
cases.summary: Work was done on the back of the building without a permit and now needs to be legalized, along with several site plan issues. With the applicant absent, the planner explained that a basic site plan (addressing refuse, parking, lighting, and safety requirements, similar to the 4 KSL Court approach) will be needed before the board can approve a site plan. No action taken.
cases.publicComment: Applicant not present; no public comment.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Noted work was done 'without a permit apparently' and that the site plan issues now need to be legalized, deferring to the planner on the basic site plan requirements.

themes.note: Dominated the 62 Nethermont hearing; board added seismic-monitor and pre-drilling conditions to protect a close neighbor.
Central to 88 Byron Ridge (after-the-fact mitigation) and 100 Buckout (buffer disturbance).
Recurring engineering-memo item at 100 Buckout and 2 & 4 Massaro Court.
Raised by neighbors at 62 Nethermont; planner confirmed the house is below the FAR/coverage threshold.
Outstanding for 100 Buckout and 2 & 4 Massaro; not required for the Coptic church walkway.
Coptic church level walkway to serve elderly/disabled parishioners.

staffInput.summary: Confirmed paperwork was in order for each hearing and drove much of the analysis: recalled the town's house-size/FAR law adopted after the mid-2000s teardown debates and confirmed 62 Nethermont is below threshold; offered to research the prior 22 Nethermont seismic-monitoring precedent and helped craft the added conditions; explained subdivision/FAR math; advised 100 Buckout to reconcile its memo; framed the 88 Byron Ridge clarifying amendment; and outlined basic site-plan requirements for the church walkway and the 850 North Broadway legalization.

Consulting/town engineering review (KSCJ memos, presented by 'Rick') drove the outstanding technical comments — driveway drainage vs. septic, NOI/one-acre disturbance, footing-drain discharge, drain pipe sizes/inverts and peak flows, and cautions about rock on up-hill cut sites — most deemed handleable administratively. Kellard's office also handled the 88 Byron Ridge additional fill remediation.

For 88 Byron Ridge, recounted the wetland-buffer violation history, the unimplemented 2022 mitigation plan, and his concern over how a fence and 7,600 sq ft of no-mow lawn entered the Conservation Board memo, confirming the plan is now installed and the board recommends approval. Also gave geotechnical input at 62 Nethermont (as a civil engineer with a geotech background) on lowering seismograph thresholds and line-drilling to protect the neighbor.

meetings.meetingSummary: Despite a snow event, the Planning Board held its previously scheduled meeting so noticed public hearings would not have to be re-advertised. The board opened and adjourned a hearing on a new home at 7 Hollow Road pending a landscape plan and ARB approval, approved site improvements at 3 Israel Townsend Hill, and approved IBM's amended site plan for EV charging stations. It reopened the 76 Virginia Road rock-wall hearing (adopting an amended negative declaration but keeping the hearing open over unresolved seismic-monitoring, bonding/repair, and truck-staging issues), took a status update on the 825 North Broadway gas station, approved a driveway field change at 26 Hurlingham Drive, and forwarded a town-board referral on a Level 3 EV-charging local law back with no changes.
meetings.durationNote: Quorum present; Michael Pollack participated by Zoom. Meeting held during a snow emergency that had lifted by 4 PM.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Road
cases.applicant: Ralph (project engineer) for a new single-family residence
cases.summary: Application for a new single-family residence on a 2.5-acre vacant lot within an approved subdivision, connecting to sewer with a proposed well and front/rear stormwater mitigation. The board opened the public hearing but Carthy noted the landscape plan was missing from the package and declined to close the hearing. A neighbor at 6 Hollow Place had submitted a letter raising tree-removal and screening concerns. The hearing was adjourned to a future meeting, to be reopened once the landscape plan is submitted and ARB approval is obtained.
cases.publicComment: No residents spoke in person; a written letter from Deb and Marie at 6 Hollow Place raised tree removal and screening concerns, to be addressed at the next hearing.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the landscape plan was missing and said 'I for one would like to see that landscape plan,' adding it could affect how the neighbor's concerns are addressed; declined to close the hearing.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed the paperwork was in order and read the public-hearing notice into the record.

cases.name: 3 Israel Townsend Hill
cases.address: 3 Israel Townsend Hill (Lot 108.01-6-1.2), R1A zoning district
cases.applicant: Andrew Vaccarello, Federal Engineering, for the property owner
cases.summary: Site improvements for an existing single-family dwelling that will remain, including a new driveway, septic system, and well replacing former systems; 17 trees proposed for removal consistent with the prior subdivision approval. The applicant flagged a lot-acreage typo (about 4.46 acres) in the draft resolution and asked to drop a landscaping condition given the heavily vegetated lot. Larry probed plantings near the septic close to the property line and confirmed a tree buffer would remain to the adjacent lot. The board closed the hearing and approved the site development plan and tree-removal/tree council permit.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public were present for this application.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Asked about plantings where the septic runs near the property line and about the tree buffer to the neighboring lot, was satisfied by the answers, confirmed he was okay moving forward, and made the motion to approve.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public-hearing notice into the record.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Joining by Zoom, when asked if he wanted to add anything he said he had nothing to add.

cases.name: IBM EV Charging Stations
cases.address: 1 New Orchard Road (Lot 113.02-1-8), OB zoning district
cases.applicant: IBM (world headquarters)
cases.summary: IBM sought amended site plan approval to install four EV charging stations in its gated visitors' parking lot, to be built as Level 2 now and upgraded to Level 3 if the town adopts the pending code change permitting Level 3 chargers. Adam confirmed no planning concern and that approval would let IBM build Level 3 later without returning to the board. Carthy questioned the applicant's use of the word 'variance,' which staff clarified was actually a town-wide law change. The board opened and closed the hearing and adopted the resolution.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public were present for this application.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public-hearing notice for the IBM EV charging stations into the record.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on why the applicant used the term 'variance,' clarifying with staff that the matter was a change in the town law rather than a variance; otherwise supportive and moved the resolution.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road
cases.applicant: Tony Viziano (attorney) and Jose Rodriguez, CC Engineering, for the property owner (645/6.45 North Broadway operator)
cases.summary: Reopened hearing on a project involving a substantial rock cut stabilized by an anchored netting system, tied to bringing the applicant's nearby office property into conformance. The applicant reported a completed Phase 1A archaeological study (no/low sensitivity, submitted to and accepted by SHPO) and the board adopted an amended negative declaration removing a mischaracterized historical-society letter reference. Major unresolved items kept the hearing open: a written seismic/vibration monitoring plan for the town engineer to review, a deeded perpetual maintenance obligation plus bonding, whether a maintenance bond also covers repair/re-pinning after a rock dislodgement, and a truck-staging/queuing plan for a project projecting ~20 trucks a day for months. Public speakers raised the NEG DEC wording and challenged anchor lengths, safety, and whether an alternate design was considered.
cases.publicComment: Two residents spoke: Edward (North Castle Historical Society) objected that the NEG DEC cited a superseded/mischaracterized society letter and asked it be corrected; Vincent Giordano challenged that the anchors were only 10-15 feet on the north and south faces (not 20-25 ft), raised ice/crash-barrier safety concerns, questioned whether the site is effectively being quarried for rock sale, and urged an alternate design. Tone was skeptical and concerned but constructive.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Drove the discussion that a $5,000 maintenance bond does not cover a repair/re-pinning after a wall failure and pressed that a single-purpose ownership entity may lack assets; said he wants a bond covering the cost of re-pinning if it becomes necessary, calling the maintenance bond helpful but not getting the board where it needs to be.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Focused on protecting Virginia Road from cars driving around queued trucks, questioning how and where trucks would stage given limited room; pushed for a staging plan written into the resolution and endorsed getting the seismic monitoring plan in writing for the town's engineer to review.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical
memberPositions.evidence: Said he was not comfortable closing the hearing, especially with the public underrepresented due to weather; insisted the seismic monitoring plan be laid out in writing so the town's consulting engineer can critique it rather than leaving it as a condition of approval; also pressed on truck queuing and perpetual maintenance.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Briefly indicated he had been wondering about the anchor question that Larry ended up asking; limited engagement on this item.

cases.name: 825 North Broadway
cases.applicant: Gas station applicant (name not stated)
cases.summary: Status update only on the 825 North Broadway gas station. Staff reported the board had previously been comfortable with the plan and requested a draft resolution, but outstanding comments remained, so the applicant made a further submission that addressed many but not all conditions. The town engineer still could not recommend adoption, so the applicant will make another submission. No action was taken.

cases.name: 26 Hurlingham Drive (field change)
cases.address: 26 Hurlingham Drive (ASR-uncertain; address in resolution being corrected)
cases.applicant: Property owner / project representative (name not stated)
cases.summary: A field change on a previously approved plan (dating to around 2021) to reconfigure the driveway serving the caretaker's cottage and main house, eliminating a looping drive in favor of a direct approach. The board found the redesign an improvement and had no substantive comments. One item noted was a correction to the property address in the resolution. The board approved the field change.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Said he had no comments or questions and called it a 'nice design,' then moved to approve the field change.

cases.name: EV Charging Local Law (Level 3) Referral
cases.applicant: Town Board (referral of a proposed local law)
cases.summary: A town-board referral on a proposed local law to permit currently-prohibited Level 3 EV charging, with an open question of whether Level 3 spaces should count toward off-street parking (a draft cap of no more than 20%). Carthy argued the board should encourage the town to reduce barriers and count the charging spaces within the parking requirement rather than requiring them in excess. Steven Sauro repeatedly cautioned about unintended consequences, including the town becoming a highway 'road stop' and businesses using chargers as a profit loophole. After an extended debate, the board declined to add a substantive recommendation and voted to send the referral back to the town board as written.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Advocated reducing barriers to EV charging as part of the town's future, urging the town board to allow Level 3 spaces to be included within the off-street parking count rather than above and beyond it.

memberPositions.stance: skeptical
memberPositions.evidence: Said 'there's so many unintended consequences that we're not seeing' and was 'not jumping headfirst'; worried about the town becoming a road stop for non-residents and about a backdoor revenue loophole for businesses charging above market, declining to make Carthy's recommendation.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Noted many parking situations are already at their limit so counting requirements could inhibit installations, and asked whether any accessibility/proximity parameters govern where chargers go; engaged analytically without taking a firm side.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Took up the motion to make the recommendation, sending the referral back to the town board as written with no further comment.

themes.note: Central to both the IBM approval and the extended Level 3 local-law referral debate.
76 Virginia Road anchored-netting system dominated discussion with safety and design scrutiny.
Pollack pressed that a maintenance bond does not cover repair/re-pinning after a failure.
Ruisi concerned about ~20 trucks/day queuing safely off Virginia Road.
Raised on 7 Hollow Road (neighbor screening) and 3 Israel Townsend Hill (buffer retained).
Whether EV charging spaces count toward off-street parking requirements.
New septic and well at 3 Israel Townsend Hill with buffer to property line.

staffInput.summary: Introduced and framed most applications; noted the 7 Hollow Road neighbor letter and pending ARB approval, advised IBM could be approved as Level 2 with Level 3 later, recommended adopting the 76 Virginia Road negative declaration as amended without waiting for SHPO's final reply, gave the 825 North Broadway status update, and explained the Level 3 EV local-law referral and the off-street-parking debate.

Reported the applicant had addressed all engineering comments and concerns on 3 Israel Townsend Hill; the board wanted the town's consulting engineer to review and opine on the 76 Virginia Road seismic monitoring plan; on 825 North Broadway the town engineer could not yet recommend adopting the resolution due to remaining conditions.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board worked through a long agenda: it continued the 7 Hollow Ridge Road public hearing (adjourned so the applicant could digest a late-arriving engineering memo), approved site-plan/subdivision resolutions for 154 Lafayette Avenue and reopened/closed and approved 124-125 Business Park Drive, and adopted a resolution for Vincent Lane. It heard a new-house/retaining-wall application at 23 North Lake (Chairman Carthy recused), referred a Citibank directional-sign request to the ZBA, took a presentation on the NYC DEP Kensico-Eastview wetland mitigation project and referred it to the Conservation Board, reviewed and returned the town's proposed short-term-rental law without formal comment, and discussed the Buck's Flower Garden nursery violations (scheduling an April 8 site walk). Several routine extensions of time were granted.
meetings.durationNote: Chairman noted at the opening that one member was absent (to return next meeting); a quorum was present. Thomas Crispi was identified as new to the board. Christopher Carthy recused himself from 23 North Lake and Steven Sauro presided over that item.

cases.name: 7 Hollow Ridge Road
cases.applicant: Lauren Brennan (Alton Engineering) with property owner Charlie Catch and a landscape architect
cases.summary: Continuation of a hearing on a single-family house with pool, patio, driveway and stormwater capture. The applicant reported reducing the disturbance area (from ~71,700 to ~62,000 sf) and tree removal (from 134 to 99). Much of the discussion centered on the town engineer's (John Kellard) memo, which had arrived late and which the applicant team had not yet seen: knoll grading, ~10-foot driveway cuts on a 14% grade, rock outcroppings, the need for a temporary sediment trap rather than just silt fence, and trench drains for driveway runoff. The board declined to adopt the resolution until the applicant reviews and addresses the memo, keeping the hearing open and adjourning. Landscaping (six white pines for rear screening) was also debated.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared for this application; the applicant referenced a rear neighbor who had raised concerns about views/screening and was said to have been spoken to.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Presided; said he personally understood why the applicant would grade out the knoll to level the property and did not want to fight over it, but insisted the applicant take home and address John's engineering memo before any resolution, keeping the hearing open.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Suggested the applicant meet with the engineer to resolve the memo issues offline and return, rather than solving everything at the table; separately defended the white pines, noting he planted white pines on his own property that grew ~40 feet and effectively screen from neighbors.

cases.name: 124 Kisco Road (extension of time)
cases.summary: Brief update on a subdivision still awaiting the county Health Department, which was reported to have signed off with the town engineer now finalizing review. The board granted an extension of time.

cases.name: 154 Lafayette Avenue
cases.applicant: Mark, representing Mike Mealy (owner present)
cases.status: public hearing opened and closed; approved with conditions
cases.summary: Change of use of a legal non-conforming home to office use, treating three existing non-conforming parcels together by moving a property line, removing one dwelling and converting another to an office, plus commercial truck storage. The long-standing sticking point was parking; the board reaffirmed acceptance of six parallel spaces in front and required the plan to clearly show the nine off-street spaces needed for the office kept truck-free, with the balance available for overnight truck storage. It was determined ARB review was unnecessary (no exterior changes) and that whether ZBA approval is needed turns on a building-inspector determination of whether the nonconformity is increased. The board struck a condition, adopted the NegDec, the site-plan resolution, and the preliminary and final subdivision resolutions.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on the parking condition, noting the plan would be expressly permitting overnight truck storage and wanting clarity that the nine required office spaces be shown; ultimately agreed ('Yeah, OK') once the nine truck-free spaces would be identified.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice into the record (procedural role); no strong independent stance beyond supporting the approval.

cases.name: 124-125 Business Park Drive
cases.status: public hearing reopened and closed; approved
cases.summary: A prior approval had expired and the applicant re-ran the planning board process, obtaining the required Zoning Board of Appeals approval. The board reopened and closed the public hearing (no public present). A board member raised that the property sits in a wetland buffer and asked whether the wetlands regulations/buffers had changed since the original 2006/2008 approvals; confirmed they had not. The board adopted the NegDec and the draft resolution.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public appeared.

cases.name: 23 North Lake
cases.applicant: David Haber (owner); Conrad Rancotti, project architect; engineer (continuity from prior design)
cases.status: discussion only (to return after Conservation Board and ARB, then public hearing)
cases.summary: A new four-bedroom house reusing an existing, never-used pool and septic field on a steep site. The item before the board was an over-six-foot retaining wall (up to ~10.17 feet, ~7.17 feet retaining soil) at the front of a courtyard, faced in native stone. The architect also floated a modification relocating the third (one-car) garage next to the two-car garage, with a reduced two-car garage and a breezeway to limit added mass. The board found the design attractive and was supportive, directing the applicant to finish with the Conservation Board (meeting the 17th), return to the ARB for the change, and then come back for a public hearing. Stormwater and septic re-certification with the Health Department were noted.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Presided over this item after Carthy recused; asked about bedroom count, septic re-certification and wall height, and encouraged the applicant ('You guys are on the right track. I can see it').

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'an attractive design' and agreed it is the homeowner's home to be happy with, seeing pros and cons in both garage options and noting wall height could be mitigated with landscaping.

cases.name: Citibank signage
cases.applicant: Applicant/sign contractor (from Long Island / Lindenhurst)
cases.summary: Applicant sought to replace existing directional freestanding signs (36 by 20) exceeding the one-square-foot directional allowance. The board explained it cannot grant that exception and referred the applicant to the Zoning Board of Appeals for the variance; if granted, the planning board could then approve the site plan. Building-mounted signs are ARB jurisdiction. The board voted to refer.

cases.name: NYC DEP Kensico-Eastview Connection Wetland Mitigation
cases.address: Route 120 wetland site (~6.4 acre DEP parcel) with Old Post Road staging area (Block 1, Lots 15 and 16)
cases.applicant: NYC Department of Environmental Protection (Angel Riness and team)
cases.summary: DEP presented the wetland mitigation component of the Kensico-Eastview Connection (KEC) water-tunnel program, tied to a shoreline stabilization project in Mount Pleasant. The mitigation would enlarge an existing wetland to establish ~2.5 acres of marsh/open water and ~1.7 acres of upland habitat, removing ~388 trees, using a Route 120 construction access and a one-acre staging area (five trees removed there). Construction expected late summer/early fall 2026 with limited truck traffic; rock removal by mechanical means with blasting as a contract option. The board asked about blasting radius, nearby houses and underground infrastructure near the reservoir/tunnel, and voted to refer the project to the Conservation Board.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Expressed general confidence in DEP to do the job right while probing the blasting radius, proximity to houses and underground infrastructure; noted the impacts are in another town while North Castle gets the wetland mitigation, and moved to refer to the Conservation Board.

cases.name: Vincent Lane
cases.summary: The board had previously closed the public hearing and instructed the applicant to obtain ARB approval before returning for adoption. With ARB approval now in hand, the board adopted the draft resolution without the applicant needing to appear.

cases.name: Short-Term Rental Law (town board referral)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Town Board)
cases.status: reviewed and returned to Town Board without formal comment
cases.summary: The Town Board referred its proposed short-term-rental law (a zoning-chapter amendment) to the Planning Board for input. The board discussed the framework at length: primary-residence requirement, the 30-day threshold, operating permits and building-department inspections, occupancy tax, quiet hours, and the provision barring a short-term rental on the same lot as an accessory dwelling unit (ADU). Views split on whether the law is too cumbersome (risking noncompliance) versus appropriately detailed for enforceability, but there was broad agreement its practical effect is to discourage short-term rentals. The board reached consensus to send it back to the Town Board with no substantive comment.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Argued the need to regulate is legitimate via a hotel analogy: short-term rentals lack the supervision, fire-code and safety safeguards of hotels, so the town should know where they occur; explained the ADU rationale that adding a short-term rental to a lot already carrying an accessory apartment increases intensity too much.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Read the law as the town trying to discourage short-term rentals, noting the primary-residence requirement plus the ADU restriction effectively signals 'we'd rather not'; referenced east-end-of-Long-Island 'creepy houses' and acknowledged North White concerns.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Cautioned that making the law too brief would leave openings people would exploit and make it harder to enforce; said he did not mind the law's extent/complexity and agreed with Larry that it is intended to discourage.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Said he read the law and watched the town board meeting; worried it may be too onerous/complex and could inadvertently cause noncompliance, wishing it were simpler and briefer, while agreeing its intent is to discourage short-term rentals.

cases.name: Buck's Flower Garden (65 Banksville Road)
cases.address: 65 Banksville Road (ASR-uncertain; also referenced as 65 Bedford)
cases.applicant: Whitney Singleton (attorney) with Joe Rina (engineer) for the nursery owner
cases.status: discussion only; April 8 site walk scheduled
cases.summary: A ~46-year family wholesale nursery with a single-family home that accrued building-department violations, chiefly an unpermitted fill/boulder retaining area (~700+ cubic yards) with no fill certification, plus an unpermitted loop road, expired sign permit and other cleanup items. The applicant seeks to legalize the site while reducing nursery intensity (abandoning retail) and building a new home and barn/garage. Staff's memo argued the town board must re-approve the special use permit due to increased intensity of use (office and equipment garage space); the board wants a narrative of operations. Concerns focused on possible contamination in the undocumented fill (soil/core sampling via HES to be initiated) and tree removal for a proposed third horse paddock. The board scheduled a site walk for April 8 at 8:30 AM, partly so new member Thomas Crispi could see the property, and left the item open for further discussion in April.
cases.publicComment: The owner was not present (described by her attorney as passionate but at times aggressive about the property).

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Drove the discussion on the undocumented fill and lack of records, saying core sampling is needed to potentially put it to rest; probed why the special use permit needs town-board re-review (intensity of use) and called for a fresh site walk to re-familiarize the board.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Engaged on soil/fill testing precedent, noting the area's environmental sensitivity (near the Mianus River area / critical environmental area) and that a fill permit and testing are required regardless of wetlands, though not opposing the cleanup path.

cases.name: 76 Virginia Road (National Lawn / Spring Court)

cases.summary: After roughly six weeks of work, the board closed the public hearing and adopted a conditioned site-plan resolution for a landscaping-business building requiring a large rock cut (up to ~70 feet, chipping not blasting, no on-site crushing) with a soil-nailed/netted retaining wall. Extensive discussion covered a seismic/vibration/air/noise monitoring plan with stop-work exceedance thresholds and town notifications, a truck-routing safety plan queuing trucks off-site, an annual operating permit and wall-maintenance manual traveling with the deed, and a Phase 1B archaeological survey (nothing on site; high Revolutionary-War sensitivity next door at Miller Hill). cases.publicComment: A member of the public was present earlier but did not wish to speak; resident Nora watched via television and had expressed prior interest.

I just want everyone to be aware of the risk.'

memberPositions.stance: neutral

memberPositions.stance: supportive

cases.summary: Reopened continued public hearing on a new residence involving steep-slope and wetland-buffer disturbance. The applicant argued that many draft resolution conditions (retaining wall, tree count, earthwork, soil testing/infiltration, silt fence) were repeat comments already addressed, and asked to be voted on tonight. The board would not approve: an SHPO/historic-cemetery notification and a tax-map-versus-survey boundary discrepancy remained open, and, most significantly, roughly an acre of wetland mitigation for about a half acre of buffer disturbance had been steered toward administrative handling by the town wetland consultant rather than the Conservation Board. The board concluded that no site directive could authorize skipping the Conservation Board, directed the applicant to prepare a full mitigation plan and route it through the Conservation Board, and to re-notice the public hearing, targeting the May meeting.
cases.publicComment: The property owner spoke from the floor, frustrated at the delay after six appearances, saying the added requirement after months was costing him time and money; the board was sympathetic but held firm on process.

memberPositions.stance: concerned

memberPositions.stance: concerned

memberPositions.stance: mixed
