cases.status: public hearing closed; re-approved for 60 days with conditions
cases.summary: The applicant sought re-approval of a previously approved (and twice-expired) house project, now controlled by a bank after the developer defaulted. Members and the direct neighbor were frustrated that the front yard remains dirt, the railing is damaged, landscaping is unfinished, and the required easement for screening on the neighbor's property was never executed. The board debated how to protect the neighbor without making the house unsellable, ultimately granting only a 60-day approval (rather than a year) with conditions requiring execution of the easement, irrigation of the plantings on the neighbor's property for two years, and a maintenance bond for the planting plan. The hearing was closed and the amended resolution adopted.
cases.publicComment: Direct neighbor Steven McLaughlin (24 Whippoorwill Road East) spoke, frustrated after paying out of pocket for an easement agreement and watching the resolution expire twice; concerned the new bank owner will cut corners and about a dry shallow well for watering.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Recapped that only a four-month extension was granted last time due to the site's state, noted the landscaping still isn't done and the railing is broken, and pushed to keep the approval short and focus on getting plants watered and established.

memberPositions.stance: mixed
memberPositions.evidence: Cautioned that piling on conditions ('the more you do, the more you're going to make this house unsellable') could create a vicious cycle and actually harm the neighbor by keeping the house from selling.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Called the property 'unsightly,' drove the shift to a 60-day approval, and championed adding an irrigation condition and a planting maintenance bond so the neighbor is protected and the bank has incentive to complete the plantings.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Asked clarifying questions about the 'next submission' and assented to the bond/irrigation conditions ('Yeah, I'm fine').

cases.name: 26 Carolyn Place
cases.applicant: Alpine Engineering (Lauren)
cases.summary: This application had its public hearing previously closed, but action was pending the applicant's ARB review. With ARB complete and a fill issue resolved (the applicant is removing the fill) plus a revised plan addressing town-engineer comments, the board proceeded. There were no outstanding board concerns. The board approved the site plan and tree-removal permit.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to approve the site plan and tree-removal permit ('Thank you, Steve').

cases.name: Cigar Bar / Membership Club at 909 North Broadway (Sir John's Plaza)
cases.applicant: James Montelione (representing the membership club)
cases.summary: A town-board special-use-permit application for a membership club at Sir John's Plaza was referred to the Planning Board for comment. The chair questioned how the code's required 25-foot-deep planting buffer would be satisfied given the site's history and rock conditions, and the planner explained the buffer requirement is aimed at screening golf-course-type clubs, not two converted storefronts. The board had no substantive objections. It voted to send a positive referral back to the town board.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Questioned feasibility of the required 25-foot planting buffer given prior review, but after the planner's context concluded the board had no objection and moved a positive referral, wishing the applicant well.

cases.name: 6 Sterling Road South
cases.applicant: Hudson Engineering (James German / Nicholas Shri) for the property owner
cases.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)
cases.summary: The applicant proposed improvements to a single-family residence on a three-acre lot: removing the attached garage and building a larger three-car garage with a small living space/bedroom (going from five to six bedrooms), reshaping the driveway, and adding a mudroom, with a net decrease in impervious area and a new infiltration practice. The applicant addressed a septic concern by showing the 2004 system was designed for eight bedrooms. The main open item is a code provision barring living quarters in a garage, to be confirmed with the building inspector. The board directed the project to the ARB before returning for a public hearing.

cases.name: Amsaro Court subdivision (final two-family lot)
cases.applicant: Applicant's engineer (Nick)
cases.status: discussion only (to ARB, then public hearing)
cases.summary: This is the last of a previously approved three-lot, two-family subdivision, with the first two lots already built. The town engineer raised concerns about the proposed house footprint's proximity and view-shed impact on the adjacent home, plus an exposed-foundation/grade drop-off at the rear northwest corner. The applicant's engineer agreed to regrade that corner (up to about 372) and consider shifting the house, while noting retaining walls are less substantial than the prior lots and structural wall designs are under town review. The board was generally comfortable and directed the project to the ARB and a revised grading plan before a public hearing.

cases.name: 263 Bedford Banksville Road
cases.applicant: Nick Shannon, Landform Landscape Architecture (new landscape architect for the applicant)
cases.status: approved (field change amendment; pergola and fence changes to return as amended planning board approval)
cases.summary: A new landscape architect proposed relatively minor tweaks to the previously approved plan on this former horse-farm property: shifting the pool closer to the house, reducing patio and retaining-wall extents, adding planting to manage runoff, minor driveway curve/gate changes, and asking to use asphalt instead of gravel on a steep driveway segment. Drainage remains as previously engineered. The board treated most items as a field change but determined the pergola and fence changes require returning to the Planning Board (rather than being handled by the RPRC) since new structures can't be approved as a field change. Conservation liaison input was sought given the site's wetland-buffer history. The board adopted the field-change amendment resolution.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Weighed in on whether the pergola/fence changes should go to the RPRC or stay before the planning board, leaning toward keeping context with the planning board ('once before the planning board stay before the planning board').

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Recalled the site's horse-farm and black-locust/tree-removal history, worked through the field-change vs. amended-approval mechanics, and moved to adopt the field-change amendment.

cases.name: Bedford Greenwich Animal Hospital
cases.applicant: Bedford Greenwich Animal Hospital
cases.summary: The applicant told staff they read the review memo and are working on it, and did not appear. The board opted to carry the item to the next meeting when they return with an amended submission addressing the comments. No substantive discussion occurred.

cases.name: Summit Club (aka summer club)
cases.applicant: Summit Club
cases.summary: No representative was present. The chair and planner gave an update noting background activity on water infrastructure: a water-line extension easement is already in place, but the timeline may accelerate so that water could be brought through the club and interconnected (potentially reaching Windmill), rather than the development operating as its own on-site water district. The board granted an extension of time.

themes.note: Central to 22 Whippoorwill (unfinished plantings, irrigation, bond) and 263 Bedford Banksville.
Erosion-control condition added on the church; infiltration/drainage discussed on 26 Carolyn, 6 Sterling, and 263 Bedford.
Recurring discussion of which body reviews what and whether items qualify as field changes.
Neighbor raised heavy truck/excavation and safety concerns at the church's busy intersection; board required a traffic-control plan.
Board debated a planting maintenance bond and irrigation obligation to keep enforcement leverage at 22 Whippoorwill.

staffInput.summary: Provided procedural framing throughout: explained DOT right-of-way documentation timing on the church, the 26 Carolyn ARB posture, the 25-foot buffer's golf-course intent for the membership club, the field-change vs. amended-approval distinction on 263 Bedford Banksville, and the Summit Club water-infrastructure update.

The consulting engineer (addressed as 'Rick' in the ASR) judged the church cut/fill volumes insignificant, offered to review a traffic-control plan, prompted the erosion condition, and flagged footprint/grading and view-shed concerns on the Amsaro Court lot; also weighed in on gravel-vs-asphalt driveway and bonding estimates.
Called up regarding 263 Bedford Banksville to speak to the site's wetland-buffer and tree-removal history (black locust); confirmed the current tweaks are not affecting wetland buffers.

meetings.meetingSummary: A short agenda following Memorial Day. The board handled an extension-of-time request for the 12 Maple Avenue restaurant site plan, which was granted but then thrown into doubt when Michael Pollack argued the underlying ZBA parking variance had expired under Town Code Section 355-77. It then held and closed a public hearing on the 6 Massaro Court two-family house (final lot of a three-lot subdivision), approving it as amended. Finally, on 23 North Lake Road (new single-family home with an 11-foot retaining wall and wetlands), Chairman Carthy recused and left; acting chair Lawrence Ruisi presided while the board approved the site plan, wetlands permit, and tree-removal permit as amended, with the applicant to return for an amendment on stormwater/rain-garden design after further conservation board review.
meetings.durationNote: Chairman Christopher Carthy recused himself and left the room for the final application (23 North Lake Road); a second board member also recused ('I'm recusing as well') but could not be identified. Lawrence Ruisi acted as chair for that item and closed the meeting.

cases.name: 12 Maple Avenue
cases.applicant: Restaurant developer (offshoot of an area farm project; new investment/celebrity partners; revised exterior approved by ARB)
cases.status: extension of time granted, then flagged; variance validity referred to town attorney and ZBA
cases.summary: The applicant sought an extension of time on a previously approved restaurant site plan, reporting secured funding, an ARB-approved revised exterior, and a request tied to the new town employee parking lot. The board granted the extension, but Michael Pollack then raised Town Code Section 355-77, arguing that the ZBA parking variance (issued Dec 7, 2023) had expired after two years because no building permit or CO had been issued, and that without a valid variance there is no site plan to extend. Town attorney 'Mary' agreed there is a two-year limit and would investigate, and planner Adam Kaufman noted variances can be extended by the ZBA. The board concluded the applicant likely must return to the ZBA for a variance extension and then get re-approved by the Planning Board.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors spoke; town attorney 'Mary' confirmed the two-year variance limit and agreed to review the file.

memberPositions.stance: opposed
memberPositions.evidence: Read Section 355-77 and argued the ZBA variance had expired with no building permit issued, so 'without a variance you don't have a site plan' and voting to extend the resolution 'is against the town code'; also called the ~400% parking reduction 'a problem for me.'

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: As chair, took the objection seriously ('I feel like we're in a predicament now'), asked the planner and attorney to confirm the two-year status, and directed that the applicant likely return to the ZBA and be re-voted, warning the attorney 'there could be some peril here.'

cases.name: 6 Massaro Court
cases.applicant: Michael Stein, Hudson Engineering
cases.status: public hearing closed; approved with conditions (as amended)
cases.summary: This was the final lot of a three-lot subdivision (two prior lots approved in January), seeking site plan and steep-slope approval to build a two-family dwelling with retaining walls, substantial grading, and a comprehensive stormwater system. Discussion focused on a condition (condition 6) requiring the grading plan be revised to eliminate a seven-foot exposed basement to the town engineer's satisfaction, and on a retaining wall shown 'by others' sitting on the property line. Michael Pollack, citing a similar issue in his own professional practice, suggested making explicit that maintenance of the wall is this property owner's obligation to avoid future disputes. The board closed the public hearing (no public spoke) and granted the resolution as amended per Pollack's suggestion.
cases.publicComment: No members of the public spoke.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Flagged that the property-line retaining wall ('by others') needs a clear maintenance obligation, suggesting the resolution make it 'the obligation of this property owner to maintain that retaining wall in the future' to head off disputes down the road; resolution was amended per his suggestion.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Had no additional concerns when polled ('Steve? Yeah') and seconded the motion to close the public hearing.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: When polled ('Tom?') indicated no further questions or objections to the application.

cases.name: 23 North Lake Road
cases.applicant: Conrad Runkati (architect) and Kalista Burton (Burton Engineering)
cases.status: public hearing closed; site plan, wetlands permit, and tree-removal permit approved as amended (applicant to return for amendment)
cases.summary: A new single-family home requiring Planning Board review for an ~11-foot (8-foot structural plus 3-foot aesthetic extension) retaining wall, on a pond-front lot with wetlands, prior-owner disturbance, and an existing pool to be reduced. Chairman Carthy recused and left; Lawrence Ruisi acted as chair and Tom Crispi read the hearing notice. The core open issue was stormwater treatment: a buried CulTec system under the courtyard versus a town-engineer-suggested bioretention/rain garden in the wetland buffer, which would require returning to the conservation board. After debating whether approving now would set a precedent for laden conditions, the board approved the current plan (site plan, wetlands permit, tree-removal permit) as amended, with the applicant expected to return for a full amendment once the rain-garden and mitigation revisions are worked out. Conservation board representative George Trapow praised the project as a model example.
cases.publicComment: No neighbors spoke; conservation board rep George Trapow spoke strongly in favor, calling it 'a wonderful project' and a model of wetlands mitigation and native plantings.

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: As acting chair, worked through the drainage/rain-garden options and voiced concern about 'setting a precedent' by approving with unresolved conditions that must go back to the conservation board; ultimately favored approving the current plan as-is and having the applicant return with a fully sorted amendment 'rather than signing off on something we really haven't focused on.'

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Engaged on the engineering memo, flagging the unusual fill condition that caught his eye ('you're near fill, and if it's not sufficient it needs to go') and the need for granular, percolating fill for the stormwater system.

themes.note: Dominated 23 North Lake Road; CulTec-under-courtyard vs. bioretention/rain-garden in the wetland buffer.
Prior-owner disturbance remediated; approved mitigation/maintenance plan praised by the conservation board.
Michael Pollack argued the 12 Maple Avenue ZBA parking variance lapsed under Section 355-77, undermining the site plan extension.
Property-line maintenance obligation flagged at 6 Massaro; 11-foot wall drove the 23 North Lake review.
Seven-foot exposed basement condition at 6 Massaro to be resolved to the town engineer's satisfaction.
Tree-removal permit approved at 23 North Lake alongside native replanting mitigation.
Pollack objected to the large parking reduction at the 12 Maple Avenue restaurant.

staffInput.summary: Reported the 12 Maple Avenue applicant had secured funding and was moving forward; when Pollack raised the expired variance, acknowledged the two-year issue rarely comes up but confirmed the ZBA can grant variance extensions, and that a lapsed variance would require a re-vote by the Planning Board.

Engaged on the 6 Massaro grading/exposed-basement condition to his satisfaction, and led the 23 North Lake stormwater discussion (concerns about storing water behind the retaining wall, suggesting a front-of-wall bioretention/rain garden, and requiring granular fill that is tested for percolation and removed if it fails).

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Planning Board closed the continued public hearing on the 100 Buckout Road wetlands permit and approved it after the Conservation Board recommended approval of the home mitigation plan and SHIPO confirmed no impact to the nearby historic cemetery. The board then worked through the parking standard for a proposed cigar membership club in Surjon's Plaza, agreeing to apply the club floor-area standard and referring the applicant to the ZBA for a parking variance only if needed. Adam Kaufman led a procedural discussion about moving extensions of time to the top of future meetings and adding whereas clauses on other-board approvals. The board granted extensions of time for 40 High Street and Ken Place (Verizon), and rescinded its prior extension for 12 April Avenue because the applicant's underlying ZBA variance had lapsed.

cases.name: 100 Buckout Road
cases.summary: This was a continuation of a public hearing on a wetlands permit that the board had previously declined to treat as a minor permit, sending the applicant back to the Conservation Board. The Conservation Board reviewed the home mitigation plan, found the structure could not be moved out of the buffer, judged the mitigation (slightly more than 2:1) adequate, and recommended approval. The applicant also confirmed via SHIPO that the project would not impact the African American historic cemetery across the street, and a previously missing page of engineering conditions was now reflected in the draft resolution. The board closed the public hearing and approved the resolution.
cases.publicComment: A Conservation Board representative ('Jane') spoke in support, explaining the board reviewed the mitigation plan and approved at slightly more than two-to-one; no neighbors objected.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: As chair, walked through the SHIPO cemetery response and Conservation Board letter, confirmed engineering concerns were addressed, and moved to close the hearing and approve the resolution.

cases.name: Cigar Membership Club (Surjon's Plaza)
cases.summary: A cigar membership club (special permit already granted by the Town Board, now in the site-plan phase) faced a parking question in the Surjon's Plaza strip mall. Adam Kaufman explained the membership-club parking code offers three standards and recommended the one-space-per-200-square-feet floor-area standard (about nine spaces), which likely avoids a variance, noting the shared lot and evening-only use. Members debated whether to use the more conservative fire-code/occupancy figure (about 17-18 spaces) as a more defensible, realistic number. The board agreed to cite a standard, made a referral to the ZBA for a parking variance if necessary, and Adam agreed to run the numbers; the submitted plan already showed 18 spaces.
cases.publicComment: The applicant/architect stated occupancy of 50 and answered parking questions; no neighbor opposition.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Asked the technical questions on capacity and fire code, pushed to use the ~17-space (fire-code) figure as more realistic and defensible than nine, while agreeing not to make it harder than necessary.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Addressed as 'Steve'; worked through the 50-member/50-car math but concluded it's a huge lot and an evening establishment, 'willing to move along with it.'

memberPositions.stance: leaning-supportive
memberPositions.evidence: As chair agreed with Adam that shared parking in the plaza means it won't be a real parking issue, said the board is entitled to be 'a little academic,' and drove the ZBA referral motion.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Addressed as 'Tom' and gave his consent on the board's referral action ('Tom, you own board of consent?' — 'Yes').

cases.name: Extensions of Time — Procedure Discussion
cases.summary: Adam Kaufman opened a policy discussion on how the board handles extensions of time. The board agreed to place extensions at the top of future meetings so professionals can dispatch them quickly, while a participating professional argued the published agenda order should not bind the chair (comparing it to a courtroom). Adam also proposed adding whereas clauses to extension resolutions stating whether another board (e.g., the ZBA) had a required approval and its status, so lapses are clearly documented. The board and staff endorsed the changes.
cases.publicComment: A professional/applicant representative debated agenda-order fairness, arguing a 7 p.m. notice implies flexible ordering like a courtroom; 'Mary' called the whereas-clause idea an excellent idea.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: As chair, said he was amenable to moving extensions to the top of the meeting and endorsed Adam's whereas-clause proposal for documenting other-board approvals.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Agreed applicants whose ZBA variance expires must go back to the ZBA ('I agree with Larry ... if there's a ZBA that expires they got to go back').

cases.name: 40 High Street
cases.applicant: Corey (representative)
cases.summary: The board considered another extension of time for 40 High Street, which has been pending since 2024. Staff reported the applicant had previously been waiting on the health department. The chair expressed impatience that it has dragged on and asked staff to find out the status before the next return. The board granted the extension.

memberPositions.stance: concerned
memberPositions.evidence: Noted the application has been going on a long time since 2024 and directed staff to find out the status before the next extension, while still moving to grant this one.

cases.name: Ken Place — Verizon Parking Plan
cases.applicant: Verizon
cases.summary: The board granted an extension of time for the Ken Place Verizon parking plan. Staff reported the required Verizon signatures had finally been obtained and the matter now rests with the department of health, and that the applicant's variance had been renewed about a year ago so there is no variance concern.

cases.name: 12 April Avenue
cases.summary: At the prior meeting the board had approved an extension of time for 12 April Avenue, but it emerged that the applicant's ZBA variance had already expired and no extension was sought before it lapsed, rendering the variance and therefore the site plan null and void. The board voted to rescind its prior approval of the extension of time.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: As chair explained the variance had expired unextended, making the site plan null and void, and moved to rescind the prior extension approval.

themes.note: Extended debate over which club parking standard to apply to the cigar club; board favored a workable outcome.
Procedure reform plus three individual extension items, one rescinded for a lapsed variance.
100 Buckout mitigation plan approved by Conservation Board and permit granted.
Referral made for cigar-club parking; 12 April Avenue variance had expired.
SHIPO confirmed no impact to the African American historic cemetery near 100 Buckout.

staffInput.summary: Presented the cigar-club parking analysis, recommending the one-space-per-200-sq-ft club standard to likely avoid a variance given shared plaza parking and evening use; led the extensions-of-time procedure reform (agenda placement and whereas clauses); drafted the 100 Buckout resolution.
His office (referenced as Kellard's/KSCJ) had raised engineering concerns on 100 Buckout that were reported as addressed and folded into the draft resolution conditions.

meetings.meetingSummary: The Planning Board granted a final extension of time for the Eagle Ridge project, then held two public hearings. The first was on the NYC DEP's Kensico-Eastview Connection (KEC) wetland mitigation project (site plan, wetlands permit, and tree removal at the Big Peninsula and Old Post Road staging area), which the board received enthusiastically and approved with SEQRA findings. The second was a change-of-use site plan for the Social Life members club / cigar lounge at 909-911 North Broadway, also approved. A resident raised traffic-safety concerns about the Whipple/King Street intersection tied to the KEC construction.

cases.name: Eagle Ridge extension of time
cases.applicant: Eagle Ridge (update relayed from Corey)
cases.summary: The board handled a routine request for an extension of time for Eagle Ridge. A member reported an update from Corey indicating the applicant is able to move forward and obtain the final sign-off, so this should be the last extension needed. The chair made a motion to grant the extension and it passed. Brief confirmation was given that the DEP paperwork was in order.

cases.name: KEC Wetland Mitigation - Big Peninsula & Old Post Road
cases.address: Kensico River and Old Post Road (25 & 27 Old Post Road); tax lots 113.01-1-1 and 113.02-1-15/16
cases.applicant: NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP); presenter Angel Vides and full design/construction team
cases.summary: The DEP presented the wetland mitigation component of the Kensico-Eastview Connection (KEC) program, including shoreline stabilization (1,600 linear feet of rip-rap hardening), creation of roughly 2.5 acres of wetland at the Big Peninsula, and a one-acre construction staging area at Old Post Road. Construction runs fall 2026 through roughly 2029-2031 within the town's noise ordinance hours, with minimal projected traffic (about three peak-hour trucks per direction). The Conservation Board reported it had done a site walk and given a positive recommendation, and the town planner noted a thorough submission with no significant concerns. The board opened the hearing, took public comment, closed it, adopted SEQRA findings identical to DEP's, and approved the site plan, wetlands, and tree removal permits.
cases.publicComment: One resident, Zach Haas of Whipple (Whippoorwill) Road off Route 120/King Street, spoke - not opposing the project but urging traffic-safety measures at the dangerous hairpin turn where Whipple meets King Street, which he said is worsened by KEC-related commuter and construction traffic. Tone was earnest and concerned.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Chaired the hearing and praised the DEP's prior comparable work: the bowling-alley mitigation is an 'amazing project' that he brings people to see; glad the Conservation Board did a site walk; walked the applicant through findings and moved approval.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice; engaged the resident on the Whipple/King intersection he knows firsthand ('so I live up... I know exactly what you're talking about'), advising caution on the right turn and supporting outreach to the highway department. Supportive of the DEP application overall.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: A non-chair member pressed technical questions - whether private contractors would do the work, motorist protection and egress on Route 120, the high-level objective of getting water to the UV plant, and the 27-foot tunnel diameter ('that's a lot of water'), expressing that the project is 'really amazing and impressive.'

cases.name: Social Life Members Club / cigar lounge
cases.address: 909 & 911 North Broadway; tax lot 122.12-4-5.2 (CP zoning district)
cases.applicant: Social Life members club applicant (cigar lounge / membership club)
cases.summary: The board took up the change-of-use site plan for the Social Life members club and cigar lounge. The planner explained the applicant already obtained its special use permit and, because the prior use was a bakery, the off-street parking calculation for the shopping center showed no parking variance was needed (17 spaces under the one-space-per-three-seats standard). With no physical changes to the site, this was a simple change of use. Members joked about the concept, asked about liquor licensing and membership tiers, then closed the hearing and approved the change-of-use site development plan.

memberPositions.stance: supportive
memberPositions.evidence: Chaired the hearing, engaged good-naturedly with the applicant, and offered a clear endorsement: 'I wish you well... any business enterprise, I wish you well,' before moving to close.

memberPositions.stance: neutral
memberPositions.evidence: Read the public hearing notice for the 909-911 North Broadway members-club site plan; no substantive concerns raised.

themes.note: Core of the DEP KEC hearing - 2.5 acres of created wetland, well received.
Resident's safety concern about the Whipple/King hairpin turn tied to KEC construction traffic; board sympathetic but felt limited jurisdiction.
1,600 linear feet of rip-rap hardening to protect the reservoir water supply.
Limited removal with re-vegetation (24 trees planted at staging area); accepted.

staffInput.summary: Called the DEP submission thorough with no significant concerns, noted DEP has done similar projects in town, and prepared/updated the draft resolution incorporating town engineer and consultant memo comments; designated as recipient of the applicant's quarterly construction updates. Also explained that the Social Life members club needed no parking variance given the prior bakery use, making it a simple change of use.

Conservation Board input relayed that the applicant presented twice (before and after a lengthy site walk of the property); the board was very pleased with the mitigation, had only a few minor comments that were resolved, and gave a positive recommendation.
